children.translated_text: "The object of cognition" (<s>cetya</s>) means that which is to be experienced. "In the self"—in the self that is mere consciousness (<s>cinmātra</s>). Moreover, proving the absence of property-hood of <s>cit</s> is untenable because the counter-correlate is not established. Nor is it better to argue that properties do not belong to <s>cit</s>, because the relational meaning of the genitive case does not fail to apply to the entity <s>cit</s>—so the opponent's position is stated—
"Even if"—

children.text: ti / pratyayānāṃ prakṛtyarthānvitasvārthabodhakatvavyutpatteḥ cito vibhaktyarthasaṃbandhitvaṃ siddhamiti tatra viśeṣasāmānyaniṣedhapratijñā vyāhatārtheti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the conventional understanding (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is that case-endings convey their own meaning as connected with the meaning of the stem, the connection of the genitive meaning with <s>cit</s> is established. Therefore, the thesis denying both particular and general relations there is self-contradictory—this is the purport.
"If establishment (<s>siddhi</s>) were accepted, <s>saṃvid</s> would possess properties (<s>sadharmatā</s>);
if not, then what is stated would be mere vacuity (<s>tucchatva</s>), like the horn of a hare." //10//

children.text: nanu siddhireva sā / kasya bhoḥ? yadi na kasyacit, na tarhi siddhireva / sā hi putratvamiva kasyacit kiñcitprati / ātmana iti cet, kaḥ ṣaṣṭhyarthaḥ ?tadevaṃ vyomāravindasadṛśavapuṣi yathoditadṛśi vedāntatātparyavarṇanaṃ vedāntāyaiva syāt /
children.translated_text: "But it is indeed established!" Established for whom, sir? If for no one, then it is not truly established. For establishment, like sonship (<s>putratva</s>), is always relative to something in relation to something else. If you say "of the self (<s>ātman</s>)"—then what is the meaning of the genitive? Thus, describing the purport of <s>Vedānta</s> regarding an entity whose form resembles sky-lotuses would only serve to undermine <s>Vedānta</s> itself.

children.text: api ca nityatve 'pyanubhuteḥ pratyabhijñānupapattistadavasthaiva / sā hi anubhavitāraṃ pūrvāparakālāvasthāyinamupasthāpayati ahamidamanvabhūvamiti / anubhūtistvanubhūtireva bhavatām, na tāṃ prati sā kartrīṃ karma vā /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, even if experience (<s>anubhūti</s>) is eternal, the impossibility of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) remains just the same. For recognition presents the experiencer as persisting through earlier and later times, as in "I experienced this before." But for you, experience is merely experience—it is neither an agent nor an object with respect to itself.
(Thus concludes the section refuting the <s>Māyāvādin</s>'s doctrine that the self is of the nature of eternal consciousness.)

body.translated_text: He resolves the difficulty regarding the motion of the self.

body.text: yadyucyeta- paramārthataḥ tathābhūtāpi bhrāntyānubhavitṛtayā parisphurati rajatatayeva śuktiḥ / na hi tathyamanavalambya mithyāvabhāsasyotthānamiti; tanna / tathā sati anubhavasamānādhikaraṇatayānubhavitāhamarthaḥ prakāśeta anubhūtirahamiti, puraḥsthitabhāsvaradravyaśaṅkhamukhacandrāderākāratayeva rajatapītamukurasthatādvitvādi / pṛthagavabhāsamāna eva tu ayamanubhavo daṇḍa iva devadattamarthāntaramahamarthaṃviśiṃṣan ālakṣyate anubhavāmyahamiti / tadevamanubhavaviśiṣṭamasmadarthamavabhāsayannayamahaṃpratyayaḥ kathamiva viśeṣaṇabhūtānubhūtimātrāvalambanaḥ pratijñāyeta, daṇḍamātra iva daṇḍī devadatta iti pratyayaḥ /
body.translated_text: If it be said—though in ultimate reality it is of such nature, through error (<s>bhrānti</s>) it appears as an experiencer, just as a shell appears as silver, and that no false appearance can arise without depending on something real—that is not so. In that case, the meaning of "I" (<s>aham</s>), being co-located with experience, should appear as identical with experience, as "I am experience," just as silver appears in the form of a shining object before one—a conch, the moon's reflection, and so forth—and yellowness, duality, etc., appear in a mirror. But in fact, this experience is perceived as quite separate, qualifying the I-meaning as something distinct, like a stick qualifying <s>Devadatta</s>: "I experience." Thus, this I-cognition (<s>ahaṃpratyaya</s>), while manifesting the I-meaning as qualified by experience, how could it be claimed to rest upon mere experience as its qualifier—just as the cognition "<s>Devadatta</s> with a stick" cannot rest upon the stick alone?

body.text: kutaścaiṣa niścayaḥ-adhyastaṃ jñātṛtvamiti? / sthūlo 'hamitivat dehātmābhimānavataḥ pratibhāsanāditi cet; nanvātmatayābhimatānubhūtirapi tadūta evāvabhātīti sāpi tathā syāt / tattvajñānodayāt parato 'pi tadanuvṛtterna tathā seti cet ; kiṃ bhoḥ! tattvajñānātparamaboddhaivāyamātmā ? hantaivaṃ varamito 'tattvaveditvam; bhrāntyāpi hi tatra bahu bhadraṃ paśyatīti /
body.translated_text: And whence comes this certainty that the knower-hood (<s>jñātṛtva</s>) is superimposed (<s>adhyasta</s>)? If you say it is because it appears just like the identification of the body with the self, as in "I am stout"—but then experience (<s>anubhūti</s>), which is also taken to be the self, also appears as identified with the body, so it too should be likewise superimposed. If you say that after the rise of true knowledge (<s>tattvajñāna</s>) it does not continue, and hence it is not so—then tell me, sir! After true knowledge, is this self merely a non-knower? Alas, then it would be better to remain in ignorance here; for even through error, one sees much that is auspicious there!

body.text: nanu jñātṛtvaṃ jñānakriyākartṛtvaṃ vikriyātmakaṃ jaḍamahaṅkāragranthistham / tatphalabhugakartāvikriyaḥ sākṣī prakāśamātra ātmā / kartṛtvādirhi dṛśyatvādrūpādivannātmadharmaḥ / kartṛtve hyātmano 'haṃpratyayagocaratve 'pi dehasyevānatmatva- parārthatvajaḍatvādiprasaṅgo durnivāraḥ / dṛṣṭaṃ ca laukikavaidikakarmasu kartṛtayā prasiddhāddehāttatkriyāphalabhujaḥ pramātuḥ ahaṃpratyayinaḥ pṛthaktvam / tathehāpi pramāturahamarthādvilakṣaṇaḥ sākṣī pratyagātmeti yuktam / naivaṃ yuktam / ahaṃ jānāmīti jñātṛtayā sidhyataḥ pratyagātmano vyatirekeṇa sikṣiṇo nāma prakāśamātrasyā'tmano 'nupalabdheḥ / dehendriyamanaḥprāṇavijñānebhyo jñānāśrayatayā vivicyamāne pratīpamañcatīva nirbhāsamāno 'haṃbhāva eva hi pratyaktvaṃ nāma / sākṣitvamapi tasya sākṣājjñātṛtvam / na hyajānan sikṣītyapadiśyate / sarvaṃ ca prakāśamānaṃ jñātre 'hamiti cakāsate prakāśata iti pratyātmasiddho 'yamanubhavaḥ- ahaṃ jānāmi, mahyaṃ prakāśata iti /
body.translated_text: The objection is: knower-hood (<s>jñātṛtva</s>) is agency in the act of knowing, which is a modification (<s>vikriyā</s>), insentient, and resides in the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-knot). The self (<s>ātman</s>) is the <s>sākṣin</s> (witness), who enjoys the fruits of that activity, is non-agent, free from modification, and is mere luminosity (<s>prakāśamātra</s>). For agency, being perceivable like color and form, is not a property of the self. If the self had agency, then even though it is the object of the I-cognition, the same absurd consequences of non-selfhood, being-for-another, insentience, etc., that apply to the body would be unavoidable. And it is observed that in worldly and Vedic rituals, the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), the subject of the I-cognition, who enjoys the fruits of those actions, is distinct from the body that is known as the agent. Similarly here too, it is fitting that the <s>sākṣin</s> (witness), the innermost self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), is distinct from the I-meaning as the knower. This is not correct. Because apart from the innermost self that is established as the knower through "I know," no witness named mere luminosity is ever apprehended. When discriminated from body, senses, mind, vital breath, and intellect as the substrate of knowledge, it is precisely the I-sense (<s>ahaṃbhāva</s>), shining inwardly as if receding from them, that constitutes innerness (<s>pratyaktva</s>). And even its witness-hood (<s>sākṣitva</s>) is direct knower-hood. For no one is called a witness who does not know. And everything that shines forth appears to the knower as "I"—this is the experience established in every self: "I know," "It shines forth to me."

children.translated_text: (Thus the establishment of the I-meaning of the knower as the innermost self.)

body.text: na cāvyākṛtapariṇāmabhedasyāhaṅkāranāmno buddhināmadheyasya vā jñātṛtvam ; dehasyevācetanatvapariṇāmitvajaḍatvaparārthatvādihetubhistadanupapatteḥ / na ca citicchāyāpattyā tayostatsaṃbhavaḥ / acākṣuṣasya chāyādarśanāt / na ca jñātṛtvaṃ citāvapi te vāstavamasti, yenāgnisaṃparkādayaḥ piṇḍa ivauṣṇyaṃ tatsaṃparkādarthāntare jñātṛtvaṃ jāyeta jñāyeta vā /
body.translated_text: Nor does knower-hood belong to the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense), which is a modification of the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), or to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); for the same reasons that apply to the body—unconsciousness, being a product of transformation, insentience, being-for-another, etc.—make it untenable. Nor is it possible for them through the reflection (<s>chāyāpatti</s>) of consciousness (<s>citi</s>); for a reflection cannot be perceived of what is itself imperceptible to the eye. Nor is knower-hood truly real even in <s>citi</s> according to you, such that—like heat in a ball of iron from contact with fire—knower-hood could arise or be known in another entity through contact with it.

children.translated_text: (Thus the demonstration that knower-hood and its cognition cannot belong to <s>ahaṅkāra</s>.)

body.text: yadyucyeta-jñāptimātramevā'tmānamabhivyañjan acetano 'pyahaṅkāraḥ svāśrayatayā tamabhivyanakti / svabhāvo hyayaṃ vyañjakānām-yadātmasthatayābhivyaṅgyamabhivyañjanti, darpaṇajalakhaṇḍamuṇḍādaya iva mukhamihirabimbagotvādīn /
body.translated_text: If it be said: the <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, though unconscious, being mere manifestation of cognition (<s>jñāptimātra</s>), manifests the self as its own substrate. For this is the nature of manifesting agents—they manifest what is to be manifested as residing in themselves, just as mirrors, water surfaces, and shaved heads manifest a face, the sun's orb, cow-hood, and so forth.

children.text: tatkṛtaścāyamahaṃ jānāmīti bhramaḥ / ata eva khalu ahamullekhavigame suṣuptimuktayoḥ svābhāvikaviśadānubhavamātrarūpeṇā'tmanaḥ prakāśaḥ / tata eva cānātmatvamahamarthasya / tathā ca saureśaṃ vacaḥ-
children.translated_text: And this error "I know" is produced by that (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>). Therefore indeed, in deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>) and liberation (<s>mukti</s>), when the I-notion ceases, the self shines forth in its natural, clear experience alone. And from that very fact, the I-meaning is established as non-self (<s>anātma</s>). Thus the verse of <s>Saureśa</s>—
If the I-sense were a property of the self, it would accompany it even in liberation and deep sleep;
since it does not follow there, this 'I' must belong to something other than the self.
Thus.
(Thus the presentation of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> that <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is the manifester of <s>saṃvid</s>.)
He establishes the possession of properties (<s>sadharmatva</s>) of <s>saṃvid</s> through yet another method—
"If establishment"—

children.text: diti / siddhiḥ prakāśaḥ / tadupagame tenaiva saṃvidaḥ sadharmatā syāt / tadanupagame tu śaśaviṣāṇādivadaprakāśamānāyā asiddhyantyāstasyāstucchatvameva prasajyata iti kārikārthaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: thus. <s>Siddhi</s> (establishment) means <s>prakāśa</s> (luminosity). If that is accepted, then <s>saṃvid</s> would have the property of possessing attributes (<s>sadharmatā</s>) through that very luminosity. If it is not accepted, then for <s>saṃvid</s>, which does not shine forth like a hare's horn and thus is not established, mere vacuity (<s>tucchatva</s>) would follow—this is the meaning of the verse. //10//

body.text: atra śaṅkate

children.translated_text: "But it is indeed establishment"—

children.text: ti / na prakāśāśrayaḥ, kintu prakāśasvarūpaiva saṃvit / tanna tucchatvaṃ sadharmakatvaṃ veti bhāvaḥ / ākṣipati
children.translated_text: The sense is: <s>saṃvid</s> is not a substrate of <s>prakāśa</s>, but is of the very nature of <s>prakāśa</s> itself. Therefore neither vacuity nor possession of properties applies. He presses the point—
"For whom, sir?"—
Frightened by the consequence of <s>saviśeṣatva</s> (having particularities), the opponent says—
"For no one"—
The <s>siddhāntin</s> (proponent) replies—
"Then not"—

children.text: ti / prakāśo hi dharmo vinā dharmiṇā na ghaṭata iti bhāvaḥ / siddheḥ sasaṃbandhikatvaṃ vyutpādayati
children.translated_text: The sense is: <s>prakāśa</s> (luminosity), being a property (<s>dharma</s>), cannot obtain without a property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). He derives the relational nature of <s>siddhi</s>—
"For it"—

children.text: ti / piturhi putraḥ / putratvamivānuyogipratiyogisāpekṣā siddhiriti bhāvaḥ / ananyagatikatayā'ha
children.translated_text: For a son belongs to a father. The sense is that <s>siddhi</s> (establishment), like sonship (<s>putratva</s>), requires both a correlate (<s>anuyogin</s>) and a counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>). He states this as the only possibility—
"Of the self"—

children.text: iti / ātmānuyogikātmapratiyogikaiva siddhiḥ saṃvida ityarthaḥ / ātmaśabdo 'tra svarūpavācī / evaṃ cet sadharmatvamāyātyeva saṃvida ityāha
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the <s>siddhi</s> of <s>saṃvid</s> has the self as both its correlate and counter-correlate. The word <s>ātman</s> here denotes essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>). If so, then the possession of properties (<s>sadharmatva</s>) of <s>saṃvid</s> necessarily follows—he says—
"What"—

children.text:
iti / pitaraṃ prati putrasya putratvamivātmapratiyogikaḥ prakāśo dharmaḥ saṃvidātmanaḥ sidhyatītyarthaḥ / evaṃ kāri
kārtha ākṣepaparihārapadakaiḥ katibhiścidvivṛtaḥ / evaṃ saṃvido nirviśeṣatvaṃ nirasya nirviśeṣasaṃvidi vedāntatātparyavarṇanaṃ vedāntānāmaprāmāṇyapraryavasāyītyāha
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as sonship (<s>putratva</s>) of a son in relation to a father, so <s>prakāśa</s> (luminosity), having the self as its counter-correlate, is established as a property (<s>dharma</s>) of the self that is <s>saṃvid</s>. Thus the meaning of the verse has been elucidated through several words of objection and resolution. Having thus rejected the attributelessness (<s>nirviśeṣatva</s>) of <s>saṃvid</s>, he states that describing the purport of <s>Vedānta</s> as residing in an attributeless <s>saṃvid</s> would result in the invalidity of the <s>Vedāntas</s> themselves—
"Thus indeed"—

children.text:
iti / vedāntāya-vedavināśāya / vedaprāmāṇyocchittyai iti yāvat /
kṣaṇikavijñānātmavāde smaraṇādyanupapattyā niraste hi nityavijñānātmavādina utthānam / etatpakṣe 'pi tāmāha
children.translated_text:
and so forth. 'For the destruction of the <s>Veda</s>' (<s>vedāntāya</s>) — for the destruction of the authority of the <s>Veda</s>. This is the meaning.
When the doctrine of the momentary-cognition-as-self has been refuted through the impossibility of memory and the like, the proponent of the eternal-cognition-as-self doctrine rises up. He states the [conflicting views] in this position too with
'moreover' (<s>api ca</s>)

children.text:
ti / jñāturnityatva evāhamidamanvabhavamityāderupapattiḥ ; natu jñānanityatvamātreṇeti bhāvaḥ /
etadeva vivṛṇoti
children.translated_text:
and so forth. The purport is: the explanation of 'I experienced this' and the like is possible only when the knower is eternal, not merely through the eternality of knowledge.
He elaborates this very point with
'experience' (<s>anubhūti</s>)
and so forth. He explains the meaning of the word 'eva' ('alone') with
'not that' (<s>na tām</s>)

children.text:
iti / yadyapi siddhānte 'pi nānubhavitṛtvamanubhūteḥ/ athāpyanubhāvyatvamiṣyate / jñātuścāhamarthasyātmano nityatvam / tathāca pūrvānubhūtānubhūtyādipratisandhānaṃ ghaṭate / paramate tvananubhāvyatvādananubhavitṛtvācca saṃvidātmano niruktapratisandhānānupapattireveti bhāvaḥ / tadevaṃ pratisandhānabalājjñāturevātmatvaṃ na jñānamātrasyeti sthita hṛdi / etadeva samarthayiṣyatyagrimagranthasandarbheṇa /
tatrādau jñātṛtvapratīterbhrāntirūpatāṃ parābhimatāmanuvadati
children.translated_text:
and so forth. Although even in the established doctrine [of Viśiṣṭādvaita], experience does not have the status of being the experiencer — nevertheless, it is accepted as the object of experience. And the knower — the 'I,' the self — is eternal. And thus the reconnection of prior experience and the like is explained. But in the opponent's doctrine, since cognition is neither the object of experience nor the experiencer — the impossibility of the stated reconnection of cognition-as-self follows — this is the purport. Thus it has been established in the heart that selfhood belongs to the knower alone, not to mere knowledge, by the force of the argument from reconnection [i.e., recognition]. He will substantiate this very point further through the arrangement of the subsequent text.
First, he reproduces the opponent's view that the cognition of knower-hood is of the nature of error, with
'if it is said' (<s>yadyucyata</s>)

children.text: ti / saṃvinmātra paramārthaḥ / sa evātmā / asminnadhiṣṭhāne jñāturahamarthasya bhrāntiḥ śuktāviva rajatasya / bhramopapattyarthamadhiṣṭhānasaṃvinmātrapāramārthyamabhyupeyamiti pareṣāmāśayaḥ / dūṣayati
children.translated_text: and so forth. Mere cognition (<s>saṃvinmātra</s>) is the ultimate reality. That alone is the self. Upon this substrate, there is an error [viz., the appearance of] the knower — the 'I'-referent — like [the appearance of] silver upon nacre. The opponent's view is: the ultimate reality of mere cognition as substrate must be accepted in order to explain the error. He refutes [this] with
'that is not [so]' (<s>tanna</s>)
and so forth.
'this being so' (<s>tathā satī</s>)
and so forth.
This is the purport:

children.text: dharmiṇi dharmyantarārope āropyādhiṣṭhānayoḥ samānādhikaraṇyena (abhedena) bhānaṃ bhavedidaṃ rajatamiti yathā / anyatrānyadharmārope cāropyadharmavatā tathā bhānaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śaṅkhaḥ pītavān, mukha darpaṇasthaṃ, candrau dvāviti / na caivamatrānubhūtirahamiti vā ahaṃvatīti vā bhānamasti / tanna saṃvidi ahamarthāropa iti yuktamiti / ahamarthe saṃvidāropopagamastu na ghaṭate pareṣāṃ satyālambanatvaniyamādāropasya, ahamarthasya cāsatyatvāditi dhyeyam /
children.translated_text: In the superimposition of one property upon a property-locus [which is actually another thing], the superimposed and the substrate appear through co-referentiality (i.e., non-difference) — as in 'this is silver.' And in the superimposition of one property upon another [locus], the appearance [occurs] such that [the superimposed property] is accompanied by its property-possessor — as observed in 'the conch is yellow,' 'the face is in the mirror,' 'there are two moons.' But no such appearance occurs here — neither as 'experience is I' nor as 'I am the possessor of experience.' Therefore, it is not appropriate [to maintain] that the 'I'-referent is superimposed upon cognition. As for the acceptance that cognition is superimposed upon the 'I'-referent — that does not hold for the opponents, because of the [Advaita] rule that superimposition must have a real substrate, and because the 'I'-referent [in their view] is unreal — this should be reflected upon.
'separately' (<s>pṛthak</s>)

children.text: giti / pṛthagavabhāsamānatvaṃ prakāratayā prakāriṇo vilakṣaṇatvena bhāsamānatvam / ahandaṇḍīti pratītitulyatvādahaṃ jānāmīti pratīterahamarthe jñānadharmavattāvagāhitvameveti yāvat /
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Appearing separately' means: appearing as a qualifier (<s>prakāra</s>), as [something] different from the qualified. Just as in the cognition 'I who hold a staff,' so in the cognition 'I know' — the [cognition] grasps the 'I'-referent as possessing the property of knowledge. This is the purport.
'thus' (<s>tadevam</s>)

children.text:
iti / daṇḍamātre iti viṣayasaptamī / daṇḍamātrālambana ityarthaḥ / yathā daṇḍī puruṣa ityatra daṇḍamātrasya satyatvaṃ puruṣasyāropitatvaṃ ca na, evamahaṃ jānāmītyatrāpi na jñānamātrasya satstvaṃ jñāturmithyātvaṃ ca / kintu jñāturahamarthasya satyatvameva yuktamabhyupagantuṃ bādhakānupalabdherityāśayaḥ /
jñātṛtvapratīterbhrāntitve 'nuyuṅle kiṃ niyāmakamiti
children.translated_text:
and so forth. 'In mere staff' — this is a locative [denoting] the object; the meaning is: having mere staff as its object. Just as in 'a man with a staff,' the mere staff is not [taken to be] real and the man [taken to be] superimposed — so too in 'I know,' mere knowledge is not [taken to be] real and the knower [taken to be] false. Rather, the purport is: it is appropriate to accept the reality of the 'I'-referent, the knower — because no sublating cognition is apprehended.
When the cognition of knower-hood is [declared to be] of the nature of error, he presses the question: what is the determining factor? — with
'whence' (<s>kutaḥ</s>)
and so forth. The opponent responds with
'gross' (<s>sthūla</s>)

children.text: iti / bhrāntairgṛhyamāṇatvājjñātṛtvamadhyāsalakṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ / nedamadhyastatvasādhakaṃ bādhitatvena sopādhikatvādityāśayamantarnidhāya pratibandīmāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. The purport is: because knower-hood is grasped by those who are in error, it has the character of superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>). Holding in mind the thought that this does not prove superimposition, because [the claim that knower-hood is grasped by those in error] is itself sublated by being conditional (<s>sopādhika</s>), he presents the counter-argument with
'but for selfhood' (<s>nanvātmataya</s>)

children.text: ti / dehātmabhramavatāgṛhyamāṇāyā api saṃvido 'bādhyatvānna mithyātvamiti samādhiṃ vācayati pūrvapakṣimukhataḥ
children.translated_text: and so forth. He voices the resolution from the mouth of the opponent [as follows]: just as in the error of the body being the self, even though cognition is not grasped [as what it truly is], it is not sublated, and therefore not false. [The opponent's reply is stated] with
'upon the arising of true knowledge' (<s>tattvajñānodaya</s>)
and so forth. He says that this [argument] applies equally to knower-hood — [which should] not [be considered] superimposed — with
'what, sir' (<s>kiṃ bhoḥ</s>)

children.text: riti / tattvajñānaphale mokṣe 'pi jñātṛtvamanuvartata ityabādhitatvamityāśayaḥ / mokṣe jñātṛtvasya nivṛttāvanarthaṃ prasañjayati
children.translated_text: and so forth. The purport is: knower-hood continues even in liberation — which is the result of true knowledge — and so it is not sublated. He points out the undesirable consequence if knower-hood were to cease in liberation, with
'alas, thus' (<s>hantaivam</s>)

children.text:
iti / duḥkhanivṛttyā mukteḥ pumarthatvamiti cedānandānubhavanivṛttyānubhavitrahamarthanivṛttyā cāpumarthatvaṃ prasajyate iti bhāvaḥ /
jñātṛtvāderanātmadharmatvāttannivṛttāvapi na pumarthatopaghāto mukteriti śaṅkate
children.translated_text:
and so forth. The purport is: if liberation is a human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) because of the cessation of suffering, then — [by the same logic] — the cessation of the experience of bliss and the cessation of the 'I'-referent who is the experiencer would make it not a human goal.
He raises the doubt that since knower-hood and the like are not properties of the self, liberation is not diminished as a human goal even when they cease, with
'but knower-hood' (<s>nanu jñātṛtvam</s>)

children.text: iti / ahaṅkāro 'ntaḥkaraṇam, tadeva durmocatvādgranthiḥ, tanniṣṭhameva jñātṛtvaṃ jñānātmanā pariṇāmalakṣaṇaṃ vikriyātmakaṃ jaḍapariṇāmatvājjaḍaṃ cetyarthaḥ / ātmanaḥ svarūpamāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. The <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>); that very [internal organ], because it is difficult to detach, is a 'knot' (<s>granthi</s>); knower-hood resides in that alone, [and since it involves] transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) having the nature of knowledge, it is of the nature of modification, and being a transformation of something inert, it is inert — this is the meaning. He states the own-nature of the self with
'the result of that' (<s>tatphala</s>)

children.text:
ti / kartṛtvasya phalabhoktā, avikriyatvādakartā,
prakāśamātnasvarūpatayā sākṣīcātmāstītyarthaḥ / prakāśaḥ mātrā yasya saḥ prakāśamātraḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. [The self] is the enjoyer of the fruit of agency; it is a non-agent, because it is without modification; and because its essential nature is mere manifestation (<s>prakāśamātra</s>), it is a witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) — the self exists. This is the meaning. '<s>Prakāśamātra</s>' — one whose measure is manifestation; [i.e.,] whose essence is nothing but manifestation.
'in agency' (<s>kartṛtva</s>)

children.text: iti / ātmā na kartā nāpyahamarthaḥ, ātmatvādananyārthatvādajaḍatvādavikriyatvādvā tannaivaṃ yannaivaṃ yathā deha iti prayogā atra garbhitāḥ / kartṛbhinnasya bhoktṛtvaṃ katham? tatrāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. The self is neither an agent nor an 'I'-referent — because of being the self, or because of not being for the sake of another, or because of being non-inert, or because of being without modification. Whatever is not so is not so, like the body — such formal arguments are embedded here. [Objection:] How can enjoyership (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) belong to [the self, which is] different from the agent? To this he says:
'it is observed' (<s>dṛṣṭam</s>)
and so forth. He refutes this with
'not so' (<s>naivam</s>)

and so forth. Having stated the sublation through non-apprehension of the self as mere manifestation (<s>prakāśamātra</s>) other than the knower, he says that the 'I'-hood of the self is to be sought through the very force of immediacy (<s>pratyaktva</s>), with
'from body and senses' (<s>dehendriya</s>)

children.text: ti / jñānasya dehādāvasaṃbhavāddhi tadvailakṣaṇyamātmanaḥ sādhitam / tajjñātṛtvamātmana eṣṭavyam / dehādiścedaṅkāragocaraḥ / tatrāhaṅkārastvābhimānika eva / tadahaṃbhāvasya dehādigatedambhāvataḥ pratīpatvaṃ viruddhatvam / pratīpamañcatīti ca pratyakū ahaṅkāragocaraḥ / tatpratyaktvādahantvamātmana āpatati / dehāderdṛśyādidaṅkāragocarāddraṣṭaryātmani pratīpaṃ viruddhamārgaṃ gacchatīvetyuprekṣā / mūle añcatīti saptamyantam / sthite ātmanīti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. Since knowledge is impossible in the body and the like, the self's distinctness from them has been established. Knower-hood of the self is to be sought. The body and the like are objects of the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> [i.e., ego-sense]. But with respect to them, the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is merely assumed [not primary]. Since the 'I'-ness attributed to the body and the like proceeds from the 'this'-cognition, the direction [of the 'I'-cognition] toward the self is opposite [to the body-directed cognition]. 'Opposite' (<s>pratīpa</s>) — the object of the 'I'-cognition goes, as it were, in the reverse direction, toward the self as seer, away from the seen [body and the like, which are] objects of the 'this'-cognition. The root '<s>añcati</s>' takes the locative [ending]. 'In the established self' is to be supplied.
'witness-hood too' (<s>sākṣitvam api</s>)
and so forth.
'The designation [sākṣin] applies to one who sees directly'

children.text: mityanuśāsanāditi bhāvaḥ / sarvaṃ ca jñeyaṃ jñātnātmana eva bhāsate na jñānamātnāya/ tataśca jñāturevātmatvaṃ na jñānamātnasyetyāha
children.translated_text: — because of this grammatical rule, the purport [is clear]. And everything knowable shines forth for the self, which is the knower — not for mere knowledge. And therefore selfhood belongs to the knower alone, not to mere knowledge. He says:
'everything' (<s>sarvam</s>)

children.text:
iti / cakāsate iti caturthyantam / ataśca na jñānamātnasya sākṣitvaṃ saṃbhavati, kintu jñātureveti tasyaivātmatvaṃ na jñānamātnasyeti hārdam / yattu jñātṛtvaṃ vikriyātmakamiti; tanna / na hi kāpilamata iva jñānapariṇāmitvaṃ jñātṛtvamiṣyate śrutyantahārdābhijñaiḥ / kintu arthaprakāśanopayogivyāpāravaddharmabhūtajñānāśrayatvameva / saviṣayake
dhātvarthe kartṛtāyā āśrayatvarūpatvāt, karmatvasya viṣayatārūpatvavat / yadapi kartṛranyasya bhoktṛtvamiti, tadapi vārtam / upādānādikāyikakriyānuguṇajñānecchāpūrvakāntaraprayatnāśrayatvarūpasya mukhyakartṛtvasyātmanyevopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. '<s>Cakāsate</s>' takes the dative case. And therefore, witness-hood is not possible for mere knowledge, but only for the knower — and so selfhood belongs to the knower alone, not to mere knowledge. This is the essential point. As for [the claim] that knower-hood is of the nature of modification — that is not [correct]. For those who know the inner purport of the <s>śruti</s> do not accept that knower-hood consists in being a transformation of knowledge, as in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> (<s>Kāpila</s>) doctrine. Rather, [it consists in] being the substrate of essential-attribute-knowledge (<s>dharmabhūtajñāna</s>), which has an operation conducive to the illumination of objects. Because the nature of agency (<s>kartṛtā</s>) in a transitive verb-meaning is being the substrate [of action], just as object-hood (<s>karmatva</s>) has the nature of being the object [of the verb]. As for [the claim] that enjoyership belongs to something other than the agent — that too is meaningless. Because primary agency — which has the nature of being the substrate of effort preceded by desire and knowledge conforming to physical action [derived] from the material cause and the like — is possible in the self alone.
'The fruit of the <s>śāstra</s> [rests] in the agent (<s>prayoktṛ</s>), because the agent is what makes the <s>śāstra</s> meaningful' —

children.text:
diti hi vedavedāntahārdābhijñāḥ / yadapi kartṛtvādirdṛśyatvānnātmadharma iti, tadapi mandam / dṛśyatvaṃ cedvāhyendriyagrāhyatvaṃ tadasiddhamāntaraprayatnādhāratvalakṣaṇe pakṣe / anubhāvyatvaṃ cettat, tarhyaprayojakatvaṃ hetoḥ / yadapi kartṛtvādau anātmatvādyapādānam, tadapi bhagnamūlam / amukhyasyaiva tasyānātmatvādivyāpyatvāt mukhyakartṛtvāhapratyayāspada ātmanyanātmatvādyaprasakteriti saṅkṣepaḥ /
evamātmana eva jñātṛtvamahaṃ tvaṃ ca mukhyamityuktvā prakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣe buddhyākhye mahattatve tatkārye 'haṅkāre vā jñātṛtvamanupapannamityāha
children.translated_text:
so say those who know the inner purport of the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Vedānta</s>. As for [the claim] that 'agency and the like are not properties of the self because they are objects of cognition (<s>dṛśya</s>)' — that too is feeble. If 'being an object of cognition' (<s>dṛśyatva</s>) means being apprehensible by the external sense organs, then it is unestablished in the thesis that [agency] has the defining characteristic of being the substrate of inner effort. And if [it means] being experienceable (<s>anubhāvyatva</s>), then the reason is non-probative. As for the attribution of non-selfhood and the like to agency — that too has its root cut. Because only non-primary [agency] is pervaded by non-selfhood and the like. Primary agency — [which is] the locus of the 'I'-cognition — does not entail non-selfhood and the like in the self. This is the summary.
Having thus stated that knower-hood and 'I'-hood of the self alone are primary, he says that knower-hood is impossible in a specific modification of <s>Prakṛti</s> called <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) or <s>mahat</s> (the great principle), or in its effect <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, with
'nor in the unmanifest' (<s>na cāvyākṛta</s>)

children.text: ti / acetanatvam-anātmatvam, na tvajñātṛtvam / sādhyahetvoraikyaprasaṅgāt / mahānahaṅkāro vā na jñātā anātmatvāt pariṇāmitvājjaḍatvātparārthatvādvā dehavaditi prayogaḥ / nanu jñātṛtvasyāsaṃbhave 'pi cicchāyāpatyā citsaṃparkādvā tatna jñātṛtvapratītirastvityatnāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Non-conscious' (<s>acetanatva</s>) — non-selfhood, but not lack of knower-hood — because there would follow the consequence of identity between the provable and the reason. The formal argument is: the <s>mahat</s> or <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is not a knower, because of non-selfhood, or because of being a transformation, or because of being inert, or because of being for the sake of another — like the body. [Objection:] Even if knower-hood is impossible [in them], let the cognition of knower-hood occur through the reflection of consciousness (<s>cicchāyāpatti</s>) or through contact with consciousness. To address this, he says:
'nor in consciousness' (<s>na ca citī</s>)

children.text:
ti / arūpatvāccito na pratibimbo buddhyādau saṃbhavati / yena sphaṭike lohitapratibhāsavattatna caitanyapratibhāso bhavet / naca citau jñātṛtvamasti / yena tatsaṃparkāttatna jñātṛtvaṃ tatpratibhānaṃ vā bhavet agnisaṅgādayasi auṣṇyabhānavaditi bhāvaḥ / sāṃsargiko guṇo doṣo vā tatna tatna jāyate jñāyate ceti jāyeta jñāyeta vetyuktiḥ /
atha jñātṛtvapratīternirvāhāya parābhimatamahaṅkārasya saṃvidabhivyañjakatvapakṣa- manuvadati
children.translated_text:
and so forth. Because consciousness is formless (<s>arūpa</s>), its reflection is not possible in the <s>buddhi</s> and the like — so that, as in the case of the redness appearing in a crystal, there would be an appearance of consciousness in them. Nor does consciousness possess knower-hood, so that through contact with it, knower-hood or the appearance of knower-hood would occur in them — as warmth or its appearance occurs through contact with fire. This is the purport. A conjoined quality or defect arises and is known in each of the two [conjuncts] — hence the expression 'would arise or be known.'
Now he reproduces the opponent's view that the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> manifests (<s>abhivyañjaka</s>) cognition — a position held [by the opponent] in order to sustain the cognition of knower-hood — with
'if it is said' (<s>yadyucyata</s>)

children.text: tyādinā / abhivyañjayan-prakāśayan / svāśrayatayā-svāśritayā / bahuvrīhestal / khaṇḍamuṇḍādayo govyakti-
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Manifesting' — illuminating. 'As its own substrate' (<s>svāśrayatayā</s>) — as what is dependent on it. This is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, <s>Muṇḍa</s>, and the like are individual
varieties of cows.
'The orb of the sun' (<s>mihirabimba</s>) — the disc of the sun. The rest is clear.
'And [the appearance] produced by that' (<s>tatkṛtaśca</s>)

children.text: ti / saṃvidabhivyañjakatvaprayuktaścāhaṅkārasya saṃvidāśrayatvapratibhāso mukhādyabhivyañjakatvaprayuktaścāhaṅkārasya saṃvidāśrayatvapratibhāso mikhādyabhivyañjakatvaprayukta iva darpaṇādermukhavattvādipratibhāsa ityarthaḥ / ahaṃbhāvaḥ prakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣasyaiva, na tvātmana ityāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. The appearance that the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is the substrate of cognition — produced by [the <s>ahaṅkāra</s>] manifesting cognition — is like the appearance that a mirror and the like bear the face, produced by [the mirror's] manifesting the face. This is the meaning. He says that the 'I'-sense belongs to the specific modification of <s>Prakṛti</s> alone, not to the self, with
'for this very reason' (<s>ata eva</s>)

children.text: ti / yato jñātṛtvapratītirbhrāntiḥ, ata eva caitanyamātratayā'tmanaḥ svāpemuktau ca bhānam / na tu tadāhambhāvabhānamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. Since the cognition of knower-hood is an error, for this very reason, the self, being mere consciousness (<s>caitanyamātra</s>), shines forth in deep sleep and in liberation. But the 'I'-sense does not shine forth at those times. This is the purport.
'for this very reason' (<s>ata eva</s>)

children.text:
ti / sauṣuptikamauktikātmānubhavato 'hambhāvānullekhādevāhamarthasyānātmatvamityathraḥ / atra saṃvādatayā sureśvarācāryavacanamu
pādatte
children.translated_text: and so forth. Because the 'I'-sense is not even hinted at (<s>anullekhā</s>) in the experience of the self in deep sleep and liberation, the 'I'-referent is not the self — this is the meaning. Here, as corroboration, he cites a statement of <s>Sureśvarācārya</s>, with
'of the self' (<s>ātmana</s>)

children.text: iti / ahambhāva ātmadharmaścetsuṣuptimuktayoryāyāt-anviyāt / yato nānveti tato 'yamanātmadharma evetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. If the 'I'-sense were a property of the self, it would accompany [the self] in deep sleep and liberation. Since it does not accompany [the self in those states], it is a property of something other than the self alone — this is the meaning.
This is incoherent. Because:

body.translated_text: Here he raises an objection—

body.text: śāntāṅgāra ivādityamahaṅkāro jaḍātmakaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Like a quenched ember [claiming to manifest] the sun, the inert <s>ahaṅkāra</s> —

body.text: svayañjyotiṣamātmānaṃ vyanaktīti na yuktimat //11//
body.translated_text: [the claim that] it manifests the self-luminous self — is not reasonable.' (Verse 11)

body.text: ātmatvābhimatājaḍānubhavādhīnā hi sarvapadārthābhivyaktayo 'bhipreyante / tādṛśamaśeṣārthasādhakamudayāstamayaviparivṛttiśūnyaprakāśasvabhāvaṃ tamanubhavaṃ tadadhīnasiddhiracidahaṅkāro 'bhivyanaktītyupahāsyamidamātmavidām /
body.translated_text: For all manifestations of all objects are intended as depending on the non-inert experience accepted as [having] selfhood. That the non-conscious <s>ahaṅkāra</s> manifests that experience — which illuminates all objects, which has the nature of manifestation (<s>prakāśa</s>) devoid of the cycle of arising and setting — is laughable to those who know the self.

body.text: pakṣamenaṃ pratikṣipati

children.translated_text: 'this' (<s>tadidam</s>)
and so forth. The fact that the inert <s>ahaṅkāra</s> cannot manifest self-luminous consciousness is incongruous and impossible, he says with
'quenched' (<s>śānta</s>)

children.text: ti / śāntāṅgāraḥ-jalanirvāpitāgnipiṇḍaḥ / aprakāśasvarūpasya tasya prakāśamayādityaprakāśakatvamivāprakāśasva- rūpasya jaḍasya prakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣasya svaprakāśasaṃvidātmasvarūpaprakāśakatvamanupapannamityarthaḥ //11//
children.translated_text: and so forth. '<s>Śāntāṅgāra</s>' — a lump of fire that has been extinguished by water. Just as it is impossible for that [extinguished ember], which is devoid of light by nature, to illuminate the sun, which is made of light — so too it is impossible for the inert [<s>ahaṅkāra</s>], a specific modification of <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is devoid of light by nature, to illuminate the own-nature of self-luminous consciousness. This is the meaning. (Verse 11)

body.translated_text: He refutes this position with

body.text: imamevārthāṃ prapañcayati

children.translated_text: 'in selfhood' (<s>ātmatva</s>)

children.text: tyādinā / sarvārthaprakāśakaṃ kadācitprakāśate 'tha na, punaḥkadācitprakāśate ityudayāstamayaparyāyavṛttirahitanityaprakāśasvarūpamanubhavātmānaṃ niyamena tadadhīnaprakāśo jaḍo 'haṅkāro 'bhivyanaktīti vipratīpavacanamidaṃ samīpasthānāmapi ātmatattvavidāmupahāsāspadamityarthaḥ / na khalu sarvaṃ sādhayataḥ svataḥsiddhasya ca sadānubhavātmanaḥ prakāśakāntarāpekṣā / naca jaḍasya niyamena tadābhāsyasyāhaṅkārasya tatprakāśanasāmarthyam / yenānubhavasyāhaṅkārābhivyaṅgyatvavacanamupapannaṃ bhavediti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'The [awareness] that illuminates all objects sometimes shines and sometimes does not, and then shines again' — [to say that] the inert I-cognition (<s>ahankara</s>), whose illumination is invariably dependent on that [awareness], manifests the self, whose nature is experience, which is eternally luminous and free from the cycle of rising and setting — this contradictory statement is an object of ridicule even for those nearby who know the truth of the self. This is the meaning. For what establishes everything and is self-established, the ever-experiential [self], has no need for another illuminator. And the inert I-cognition, which is invariably illuminated by that [awareness], does not have the capacity to illuminate it. Hence the statement that experience is manifested by the I-cognition is untenable. This is the purport.
Moreover — the mutual relation of manifested and manifestor between [awareness and the I-cognition] would not be possible, because of the contradiction.
If [awareness] were manifested [by another], it would not be experience, just as in [the case of] a pot.

children.text: dinakarakaravyaṅgyakaratalaṃ tadabhivyañjakaṃ dṛṣṭamiti mā vocaḥ / karatalasya tadbāhulyamātrahetutvāt / tathābhūtāśca dinakaramarīcayaḥ sphuṭamupalabhyanta iti na karatalavyaṅgyatvam /
children.translated_text: Do not say that the palm of the hand, which is manifested by the rays of the sun, is seen to be the manifestor of those [rays]. Because the palm of the hand is merely the cause of [the rays'] aggregation [through blocking their path]. And those sun-rays in their aggregated [state] are clearly perceived [to shine] on their own.

children.text: api ca keyamabhivyakti ? yānubhūtirūpasyātmano 'haṅkāreṇa kriyata ityucyate / na tāvattatsiddhiḥ, tasya svataḥsiddhatvenānanyādhīnasiddhitvābhyupagamāt / nāpi tadviṣayajñānam, jñānāntarānanubhāvyatvāt / anubhāvyatve hi ghaṭādivadananubhū
children.translated_text: Moreover, what is this manifestation that the I-cognition is said to perform upon the self, whose nature is experience? It is not the establishment of that [self], because it is accepted that [the self] is self-established and its establishment is not dependent on anything else. Nor is it knowledge regarding that [self], because [awareness] is not experienceable by another knowledge. For if it were experienceable [by another], there would follow the consequence of its being a non-experience,

body.translated_text: He elaborates this very point with

body.text: titvaprasaṅgaḥ / ata eva na jñānakaraṇānugrahaḥ / sa hi vedyagatajñānodayapratibandhakāpanayanena vā dīpeneva santamasanirasanena cakṣuṣaḥ; vedyasannikarṣopādhitvena vā vyaktidarpaṇāderiva jātinijamukhādibodhakasya nayanādeḥ; vittṛgatakalaṅkakṣālanena vā śamadamādineva parāvarātmatattvajñānopāyasyā'gamādeḥ / na tāvadanubhavagamahaṅkārāpaneyamasti kiñcit jñānodayaparipanthi / ajñānaṃ tu jñānasamānāśrayaviṣayatayā na tadubhayabhāvavirahiṇi bhavadabhimatasākṣiṇi nikṣepamarhati / na khalu jñānaprasaktiśūnyo ghaṭādirajñānītyucyate / tathaiva na jātucit jñātṛtvaṃ jñānamātrasyeti na tasyāpyajñānaṃ bhavet / bhavadapi vā tadahaṅkārāpaneyaṃ neṣyate; jñānaikanivartyatvādajñānasya, tathābhyupagamāñca / jñānaṃ ca svaviṣaya evājñānaṃ nivartayati / na ca tadviṣayatvamātmatayābhimata syānubhavasyeṣyata iti tatratyamajñānaṃ na kenacitkadāciducchidyeta / jñānaprāgabhāvarūpaṃ cājñānaṃ na jñānotpattipratibandhakamiti śakyaṃ vyapadeṣṭum / bhāvarūpamajñānamanirvacanīyaṃ jagadupādānamityādi pralāpamātramiti saṃbandhanirūpaṇe pratipādayiṣyate / ato na vedyadoṣāpanayanarūpā ahaṅkāreṇānubhavābhivyaktiḥ /
body.translated_text: like a pot and the like. For this very reason, it is not the assistance to the instrument of knowledge. For that [assistance] is [achieved] either: (1) by removing the obstacle to the arising of knowledge regarding the knowable — like a lamp removing darkness for the eye; or (2) by serving as the means for the proximity of the knowable — like a [transparent] individual or a mirror and the like for the eye, which makes known the universal, one's own face, and the like; or (3) by cleansing the defect in the knower — like tranquility, self-control, and the like for scripture, which is the means of knowledge of the reality of the higher and lower [self]. Now, first: there is nothing in experience-as-self that obstructs the arising of knowledge and that the I-cognition could remove. And as for <s>ajnana</s> (ignorance), since it has the same substrate and object as knowledge, it cannot be deposited in the witness (<s>saksin</s>) as you conceive it, which lacks both [substrate-hood and object-hood of knowledge]. For a pot and the like, which are devoid of any connection with knowledge, are not said to be 'ignorant.' Similarly, since mere knowledge never has the property of being a knower, there would be no ignorance for it either. Even on your own view, the I-cognition is not accepted as removing that [ignorance], because <s>ajnana</s> is removable only by knowledge, and because that is what is accepted. And knowledge removes <s>ajnana</s> only regarding its own object. And you do not accept that experience — which you hold to be the self — is the object of that [knowledge]. Hence the <s>ajnana</s> pertaining to it would never be dispelled by anything at any time. And <s>ajnana</s> in the form of the prior non-existence of knowledge cannot be designated as an obstacle to the arising of knowledge. As for <s>ajnana</s> as a positive entity, indeterminable, and the material cause of the world — that is mere prattle, as will be demonstrated in the examination of relations. Therefore, the manifestation of experience by the I-cognition is not in the form of removing a defect in the knowable.

body.text: astu vi'nubhavasya kenacidvyaṅgyatvam / astu vāhaṅkārasya kiñcidabhivyañjakatvam / paraṃ tadabhivyaṅgyaikasvabhāvasyāhaṅkārasya tadabhivyañjakatvamanupapannamityāha

children.translated_text: 'kinca'
('moreover').
'vyangyah'

children.text: ti / anubhavātmāhaṅkārayoḥ parasparaṃ vyaṅgyavyañjakabhāvo 'nupapannaḥ / prātikūlyataḥ-svabhāvavirodhalakṣaṇāduktātpratikūlabhāvata ityarthaḥ / niyamena tadvyaṅgyasvarūpasya tadvyañjakatvaṃ hi viruddhamiti proktam/ ahaṅkārasya saṃvidadhīnavyaktereva tadvyañjakatvaṃ syāt / mithyāpadārthasya pratibhāsādhīnasattākasya pratibhāsābhāve sattāyā eva dirlabhatvāt / saṃvicca svayaṃ bhāsamānaivāhaṅkāraṃ vyañjet / anyathā jaḍatvaprasaṅgāt / tathāca svaprakāśasaṃvidadhīnaprakāśāhaṅkārādhīnaprakāśatvaṃ saṃvida uktaṃ bhavet / tathā cānyonyāśrayaḥ-saṃvitprakāśādhīno 'haṅkāraprakāśaḥ ahaṅkāraprakāśādhīnaśca saṃvidaḥ prakāśa iti / uktalakṣaṇātprātikūlyādvādhakopanipātānna mitho vyaṅgyavyañjakatvaṃ saṃvidahaṅkārayoḥ saṃbhavatīti ca tātparyāntaraṃ varṇitaṃ śrīmannigamāntagurucaraṇaistattvaṭīkāyām / paramate saṃvido 'haṅkāravyaṅgyatve dūṣaṇāntaramāha
children.translated_text: ('the manifested'). The mutual relation of manifested and manifestor between the self that is experience and the I-cognition is untenable. 'Because of the contradiction' (<s>pratikulyatah</s>) — because of the stated unfavorable relation characterized by the contradiction of essential natures. This is the meaning. For it has been stated that the very nature of what is invariably manifested by that [awareness] having the capacity to manifest that [awareness] is contradictory. The I-cognition could be a manifestor only through its own manifestation being dependent on awareness. Because for a false entity, whose existence depends on its appearance, when there is no appearance its very existence is difficult [to maintain]. And awareness, being self-luminous, would manifest the I-cognition only [on that basis]. Otherwise there would follow the consequence of inertness. And thus, what has been stated is that the illumination of awareness depends on the I-cognition whose illumination depends on self-luminous awareness. And thus there is mutual dependence: the illumination of the I-cognition depends on the illumination of awareness, and the illumination of awareness depends on the illumination of the I-cognition. From the stated unfavorableness, because of the descent of a sublating [argument], the mutual manifested-manifestor relation between awareness and the I-cognition is not possible — this alternative interpretation has been set forth by the venerable teacher of the <s>Nigamanta</s> [i.e., Vedanta] in the <s>Tattvatika</s>. He states another defect in the opponent's view that awareness is manifested by the I-cognition with
'vyangyatve'
('if manifested'). If illumination is dependent on another, experience would have the consequence of being a non-experience, just as a pot and the like. This is the meaning.

body.translated_text: Let experience be manifested by something. Or let the I-cognition be a manifestor of something. But it is untenable that the I-cognition, whose sole nature is to be manifested by that [awareness], could be its manifestor — thus he says

children.translated_text: 'tadvya-'

children.text: ṅgyasyāpi tadvyañjakatve na virodhaḥ, dṛṣṭatvāditi śaṅkāmapanudati
children.translated_text: He removes the doubt that there is no contradiction even in the manifested being the manifestor of the very [entity that manifests it], because it is observed [in some cases], with
'dinakara' ('the sun').

children.text: ti / hastatalasya vātāyanavivarapraviṣṭasūryakiraṇānāṃ gatipratirodhena saṃhatimātrahetutvam / saṃhatānāṃ ca teṣāṃ sphuṭaprakāśaḥ svata evetyāha
children.translated_text: The palm of the hand merely causes the aggregation of the sun's rays that have entered through a window aperture, by obstructing their path. And those aggregated [rays] clearly shine on their own — thus he says
'karatalasya' ('of the palm of the hand').

children.text:
ti / gatipratirodhenāpi saṃvitsphuṭaprakāśahetutvaṃ karatalasyeva durghaṭamahaṅkārasyāmūrtasyeti hārdam /
evamahaṅkāravyaṅgyatvaṃ saṃvidātmano 'napekṣitamanupapannaṃ cetyuktam / abhivyaktiprakārāṇāṃ saṃbhāvitānāṃ prakṛte 'nupapatterapi nāhaṅkārasya tadabhivyañjakatvamityāha
children.translated_text: Even [the function of] causing the clear illumination of awareness through obstruction of motion is difficult for the I-cognition — which is formless — as for the palm of the hand. This is the inner meaning. Thus it has been stated that the manifestation by the I-cognition of the self that is awareness is neither needed nor tenable. Because the types of manifestation that were postulated are untenable in the present context, the I-cognition does not manifest it — thus he says
'api ca' ('moreover')

children.text:
tyādinā / tatsiddhiḥ- saṃvidātmaprakāśaḥ /
svaprakāśatvenānyāpekṣūprakāśatvābhāvopagamānna saṃvitprakāśahetutvamahaṅkārasya / saṃvido jñānāntarāgocaratvena tadviṣayakajñānajanakatvamapi tadabhivyañjakatvamahaṅkārasya neti prakāśanaprakāśakajñānajanakatvarūpābhivyañjakatvaprakāradvayaṃ dūṣitam /
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'That establishment' — the illumination of the self that is awareness. Because self-luminosity entails the acceptance of the absence of dependence on anything else for illumination, the I-cognition is not the cause of the illumination of awareness. And because awareness is not within the range of another knowledge, the capacity to generate knowledge regarding it as its object is also not the I-cognition's form of manifestation — thus two forms of manifestation, namely being the illuminator and being the generator of illuminating knowledge, have been refuted.
'ata eva' ('for this very reason')

children.text: ti / ananubhāvyatvādevānubhavasya tadviṣayakānubhavakaraṇasyāprasiddhyā tadanugrahalakṣaṇābhivyaktiprakāro 'pi na saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ / astu vā tajjñānakaraṇaṃ kiñcit / tadanugrahaprakārāḥ prakṛte na saṃbhavantīti vadan anugrahaṃ vikalpayatitāvat
children.translated_text: Because of the non-experienceability of experience itself, and because of the non-establishment of the instrument of knowledge regarding it as its object, even the type of manifestation characterized by assisting the instrument [of knowledge] is not possible. This is the meaning. Or let there be some instrument of knowledge regarding it. The types of assistance [to such an instrument] are not possible in the present context — thus saying, he examines the [possible types of] assistance with
'sa hi' ('for that').
'That' — assistance, characterized by providing the accessory-conditions to the apprehender.
'vedyagate' ('residing in the knowable')
The first alternative of assisting the instrument of knowledge through removing obstacles to the arising of knowledge regarding the knowable. He states the second with
'vedye' ('in the knowable').

children.text: ti / karaṇasya grāhyasannikarṣaprayojakatveneti yāvat / vyaktirhi svadvārā cakṣurādervedyajātyādisannikarṣaṃ saṃpādayati / darpaṇādiśca cākṣuṣaraśmigatiparāpartanena mukhādisannikarṣaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ / tṛtīyamāha
children.translated_text: In the sense that the instrument serves as the means for the proximity of the apprehensible. For an individual (<s>vyakti</s>) provides, through itself as a medium, the proximity of the universal (<s>jati</s>) and the like of the knowable to the eye and the like. And a mirror and the like, by deflecting the path of visual rays, [provide] the proximity of the face and the like to the eye. He states the third with
'vettrigate' ('residing in the knower').
'Defect' (<s>kalanka</s>) — sin and the like that obstruct the arising of knowledge.
'One who has not ceased from bad conduct'

children.text: dityādinā ca śamādestattvajñānajanakaśāstrasahakāritvaṃ jñāyate / niṣkāmakarmaṇā śamādinācāpākṛtapāparāgādidoṣasya śuddhacittasyaiva hi śāstreṇa tattvajñānotpattiḥ / prakṛte prathamānugrahakalpasyānupapattimaha
children.translated_text: — from this and the like, it is known that tranquility and the like serve as auxiliaries to scripture, which generates knowledge of reality. For only one whose mind is purified through the removal of defects such as sin, attachment, and the like — through desireless action and tranquility and the like — attains the knowledge of reality through scripture. The untenability of the first type of assistance in the present context [is stated with]
'na tavad' ('to begin with, not').

children.text: diti / nanvajñānameva jñānotpattivirodhi vedye 'nubhavātmani vartata iti cettatrāha
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But <s>ajnana</s> (ignorance), which obstructs the arising of knowledge, resides in the knowable, namely the self that is experience. To this he says
'ajnanam' ('ignorance').

children.text: iti / jñānena samānāvāśrayaviṣayau yasyaivaṃbhūtamajñānam, jñānasamānāśrayaṃ jñānasamānaviṣayaṃ ceti yāvat / tadubhayabhāvavirahiṇi-jñānāśrayatvajñānaviṣayatvarahite / nikṣepaṃ-padanyāsam, saṃbandhamiti yāvat / ajñānaṃ hi jñānaprāgabhāvarūpaṃ tatsamānayogakṣemaṃ vānyat jñātṛtvaprasaktiśūnye bhavadabhimate 'nubhavātmani na ghaṭate ghaṭādāviveti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>ajnana</s> that has the same substrate and object as knowledge — that is, what has the same substrate as knowledge and the same object as knowledge. 'In what lacks both those statuses' — in what lacks the status of being a substrate of knowledge and the status of being an object of knowledge. 'Deposit' — placement, i.e., connection. For <s>ajnana</s>, whether in the form of the prior non-existence of knowledge or as something else having the same fate as knowledge, does not fit in the self-as-experience as you conceive it — which is devoid of any connection with being a knower — just as in a pot and the like. This is the purport.
'bhavadapi' ('even on your view')

children.text: tyabhyupagamya vādaḥ / ātmāśritatve 'pyajñānasyāhaṅkāreṇa nivartyatvābhāvādvedyadoṣāpanāyakatvarūpamabhivyañjakatvaṃ na tasyeti bhāvaḥ / parābhimate 'nubhavātmani ajñānasyopagame 'niṣṭaṃ cāha
children.translated_text: — this is an argument based on the opponent's own acceptance. Even if <s>ajnana</s> resides in the self, since it is not removable by the I-cognition, the I-cognition does not have the capacity to manifest [the self] in the form of removing a defect in the knowable. This is the purport. He states the unwanted consequence if <s>ajnana</s> is accepted as residing in the self-as-experience, according to the opponent's view, with
'jnanam ca' ('and knowledge').

children.text:
ti / ātmaniṣṭhamātmaviṣayaṃ cājñānamātmano 'nanubhāvyatvājjñānānivartyaṃ nityaṃpra
sajyate, samānāśrayaviṣayatvenaiva jñānājñānayorbādhakabādhyabhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / ātmaviṣayakajñānopagamaśvāpasiddhāntaparāhataḥ / etenāntaḥ-karaṇavṛttivyāpyatvameveṣyate ātmanaḥ / natu tadavacchinnacaitanyavyāpyatvam / yena jaḍatvādi prasajyeta / ātmākārāntaḥkaraṇavṛttyaivātmājñānanivṛttirityapi nirastam / vṛtterjaḍabhūtāyā ajñānanivartakatvāyogāt / jñānameva hyajñānasya nivartakam / tadavacchinnacaitanyanivartyatve tu jñeyatvādyātmano 'varjanīyameveti dik / ajñānaṃ ca kiṃ jñānaprāgabhāvarūpam; āhosvidbhāvarūpamiti vikalpya dūṣayati
children.translated_text: <s>Ajnana</s> that resides in the self and has the self as its object, because the self is not experienceable [by another knowledge], is not removable by knowledge and becomes permanent — because it is only through having the same substrate and object that knowledge and <s>ajnana</s> have the relation of sublater and sublated. This is the purport. The acceptance of knowledge regarding the self contradicts the established doctrine that [the self is not an object of knowledge]. By this, what is accepted for the self is pervadedness by the modification of the internal organ (<s>antahkarana</s>) alone. Not pervadedness by consciousness delimited by that [modification]. For from that [latter view], inertness and the like would follow. The [view] that <s>ajnana</s> of the self is removed by the modification of the internal organ in the form of the self is also refuted — because the modification, being inert, cannot remove <s>ajnana</s>. For only knowledge is the remover of <s>ajnana</s>. And if [it were] removable by consciousness delimited by that [modification], then the knowability and the like of the self would be unavoidable. This is the gist. He examines whether <s>ajnana</s> is in the form of the prior non-existence of knowledge or is a positive entity, and refutes [both], with
'jnane'
and so forth, in two sentences.
Because the instruments [of knowledge] have no scope [here], [the I-cognition] cannot be the cause of [the self's] connection [with knowledge].
Because the 'I'-object has the nature of the knower, it is not purified by that very [I-cognition].

children.text: na ca svāśrayatayābhivyaṅgyaprakāśanamabhivyañjayituḥ svabhāvaḥ; pradīpādāvadarśanāt / yathāvasthitavastuprakāśānukūlasvabhāvatvācca jñānatatsādhanatadanugrāhakāṇām / tacca svataḥprāmāṇyanyāyāt; tadanabhyupagame ca sarvatrānāścāsaprakaṅgāt / vyaktestu jātirākāra eveti tathā pratyāyanam; na vyañjakatvaprayuktam ; uktādeva vyabhicārāt / darpaṇādistu nāyanamahaḥpratiphalanalakṣaṇadoṣaheturnābhivyañjako vadanādeḥ / vyañjakastvālokādireva / vyañjakatve 'pi pratīpagamanadoṣaprayuktastatrānyathāvabhāsaḥ / na ceha tathāhamarthasya tādṛśadoṣāpādakatvaṃ svabhāvaḥ / tathā sati sarvasyāpi pratyakṣāderaprāmāṇyaprasaṅgānna kiñcittathyaṃ syāt / tasmājjñātṛtayā siddhyannahamartha eva pratyagātmā; na jñaptimātram /
children.translated_text: And it is not the essential nature of the manifestor to illuminate through being the substrate of the manifested — because this is not observed in lamps and the like. And because knowledge, its instruments, and their auxiliaries have an essential nature favorable to the illumination of things as they are. And that [self-validity] is from the principle of <s>svatahpramanya</s> (intrinsic validity). And if that is not accepted, there would follow the consequence of [all cognitions being] unreliable everywhere. As for the individual (<s>vyakti</s>), it is only the form of the universal (<s>jati</s>) — so its making known [of the universal] is due to that [universal-form], not due to being a manifestor — because of the deviation already stated. And the mirror and the like are not manifestors of the face and the like, but rather the cause of a defect characterized by the reflection of the light of the eye — while the manifestor [of the face reflected in the mirror] is light and the like alone. Even if it is a manifestor, the erroneous appearance there is caused by the defect of reverse travel [of light]. And here, it is not the essential nature of the 'I'-object to produce such a defect [in the self]. If it were so, then since even perception and all other [cognitions would] have the consequence of being invalid, nothing would be true. Therefore, the 'I'-object — which is established as the knower — is the inner self (<s>pratyagatman</s>); not mere awareness alone.
(Thus ends the section on the refutation of the I-cognition as the manifestor of awareness.)

children.text: yattu suṣuptisuktayorjñaptimātratayā sphuraṇam, ahamiti tu na pratibhātīti; tatra suṣuptau tathāvasthitiḥ purastādeva nirastā / ahamityekarūpeṇa āprabodhāttatrāpyātmanaḥ sphuraṇāt / yadi paraṃ parāgarthānanubhavāttamoguṇābhibhavācca na vivicya sphuṭaṃ cakāsti; bhavadabhimatānubhūtirapi tadānīṃ tathaiva hi prathata iti vācyam / nāhamaham, nāpyarthāntaram, api tvanubhūtimātramajñānasākṣitayāvatiṣṭhata ityevaṃvidhaṃ svāpasamayabhavamanubhavaṃ nahi suptotthitaḥ kaścit parāmṛśannupalabdhacaraḥ / etāvantaṃ kālaṃ na kiñcidahamavediṣamiti parāmarśanādeva tathātvaṃ labhyata iti cet; kathamiva? na kiñciditi nirdeśāditi cet; nanvevamanubhūtipratibhāso 'pi pratyākhyātaḥ syāt / api ca suṣuptisamayasiddhamātmānamahamiti parāmṛśya na kiñcidavediṣaṃmiti tasya vedane pratiṣidhyamāne tātkālikīṃ
children.translated_text: As for the [objection that] in deep sleep and in the scriptural statement [about deep sleep], there is the shining of mere awareness, but it does not appear as 'I' — regarding that: the position that [the self] exists in that way in deep sleep has already been refuted previously. Because the self shines in the single form 'I' even up to the point of awakening [i.e., throughout sleep]. If however [it is said that] due to the non-experience of external objects and the overpowering by the quality of <s>tamas</s>, it does not shine distinctly and clearly — then it must be said that the experience as you conceive it too shines in exactly the same way at that time. 'Not I, not I, nor anything else, but mere experience alone subsists as the witness of <s>ajnana</s>' — no one who has risen from sleep is found to recollect such an experience occurring during the time of deep sleep. [Objection:] Such [a state] is obtained from the recollection 'for so long, I did not know anything' alone. [Reply:] How so? [Objection:] Because of the expression 'nothing.' [Reply:] But then, by the same token, even the appearance of experience [during sleep] would be rejected. Moreover, having recollected the self that is established during the time of deep sleep as 'I,' when knowledge is denied in 'I did not know anything' — at that time

body.text: vittisiddhimahamarthasya cāsiddhimabhidadhāno 'nubhavavirodhamapi na jānāti devānāṃ priyaḥ / nirviṣayā nirāśrayā ca vittirnāstītyuktameva /
body.translated_text: The dear friend of the gods, while stating the unestablishedness of the 'I'-object for the establishment of awareness (<s>vitti</s>), does not even know the contradiction with experience. It has already been said that awareness without an object and without a substrate does not exist.

body.text: nanu māmapyahaṃ na jñātavān prasupta ityasti hi prabodhe pratyayaḥ / satyam; sa tu varṇāśramādiviśiṣṭatayā prabodhasamayasaṃvedyamānaṃ dehinaṃ māmityādāya svāpyayāvasthāprasiddhāviśadasvānubhavaikatānāhamarthasya tena rūpeṇājñātatvaṃ prajñātatvaṃ prajñāpayati, na punarjñasvabhāvasyāhamarthasyāpi / evamiva khalvayamanubhavaḥ-atra supto 'hamīdṛśaścetyevaṃ māmapi na jñātavānahamiti / api ca, ātmā suṣuptau ajñānasākṣitvenā'sta iti hi yauṣmākī sthitiḥ / sākṣitvaṃ ca sākṣājjñātṛtvamityuktam / sa cāyaṃ jānāmīti pratibhāsamāno 'smadartha eveti kathamiva tadānīmahamartho na pratheta / svasmai prakāśamāno 'hamityeva hi prakāśata iti / tatsiddhaṃ svāpādidaśāsvapyātmā prakāśamāno 'hamityeva prakāśata iti /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But there is indeed this cognition upon waking: 'I did not know even myself while asleep.' True; but that [cognition], taking the embodied self — which is apprehended at the time of waking as qualified by class, social order (<s>varṇāśrama</s>), and the like — as 'myself,' indicates [merely] that the 'I'-object, whose nature in deep sleep is an uninterrupted dim self-experience, was not known in that form [i.e., as qualified by varṇāśrama and the like] — but not [that] the 'I'-object, whose essential nature is knowledge, [was absent]. Indeed, this experience is of the following kind: 'I, being of such-and-such a nature, slept here — and I did not know even myself [as such].' Moreover, your own position is that the self in deep sleep exists as the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) of ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>). And witness-hood has been said to be direct knower-hood. And this [witness], appearing as 'I know,' is indeed our very 'I'-object — so how could the 'I'-object not shine forth at that time? For what is luminous for itself shines forth precisely as 'I.' Therefore it is established: even in deep sleep and the like, the self shines forth precisely as 'I.'

children.translated_text: (Thus ends the section on the justification of the appearance of the 'I'-object in deep sleep.)

body.text: yattu muktāvahamartho nopāvartata iti; tadvārtam / yatastathā sati vaināśikadarśana ivātmanāśa evāpavargaḥ prakārāntareṇa pratijñātaḥ syāt / no khalu ahamiti dharmamātram, yena tadapagame 'pyavidyānivṛttyāmivātmanaḥ svarūpeṇāvatiṣṭhata ityucyate / ahamityeva hi tasya svarūpam / jñānamapi hi taddharmatvena tasyaiva prakāśate jñānaṃ me jātamiti / kā kathā punararthāntarasyā'tmatve ? /
body.translated_text: As for [the objection] that the 'I'-object does not recur in liberation — that is mere gossip. Because in that case, just as in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> doctrine, liberation would be proclaimed as the destruction of the self in another guise. 'I' is certainly not a mere property, such that — upon its removal, like the removal of <s>avidyā</s> — the self could be said to remain in its essential nature. For its essential nature is precisely 'I.' Even knowledge appears as its property: 'Knowledge has arisen in me.' What to speak, then, of anything else being the self?

body.text: anyaśca-yaḥ sāṃsārikaduḥkhaiḥ duḥkhitvenā'tmānaṃ tattvatobhrāntyā vā pratyeti duḥkhyahamiti, saḥ sarvamidamaniṣṭajātaṃ kathamahamapunarūdayapanudyāvyākulaḥ svastho bhūyāsamiti sañjātamumukṣaḥ tatsādhane pravartate / sa yadi sādhanānuṣṭhānādahameva na bhaviṣyāmītyavagacchati, apagacchedasau mokṣakathāprasaṅgādapi / tataścāsambhavadadhikāritayā sarva eva vedāntavidhayaḥ sarvāṇi ca mokṣaśāstrāṇi prāmāṇyādeva pracyaveran / ahamupalakṣitaḥ prakāśo 'pavarge 'vasthāsyata iti cet, kimataḥ? na hi mayi naṣṭe 'pi ko 'pi prakāśaḥ sthāsyatīti kaścitprekṣāvān prayasyati /
body.translated_text: And another [consideration]: one who cognizes the self as afflicted by the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> — whether in truth or through error — [thinking] 'I am suffering,' having developed the desire for liberation, [thinking] 'How may I, free from disturbance, having forever removed all this that is undesirable, become tranquil?' — such a one engages in the means to that [liberation]. If he understands that through the practice of the means he himself will not exist at all, he would turn away even from the very talk of liberation. And consequently, since there would be no qualified aspirant due to [this] impossibility, all the injunctions of <s>Vedānta</s> and all the treatises on liberation would fall from their validity. [Objection:] If it is said that the luminosity marked by 'I' will remain in liberation — [Reply:] What of it? For no discerning person would exert himself [thinking] 'Even when I am destroyed, some luminosity will remain.'

children.text: etena tadapi parāstam, asmatpratyaye yo 'nidamaṃśaḥ cidekarasaḥ prakāśaḥ sa ātmā / tasmiṃstadbalanirbhāsitatayā lakṣaṇato yuṣmadartha evāhaṃ jānāmīti sidhyannartha
children.translated_text: By this, the following too is set aside: 'In the I-cognition, the non-this aspect — the homogeneous consciousness that is pure luminosity — is the self. Within it, [the knower-object] that manifests by its power and is technically of the nature of the you-object appears as established in "I know"'

body.text: iti / pratyakṣavirodhāt / ahaṃ jānāmīti sidhyaścetano suṣmadartha iti mātā bandhyetivadvyāhatārthaṃvacaḥ / na cāsau anyādhīnāvabhāsaḥ, caitanyasvabhāvatayā svayañjyotiṣṭvāt / prakāśaśca prakāśatvādeva kasyacidbhaveddīpādiprakāśavaditi nātmā bhavitumarhati / ato jñātṛtayāhamiti siddhyannartha evā'tmā /
body.translated_text: — [this is set aside] because of contradiction with perception. The statement 'the conscious [entity] that is established as the you-object in "I know"' is self-contradictory, like saying 'My mother is barren.' Nor is it [the self] one whose appearance depends on something else, because — having consciousness as its essential nature — it is self-luminous. And luminosity, being merely luminosity, could belong to anything, like the luminosity of a lamp and the like — so it is not fit to be the self. Therefore, the self is precisely the 'I'-object that is established as the knower.

body.text: sa ca muktāvapyātmane 'hamityeva prakāśate, svasmai prakāśamānatvāt / yo yaḥ svasmai prakāśate sa sarvo 'hamityeva prakāśamānodṛṣṭaḥ, yathā tathāvabhāsamānatvenobhayavādisaṃmataḥ saṃsāryātmā / yaḥ punarahamiti na cakāsti nāsau svasmai prakāśate, yathā ghaṭādiḥ / svasmai prakāśate cāyaṃ muktātmā / tasmāt so 'hamityeva prakāśate / na caivaṃ prakāśamānatve muktasyājñānitvasaṃsāritvādiprasaṅga āpādanīyaḥ / muktatvavirodhāt / atadupādhitvācca tatpratyayasya / na hyajñānopādhirahaṃpratyayaḥ / brahmātmaparokṣajñānakṣapitaniravaśeṣāvidyānāmapi vāmadevādīnāma(me) tatpratyayadarśanāt / śrayate hi 'taddhaitatpaśyan ṛṣirvāmadevaḥ pratipede ahaṃ manurabhavaṃ suryaśca ahameva ca vartāmi bhaviṣyāmī'tyādi / tathā kathañcidapyavidyādikleśairleśato 'pi jātucidaparāmaṣṭasya paramapuruṣasyāpyahamityātmaparāmarśaḥ prajñāyate 'hantāhamimāstistro devatāḥ' 'bahu syāṃ prajāyeya' 'sar ikṣata lokānnu sṛjā iti', tathā- 'yasmāt kṣaramatīto 'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ / ato 'smiloke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ' // 'teṣāmahaṃ samuddhartā ' 'ahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitāḥ' 'vedāhaṃ samatītāni' ityevamādibhiḥ /
body.translated_text: And that [self], even in liberation, shines forth for itself precisely as 'I' — because of being luminous for itself. Whatever is luminous for itself is observed to shine forth precisely as 'I' — like the self in <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is agreed upon by both sides as shining forth in precisely that manner. But whatever does not shine forth as 'I' — that is not luminous for itself, like a pot and the like. And this liberated self is luminous for itself. Therefore, it shines forth precisely as 'I.' Nor should the consequence of the liberated [self] being ignorant or being in <s>saṃsāra</s> and the like be charged when it shines forth thus — because of the contradiction with being liberated. And because the I-cognition is not conditioned by that [ignorance]. For the I-cognition does not have ignorance as its conditioning adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>). Because even for <s>Vāmadeva</s> and others, whose entire <s>avidyā</s> has been destroyed by the direct knowledge of the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and self, the I-cognition is observed. For it is heard: 'The seer, the sage <s>Vāmadeva</s>, seeing this, understood: "I was <s>Manu</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>. I exist now and shall exist hereafter."' Similarly, even for the Supreme Person (<s>Paramapuruṣa</s>), who is never even slightly touched by <s>avidyā</s> and other afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), the self-apprehension as 'I' is recognized: 'Let me enter these three deities,' 'May I become many, may I be born,' 'He considered: Let me create the worlds.' Likewise: 'Because I transcend the perishable and am higher than even the imperishable, therefore I am celebrated in the world and in the <s>Veda</s> as <s>Puruṣottama</s>.' 'I am their deliverer,' 'I am the seed-giving father,' 'I know all past [beings]' — and so forth.

body.text: evaṃ ca sākṣādahamarthādātmano vilakṣaṇe 'pi dehe yenā'vyaktikapariṇāmabhedenāhamiti bhramaḥ, tadabhiprāyo 'haṅkārasya kṣetrāntarbhāvopadeśo bhagavataḥ 'mahābhūtānyahaṅkāra' iti / bahumantavyajanāvadhīraṇahetuścāsau garvāparaparyāyaḥ tatra tatra śāstreṣu prāyaśoheyatayopadiśyate / tasmādahamiti matirbādhakāpetā sākṣādātmagocaraiva / anātmani tu śarīre bhavantī avidyeti yuktam / uktaṃ ca 'śrūyatāṃ cāpyavidyāyāḥ svarūpaṃ kulanandana / anātmanyātmabuddhiryā' iti maharṣiṇā vāsiṣṭhanandanena / naca jñaptimātra pratibhāsaḥ kasyacit śarīre 'sti / yena tanmātrātmavādino 'pyanātma (nyotma) buddhirupapadyeta /
body.translated_text: And thus, the intention behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching that includes <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) within the 'field' (<s>kṣetra</s>) — 'the great elements, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>...' — is that even regarding the body, which is different from the 'I'-object that directly [refers to] the self, there is the error of 'I' through a particular modification of the <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest <s>Prakṛti</s>). And that [ego-sense], being a cause of disregard for those who are to be honored — having the alternative name 'pride' (<s>garva</s>) — is for the most part taught as something to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>) in the various <s>śāstras</s>. Therefore, the cognition 'I,' when free from sublation, has directly the self as its object. But when it occurs regarding the non-self, namely the body, it is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — this is fitting. And as the great sage, the son of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [i.e., <s>Parāśara</s>], has said: 'Hear also the essential nature of <s>avidyā</s>, dear son of the clan: it is the cognition of selfhood in what is not the self.' Nor does anyone have the appearance of mere cognition (<s>jñaptimātra</s>) in the body — by which, even for the proponent of mere-cognition-as-self, the cognition of selfhood in the non-self would be explicable.

body.text: dvitīye 'nugrahakalpe dūṣaṇaṃ

children.translated_text: 'of the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>)'

children.text:
iti / abhūmitvāt-aviṣayatvāt / indriyāgrā
hyatvādātmano nātmendriyasannikarṣopādhitvenābhivyañjakatvamahaṅkārasya saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ / tṛtīye dūṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: — 'because of inappropriateness' — because of not being an object [of the senses]. The meaning is: because the self is ungraspable by the senses, the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> cannot have the status of manifesting [the self] by way of being a condition for the contact between the self and the sense organs. The refutation of the third [alternative]:
'of the I-object'

children.text: ti / svagatakalmaṣasya svenaiva kevalena nivartanāyogānna tṛtīyo 'pi kalpaḥ kalpata ityarthaḥ //13//
children.translated_text: — the meaning is: because the internal impurity (<s>kalmaṣa</s>) [of the self] cannot be removed by itself alone, the third alternative too does not work.

body.translated_text: The refutation of the second alternative of the [three] interpretive possibilities [regarding how ahaṅkāra manifests the self]:

body.text: evaṃ vyañjakatvaṃ nirasya parābhimataṃ vyañjakasvabhāvamapi nirasyati

children.translated_text: 'na ca'

children.text: ti / pradīpo hi ghaṭādeḥ prakāśako na svavṛttitayā taṃ prakāśayati / na khalvevaṃ pratītiḥ pradīpe ghaṭa iti, pradīpo ghaṭavāniti vā / kintu yathāvasthitaveṣeṇaiva bhūtale ghaṭa itīti bhavadukte niyame 'naikāntyamiti bhāvaḥ / jñānādīnāṃ yathāvasthitavastuprakāśahetutvamevetyatra yuktimāha
children.translated_text: ('nor'). For a lamp, which illuminates a pot and the like, does not illuminate it by way of existing in it (<s>svavṛtti</s>). Indeed, the experience is not: 'The pot is in the lamp' or 'The lamp possesses the pot.' Rather, [the experience is:] 'The pot is on the ground, in its actual position.' The sense is: the invariable rule you stated is inconclusive. He states the reasoning for [the view that] knowledge and the like are simply the cause of illuminating objects as they are, with
'tac ca'

children.text: ti / prāmāṇyasvatastvātmakayukterityarthaḥ / jñānasāmagrīprayojyatvaṃ jñānabhāsakasāmagrībhāsyatvaṃ ca prāmāṇyasyotpattau jñaptau ca svatastvam / nanu svataḥprāmāṇye kvacijjñāne viparītākārāvagāhanaṃ kutaḥ? jñānasāmagrayāmatiriktadoṣasaṃvalanādeva / svataḥprāmāṇyagrahe 'pyanabhyāsadaśāpannajñāne prāmāṇyasaṃśayaśca doṣamūlatvasaṃśayādeveti ca bodhyam / prāmāṇyasya svatastvānupagame bādhakamāha
children.translated_text: ('and that'). The meaning is: through the reasoning that constitutes the doctrine of the intrinsic validity of knowledge (<s>svataḥprāmāṇya</s>). The intrinsic validity [means]: knowledge's being produced by the causal complex of knowledge, and knowledge's being made known by the causal complex that makes knowledge known. [Objection:] But if validity is intrinsic, whence comes the apprehension of an inverted form in some cognitions? [Reply:] Precisely from the contamination by a defect extrinsic to the causal complex of knowledge. And it should be understood that even when intrinsic validity is accepted, the doubt about validity in cognition that has not reached the stage of familiarity arises precisely from the doubt about the root being a defect. He states the defeating consequence if the intrinsic validity of knowledge is not accepted, with
'tadanabhyupagame'

children.text: iti / sarvajñāneṣvapi aprāmāṇyaśaṅkāprasakteḥ prāmāṇyasya svatastvānupagame svatastvameṣṭavyam / anyathā tu jāte 'pi prāmāṇyaniścaye 'prāmāṇyaśaṅkā nirargalaprasarā bhavedeva / niṣkampapravṛttiśca kutrāpi na ghaṭeteti bhāvaḥ / vyakte riti / vyakternābhivyañjakatvaprayuktaṃ svāśritatayā jāteḥ prakāśanam / kintu vyaktayapṛthaksiddhaprakāratvarūpavastusvabhāvādeva / vyañjakastvālokādireva / vyaktervyañjakatvamapi na saṃpratipannamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: ('if that is not accepted'). Because the suspicion of invalidity would attach to all cognitions — if the intrinsic validity of knowledge is not accepted, intrinsic validity must be accepted. Otherwise, even after the determination of validity has arisen, the suspicion of invalidity would have an unobstructed course. And unwavering activity would not be possible anywhere — this is the sense. 'Of the universal (<s>vyakti</s>)' — the illumination of the universal (<s>jāti</s>), which subsists inseparably in the universal, is not caused by [the universal's] being a manifestor (<s>abhivyañjaka</s>). Rather, [it is] simply from the essential nature of the thing — the form of being an inseparable mode (<s>apṛthaksiddhaprakāratva</s>) of the universal. The manifestor, however, is light (<s>āloka</s>) and the like. The sense is: the manifesting function of the universal itself is also not accepted.
'darpaṇādi'

children.text: riti / darpaṇādi pratihatagateścākṣuṣatejasaḥ pratinivṛtya mukhābhimukhatayā prasaraṇameva mukhasyānyathāpratītau doṣarūpaṃ prayojakam / pratilomagatirūpadoṣaprayojakasya darpaṇādervyañjakatvaṃ bhavatu, mā vā / na vyañjakatvaprayuktamanyathābhānamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: ('mirror and the like'). What is responsible — as a defect — for the otherwise-cognition of the face is precisely the reversal of the visual faculty's course: the visual ray, having its course obstructed by the mirror and the like, turns back and proceeds toward the face. Let the mirror and the like, whose defect consists in this reversed course, have or not have the status of manifestor — the otherwise-appearance is not caused by the manifesting function. This is the sense.
'na ca iha'
('nor here'). 'The capacity to produce such a defect' — the capacity to produce a defect in the form of an operation conducive to inverted apprehension on the part of the instruments of knowledge.
'tathā sati'

children.text: ti / pramāṇādhīnapramitāvahamarthasyāpi hetutvāt pramāṇadoṣasaṃpādakatve tasya na kiñcidapi yathārthajñānaṃ saṃbhavetpramāṇajanyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: ('in that case'). The meaning is: because the 'I'-object too is a cause of cognition that depends on a means of valid knowledge, if it has the capacity to produce defects in the means of valid knowledge, then no veridical knowledge whatsoever — produced by a means of valid knowledge — would be possible.
'tasmāt'

children.text:
diti / jñātṛtvapratīterniruktadiśā bhrāntitvāyogājjñātṛtayā siddhyannahamartha evātmā / na jñāptimātramiti bhāvaḥ / atrāyaṃ prayogaḥ-jñānaṃ nātmā dharmatayā pramitatvādrūpādivaditi / evaṃ jñāturahamarthasyātmatvaṃ samarthitam /
