Nor, when the non-<s>āhaṅkārika</s> nature and being-for-another-composite are refuted by another means of valid knowledge, should the [argument from] composite-being-for-another's-sake also be abandoned as unrefuted. Thus the self, being non-composite, is established as devoid of the three <s>guṇas</s> and such which are invariably associated with composite-ness.

children.text: tathā dehādayaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatayā pareṇādhiṣṭhīyante, yantrādibhiriva rathādayaḥ / api
children.translated_text: Likewise, the body and so forth, being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, are presided over by another — just as chariots and such [are presided over] by machines and the like. More-

over, pleasure and pain, which are experienced as agreeable and disagreeable respectively, [require an experiencer] — just as a servant and a rival kinsman [are understood as such only in relation to]  agreeable and disagreeable [treatment].

body.text: kūlanīyavatī / dṛśyatvāddehādayo ghaṭādaya iva vilakṣaṇadraṣṭṭakā iti / adhiṣṭhāturanukūlapratikūlavedakasya draṣṭuḥ traiguṇyādiviparyayaḥ pūrvavadeva nirṇetavyaḥ / tathā dehāderavyaktāntasya kṛtsnsya triguṇātmakatayātyantaduḥkhopaśamanalakṣaṇamokṣadaśānupapatteḥ tadarthaṃ ca śāstrāṇāṃ mahādhiyāṃ ca pravṛtterasti dehādivyatirikto 'saṃhataḥ traiguṇyādyasaṃspṛṣṭaḥ puruṣa iti //
body.translated_text: to be drawn down [i.e., the conclusion follows]. The body and the like, being visible, have a seer of a distinct nature — like a pot and the like. The contrariety regarding the three <s>gunas</s> and the like of the seer — who perceives what is favorable and unfavorable to the controller — is to be determined just as before. Likewise, since the entire [reality] from the body to the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), being of the nature of the three <s>gunas</s>, cannot [attain] the state of liberation characterized by the complete cessation of extreme suffering — and since the scriptures and the great sages are engaged [in instruction] for that purpose — there exists a <s>purusa</s> (conscious self) distinct from the body and the like, non-composite, untouched by the three <s>gunas</s> and the like.

body.text: (iti sāṅkhyābhimatātmānumānanirūpaṇam)

children.text: atrāpi saṅghātapārārthyādibhiryadyapi paraḥ ko 'pyadhiṣṭhātā draṣṭā siddhaḥ, tathāpi na tasyāsaṃhatatvātriguṇatvādirabhimataviśeṣaḥ śakyaniścayaḥ / tathāhi-saṅghātasya saṅghātāntarārthatvaniyamadarśanabalādāpatantī parāparā saṅghātakalpanā na doṣāya, kāryatayevānādi kāraṇaparamparāparikalpanā / na cāprayojakatvamapi; asaṅghātasyāsaṅgasyāśeṣavikriyāśūnyasyānādheyātiśayakūṭasthacitimātravapuṣaḥ puruṣasya saṅghātaṃ prati paratvānupapatteḥ / tadvi tasya śeṣi bhavati, tacca tadartham; yadyenopakriyate kriyate vā, yaccopakaroti karoti vā / na ca tathā sāṅkhyapuruṣa iti kataṃ tasya saṅghātaṃ prati paratvam ? kathantarāṃ ca saṅghātasya tādarthyam ? / anupakāryopyupakāryatayā'tmānaṃ manyata iti cet; kāmaṃ manyatām; kimāyātamupakāryatvasya? / na khalu bālāstalamalinatādimattayā gaganamabhimanyanta iti tasya tathātvaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Even here, although through the being-for-another-purpose of the aggregate and the like, some other controller and seer is established — nevertheless, the specific attributes he holds, such as being non-composite, being free from the three <s>gunas</s>, and the like, cannot be ascertained with certainty. For thus: the successive postulation of further aggregates, arising by the force of observing that an aggregate invariably serves the purpose of another aggregate, is not a fault — just like the postulation of a beginningless chain of causes through being effects. Nor is it purposeless — because for the <s>purusa</s>, who is non-composite, unattached, devoid of all modifications, incapable of receiving any further excellence, and whose form is merely immutable consciousness — subordination to the aggregate is untenable. The superior (<s>sesin</s>) is one toward whom [things] serve as accessories; and that [aggregate] exists for that [superior's sake]. That by which [the superior] is benefited or served, and that which benefits or serves — but the <s>Sankhya purusa</s> is not so. Then what is its superiority over the aggregate? And how is the aggregate for its sake? [Objection:] Even though not [actually] benefited, it considers itself benefited. [Reply:] Let it consider so as it pleases; what has come of [actual] benefited-ness? For it is not the case that because children imagine the sky to be dirty and the like, it thereby becomes so.

children.text: api ca tathāvidhabhramo 'pi kasya kathamudayata iti vivecanīyam / na tāvaccitiśakteḥ; sarvavikriyāśūnyatayātiviśuddhāyāmaśubhaśatanidānabhūtabhramapariṇāmāsambhavāt / antaḥkaraṇaṃ tu buddhyaparaparibhāṣābhidhānamacetanatayā tanuriva na bhrāmyati / acidapi svacchatayā citicchāyāpannaṃ cetanāyata iti cet; na; nīrūpāyāḥ citerbuddheśca chāyātadgrahaṇānupapatte / chāyeva chāyeti cet; kaḥ khalu ivārtha? ;citisarūpatvamiti cet; hantaivamaśeṣavikārarahitacitisarūpatāpattāvantaḥkaraṇamapi pratyastamitasamastavṛttikamāpadyata iti durupapādataro 'yaṃ bhramasukhaduḥkhādivikārayogaḥ pratyātmasiddhaḥ / cetanatvena sarūpatvamiti cet; na; citireva hi te puruṣaḥ, na cetayitā / yathā'ha tatrabhavān patañjaliḥ "
children.translated_text: Moreover, even such an error — for whom and how does it arise? — this should be examined. Not, to begin with, from the power of consciousness (<s>citisakti</s>); because in [consciousness] that is utterly pure through being devoid of all modifications, the transformation into error — which is the source of a hundred inauspicious [consequences] — is impossible. And the internal organ (<s>antahkarana</s>), designated by another name as <s>buddhi</s>, being non-conscious, does not err, like a body. [Objection:] Even the non-conscious, through its transparency, when it has taken on the reflection of consciousness, becomes as if conscious. [Reply:] No; because consciousness is formless and <s>buddhi</s> [is material], both the reflection and the apprehension of that [reflection] are untenable. [Objection:] Like a reflection, it is merely like a reflection. [Reply:] What is the point of the word 'like'? [Objection:] Similarity of form with consciousness. [Reply:] Alas! If it attains similarity of form with consciousness that is devoid of all modification, then the internal organ too would become one in which all mental activities have ceased — hence this [alleged] conjunction of error, pleasure, suffering, and the like of modification, which is established in one's own experience, becomes even harder to account for. [Objection:] The similarity of form is in being conscious. [Reply:] No; for your <s>purusa</s> is consciousness itself, not a conscious agent. As the venerable <s>Patanjali</s> says:

children.text: yadā citireva puruṣaḥ kimatra kena vyapadiśyata
children.translated_text: 'When consciousness alone is the <s>purusa</s>, what is designated here by whom?'

children.text: iti / ajaḍāyamānatvamivārtha iti cet; ajaḍatvamapi na jñātṛtvā
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The meaning of 'like' is 'becoming as if non-inert.' [Reply:] Non-inertness too is nothing other than being a knower

body.translated_text: (Thus ends the examination of the inference for the self as maintained by the <s>Sankhyas</s>.)

body.text: tirikta kiñcidityuktameva / tenaiva tadvivaraṇamiti ca na kiñcidetat / api ca citisannidhānādhīnāṃ buddhisiddhimabhidadhānaḥ kathamiva tadajaḍimānaṃ pratijānīyāt? naca citisvāntayorbimbapratibimbādhārābhimatayoranyatarasminnapyavidyamānasya viṣayaviśeṣoparaktajñātṛtvalakṣaṇadharmabhedasya pratibimbe sambhavaḥ / pratyuktaścāyaṃ pratibimbavādaḥ pracchannabāhyamatapratyādeśe /
body.translated_text: — this has already been stated. And [the claim] that it is explained by that very [non-inertness] amounts to nothing. Moreover, how could one who asserts the establishment of <s>buddhi</s> as dependent on the proximity of consciousness claim non-inertness for it? And in the image-reflection model accepted [by the opponent] regarding consciousness and the internal organ — a specific property characterized by knower-hood colored by a specific object, which does not exist in either of them — cannot arise in the reflection. And this reflection theory has been refuted in the rejection of the covert externalist [Advaita] view.

body.text: yaducyate-nirvikārāyāpi puṃse tatsannidhimahimasamutthāpitapramāṇaviparyayādivicitravṛttibhedaṃ svāntameva svavṛttiṃ viṣayaviśeṣāṃścopadarśayati, sāmantacakramiva parākramīyaḥ pratibalavilolanādivṛttīḥ svāmine, tataḥ sākṣī bhoktā cāpadiśyate, rājeti vikramī vijayī ceti; tadanupapannam / draṣṭre hi darśanīyaṃ dṛśyate / naca dṛśimātrātmavādināṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ tadupajīvināṃ ca pracchannānāṃ draṣṭṛtvaṃ vāstavamasti / naca kālpanikena śeṣitvasambhavaḥ / kalpanāpi na sambhavatītyuktameva / rājā tu sāmānyato viśeṣato vā teṣu karmasvamātyān niyuñjānaḥ tatphalamaiśvaryādi cāśruvānaḥ svasvāmibhāvahetukrayapratigrahajananādi- vyāpārayogī na niṣkriyasyānādheyātiśayasya puṃso nidarśanamiti yatkiñcidetat /
body.translated_text: As for the statement: 'Even for the <s>purusa</s> who is without modifications, the internal organ — whose variegated modifications of valid cognition, error, and the like have been raised by the majesty of his proximity — displays to [the <s>purusa</s>] its own modifications and the specific objects, like a retinue displaying to the master the activities of the opposing forces such as agitation and the like; hence he is designated as witness and enjoyer — just as [the master is called] king, valiant, and victorious' — that is untenable. For what is to be seen is seen by the seer. And for the <s>Sankhyas</s> who hold the view that the self is mere sight (<s>drsi</s>), and for the covert [Advaitins] who rely on them, there is no real seer-hood. And with a merely constructed [seer-hood], the <s>sesin</s>-relation (being the principal) is not possible. And even the construction is not possible, as has been stated. But a king, who engages his ministers in specific or general tasks, who experiences the fruits such as sovereignty and the like, and who is capable of activities such as purchase, acceptance, and birth that are the causes of the master-servant relation — is not an example for the <s>purusa</s>, who is without activity and incapable of receiving any further excellence. So this amounts to nothing.

body.text: (iti kāpilābhimatātmānumānanirasanam)

children.text: sthūlo 'haṃ, gacchābhyahamityādipratyakṣamṛditaviṣayatayā prasiddhaivātītakālatā vyatorekānumānabhedānāmityānumānikīmapyātmasiddhimaśraddadhānāḥ śrautīmeva tāṃ śrotiyāḥ saṅgirante /
children.translated_text: Since the subject matter of the perceptions 'I am stout,' 'I go,' and the like has been crushed [i.e., the bodily identification refuted], the past-ness is well-established for the varieties of separation-inferences. Therefore, those who do not accept even the inferential establishment of the self, the scriptural scholars (<s>srotriyas</s>) accept only its scriptural [establishment].
For the scriptures directly show the distinctness of the self from the body and the like:

children.text: 'sa eṣa neti neti' 'akāyamavraṇamasnāviraṃ śuddhamapāpaviddham' 'yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ / sthāṇumanye' 'na jāyate mriyate vā kadācit' 'jīvāpetaṃ vāvakiledaṃ mriyate' 'na hi vai saśarīrasya sataḥ
children.translated_text: 'That is "not this, not this" (<s>neti neti</s>)'; 'Bodiless, without wound, without sinew, pure, untouched by sin'; 'Some embodied ones enter a womb for embodiment; others [enter] a pillar'; 'It is never born and never dies'; 'This body dies when abandoned by the living [self]'; 'For one who has a body, there is no escape

body.translated_text: (Thus ends the refutation of the inference for the self as maintained by the <s>Kapila</s> [i.e., <s>Sankhya</s>] school.)

body.text: priyāpriyayorapahatirasti / aśarīraṃ vāva santaṃ na priyāpriye spṛśataḥ' ityādyāḥ / kālāntarabhāvisvargādisādhanavidhayaścā'kṣipanti dehādivyatiriktaṃ nityaṃ cetanamiti śrutitadanupapattipramāṇako 'yaṃ pratyagātmeti /
body.translated_text: from the pleasant and the unpleasant. But the pleasant and the unpleasant do not touch one who is bodiless' — and so forth. And the injunctions of means to [attain] heaven and the like, which belong to a future time, also imply a self that is distinct from the body and the like, eternal, and conscious — [this being] established through scripture and the impossibility [of these injunctions] otherwise. This is the inner self (<s>pratyagatman</s>).

body.text: (iti vilakṣaṇātmanaḥ śāstraikapramāṇakatvapakṣanirūpaṇam)

children.text: nanu hitāhitaprāptiparihāramātraparasyā'mnāyasya śirasi kimiti mahānayaṃ bhāraḥ prakṣipyate? anumānāgamādyaśeṣapramāṇamūlabhūtena pratyakṣeṇaiva hyenaṃ pratipadyāmahe / mamedaṃ śarīram, idamahaṃ jānāmīti ghaṭādidṛśyebhya ivāyaṃ draṣṭā dehādapi pṛthagbhūtaḥ pratyakṣaṃ parisphurati /
children.translated_text: Objection: Why is this great burden placed upon the head of scripture, which is concerned solely with the attainment and avoidance of what is beneficial and harmful? For we apprehend this [self] through perception alone, which is the foundation of all other means of valid cognition including inference and scripture. 'This body is mine,' 'I know this' — just as this seer, distinct from visible things like pots and the like, is directly perceived as distinct even from the body.
(Thus the introduction of the position that the self is perceptible.)

children.text: maivaṃ vocaḥ / indriyārthasannikarṣajaṃ hi vijñānaṃ pratyakṣam / na cendriyāṇi rūpādivyatirekiṇi niratiśayasūkṣme pratīci parāgartha iva sannikarṣeṇa jñānaṃ janayitumarhanti / yathā āmnāyate 'parāñciravāni vyatṛṇat svayaṃbhūḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: Do not say so. For the cognition born from the contact of a sense organ with its object is perception. And the sense organs, which are directed outward (<s>paragarthah</s>) toward objects such as color and the like, are not capable of generating knowledge through contact with the inner [self], which is extremely subtle and distinct [from all sensory objects] — just as [they are incapable] regarding an outward object [that is beyond their range]. As it is stated in scripture: 'The self-born one pierced the openings [of the senses] outward.'
He establishes the very incapacity [of perception regarding the self] with
'kim'

children.text: mityādinā sārdhaślokena / kiṃ nīlādirviṣayo 'svayaṃprakāśatvātsvavyavahārāya prakāśaṃ-svaprakāśakaṃ jñānamākāṅkṣate, utāho tadabhedataḥ-saṃvidabhinnatvāt prakāśamanurudhyate iti saṃdehānnīlatadviyorabhedo 'śakyanirṇaya ityarthaḥ / saṃvidanurodhitvaṃ nīlādeḥ saṃvidā sahaivopalabhyamānatvalakṣaṇam / idaṃ ca kiṃ saṃvidabhedaprayuktamuta svaprakāśe nīlāderjaḍasya svaprakāśasaṃvidapekṣāprayuktamiti viśaye yāvadabhedaprayuktatvanirṇayo na bhavati, na tāvadasyābhedasādhakatvam / abhedaprayuktatvanirṇāyakaṃ ca nāsti / tathā cāprayojakatvamiti bhāvaḥ / syādvāsahopalambhaniyamo bodhyayorevābhedasādhakaḥ, na tu buddhibodhyayorbuddhiboddhrorvetyāha
children.translated_text: and so forth, in a verse and a half. Is the object such as blue and the like — because it is not self-luminous — in need of a cognition that illuminates it, i.e., a self-luminous cognition, for its own conventional usage? Or does it conform to illumination because of its non-difference from awareness? Because of this doubt, the non-difference of blue and awareness cannot be determined. This is the meaning. The 'conformity to awareness' of blue and the like means being apprehended only together with awareness. And this [co-apprehension] — is it caused by non-difference from awareness, or caused by the dependence of the inert blue and the like on self-luminous awareness for their self-luminosity? Until the determination that it is caused by non-difference occurs, it does not serve to prove non-difference. And there is nothing that determines it to be caused by non-difference. And thus [the argument from co-perception] is inconclusive. This is the purport. Or perhaps the rule of co-perception (<s>sahopalambhaniyama</s>) proves the non-difference only of knowables, not of cognition and knowable, nor of cognition and knower — thus he says
'bodhyastha'

children.text: iti / buddhīnāṃ boddhṝṇāṃ vā sahopalabhyamānānāṃ nābhedaḥ / buddhasya baddhatvāpātāt / nāpi buddhibodhyayorbuddhiddhrorvā, buddherjaḍatvādiprasaṅgāt satyamithyārthayoraikyaprasaṅgācca / kintu bodhyayoreva tathābhūtayorabheda iṣyatāṃ guṇaguṇiprabhṛtyoḥ kathañcidityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: ('residing in the knowable'). There is no non-difference of cognitions that are co-perceived, or of knowers — because there would follow the consequence of the enlightened one being bound. Nor of cognition and knowable, or of cognition and knower — because there would follow the consequence of cognition being inert, and the consequence of the unity of the true and the false [objects]. Rather, let non-difference be accepted only of knowables that are so [i.e., co-perceived], like quality and qualified, in some manner. This is the meaning.
'buddhiboddhrga-'

children.text: iti tu prakṛtābhiprāyeṇa / yadvā bodhyayoreva sahopalambhaniyamaḥ saṃbhavati / na punarbuddhiboddhadhroḥ / buddhimantarāpi boddhuḥ prakāśāt svāpādāvityarthaḥ //15//16//
children.translated_text: is stated with the intention of the present context. Or alternatively, the rule of co-perception applies only to knowables. Not to cognition and knower. Because the knower shines even without cognition, as in deep sleep and the like. This is the meaning.

body.translated_text: (Thus ends the examination of the position that scripture alone is the means of knowing the distinct self.)

body.text: jñānajñātrorabhedasādhane pratyakṣabādhitatvamapyāha

children.translated_text: 'spastasca' ('and clear').

children.text: ti / ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmīti hi sphuṭo jñeyajñātṛjñānānāṃ bhedapratibhāsaḥ / tadvādha ityarthaḥ / śaṅkate
children.translated_text: For in 'I know the pot,' the appearance of the difference of the knowable, the knower, and knowledge is vivid. That is the contradiction. This is the meaning. He raises the objection:
'na ca' ('but not').

children.text: ti / pratyakṣajñānaviṣayatvaṃ, jñānaviṣayatvaṃ vā pratiyoginaḥ tadbhedapratyakṣe kāraṇatvenāpekṣitam / prakṛte saṃvido jñānāntarāgocaratvena svayaṃprakāśatvāttadbhedapratyakṣaṃ jñātari na saṃbhavatīti śaṅkiturāśayaḥ / parihati
children.translated_text: Being an object of perceptual knowledge, or being an object of knowledge [in general], is required as a cause in the perception of its difference from the counter-correlate. In the present case, since awareness is not within the range of another knowledge, being self-luminous, the perception of its difference from the knower is not possible — this is the intent of the objector. He replies:
'siddhimatrena' ('through mere establishment').

children.text:
ti / pratiyoginaḥ saṃvidaḥ siddhimātreṇa-prakāśamātreṇa, tadupapattau-saṃvidbhedapratyakṣopapattau, aprayojakatvena-pratyakṣadijñānāntarādhīnatatprakāśasya bhedapratyakṣe 'hetutvena, tadviśeṣa
sya-prakāśaviśeṣasya pratyakṣādijñānāntarādhīnasya anākṣepāt-ākṣepāyogādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the mere establishment, i.e., mere illumination, of the counter-correlate, namely awareness — when the perception of the difference of awareness is justified — being inconclusive, i.e., not being a reason in the perception of difference, the specific [feature of] illumination dependent on perception and the like, i.e., another knowledge, is not entailed. This is the meaning.
The purport is this:

children.text: anyonyābhāvapratyakṣe 'dhikaraṇasya pratyakṣamevāpekṣitam, pratiyoginaḥ prakāśamātraṃ ca / natu pratiyoginaḥ pratyakṣam / stambhe piśācabhedasyāpratyakṣatvāpatteḥ / pratiyoginaḥ prakṛte vedanasya prakāśastu svata evāsti / tata eva veditari tadbhedapratyakṣe nānupapattiriti / vastutastattadasādhāraṇākāra eva itaratādātmyadhīvirodhitvena tasya tasyetarasmādbhedarūpaḥ / sa ca pratiyogyanavabhāse 'pi bhāsata evotyāha
children.translated_text: In the perception of mutual absence, what is required is only the perception of the locus and the mere illumination of the counter-correlate. Not the perception of the counter-correlate [through another cognition]. Because there would follow the consequence of the non-perceptibility of the difference of a ghost from a pillar. And the illumination of awareness, which is the counter-correlate in the present case, exists by itself. Therefore, there is no difficulty in the perception of its difference from the knower. In reality, the very specific form [of each entity] — not shared [with the other] — is of the nature of the difference of each from the other, precisely through being contradictory to the cognition of the identity of that with the other. And that [specific form] shines even without the counter-correlate appearing — thus he says
'anavabhasamana' ('not appearing').

children.text: iti / tathā ca jñāturahantvena bhānameva saṃvidbhedagrahaṇamiti bhāvaḥ / tadbhinnatvavyavahāre punaḥ pratiyogiparāmarśasahakṛtamasādhāraṇākārajñānaṃ heturiti bodhyam /
children.translated_text: And thus, the very shining of the knower as 'I' is the apprehension of the difference from awareness. This is the purport. But in the convention of being different from that, the knowledge of the specific form [of the knower], assisted by the recollection of the counter-correlate, is the cause — this should be understood.
'sarvaloke' ('in the entire world')

children.text: ti / etena bhedasya pratyakṣaṃ na saṃbhavati / kṣaṇikasya pratyakṣasya pratiyogigrahaṇapūrvakabhedagrahaṇaparyantamanavasthānāt / yugapatpratiyogyabhāvādhikaraṇagrahe tu samūhālambanavadupaśleṣaviśeṣāsiddhiprasaṅgāt / ato bhramarūpa eva bhedagraha ityapāstam / tattadasādhāraṇa dharmasyaivetarabhedarūpatvāttasya ca dharmiṇi prathamakṣaṇa eva gṛhīteḥ / ata evāpūrvavastudarśane vilakṣaṇo 'yaṃ kaścana padārtha iti bhedapratītirlokasammatā svānubhavasiddhā ca nāpahnavārhā iti
children.translated_text: By this [the following objection is refuted]: 'The perception of difference is not possible. Because momentary perception cannot sustain [the process] from the apprehension of the counter-correlate to the apprehension of difference. And in the simultaneous apprehension of both the absence and the locus [of the counter-correlate], there would follow the consequence, as in aggregate-apprehension, of the non-establishment of the specific connection.' Therefore, the apprehension of difference is merely of the nature of error — [this objection] is set aside. Because the very specific property — not shared [with others] — of each [entity] is of the nature of difference from the other, and because that [property] is apprehended in the very first moment in the property-bearer. For this very reason, upon seeing a novel object, the cognition 'this is some distinct thing' — this awareness of difference, which is accepted by the entire world and established in one's own experience — should not be denied.
'The witness of the entire world'
is what was said. He raises the objection:
'nanu jivata' ('but as long as [one] lives')

children.text: iti / śirasi padanidhānena-tiraskaraṇena / pratibandhagrahaṇaṃ-vyāptigrahaṇam / tataḥ-bhedapratyakṣataḥ / tadvādhasambhavaḥ-abhedānumānabādhasaṃbhavaḥ / tathāsati-pratyakṣasyānumānabādhakatve / apodyeta-bādhyeta /
children.translated_text: By placing [the head] upon the head — by concealing. 'Apprehension of the invariable connection' — apprehension of the pervasion. 'From that' — from the perception of difference. 'The possibility of sublating that' — the possibility of sublating the inference of non-difference. 'In that case' — if perception sublates inference.
The purport is:

children.text: bhinnatvena gṛhyamāṇayoreva hi sahopalambhaniyamo 'bhedavyāpyatvena gṛhītaḥ / tena cābhedānumāne pratyakṣe bhedagrahaṇāṃśobhramalakṣaṇa iti niścīyate / na copajīvyavirodhaḥ / pratyakṣasiddhavastusvarūpasya vyāptigrahopayogino 'bhyupagamāt / bhedasya ca vyāptigrahānupayuktatvāditi / pariharati
children.translated_text: The rule of co-perception is grasped as pervaded by non-difference only of [things] that are apprehended as different. By that [inference of non-difference], in the perception of difference that forms a component of the inference of non-difference, the error-character [of that perception of difference] is ascertained. And there is no contradiction with what is relied upon — because the acceptance of the real nature of the thing established by perception is for the purpose of grasping the pervasion. And because the difference is not useful for the pervasion-apprehension. He replies:
'avisesajna' ('one who does not know the distinction')
— the meaning is: you do not know the dissimilarity between the example and the exemplified. He justifies that very [dissimilarity], with
'tatra'

children.text: ti / na pratyakṣatvamanumānatvaṃ vā bādhyatve bādhakatve vā prayojakam / kintu doṣamūlatvamadoṣamūlatvaṃ caiva tathā / tathā ca yathā jvālābhedānumānamadośamūlaṃ bādhakam, jvālaikyapratyakṣaṃ tu sādṛśyadoṣamūlaṃ bādhyaṃ bhavati; naivaṃ prakṛte jñātṛjñeyajñānabhedagrahasya doṣamūlatvamiti samuditāśayaḥ / jvālaikyapratyakṣe kḷptakāraṇadoṣānuvṛttimupapādayati
children.translated_text: ('there'). It is not perceptual-ness or inferential-ness that is the cause of being sublated or being the sublator. Rather, it is being rooted in a defect or being free from a defect that is so. Accordingly, just as the inference of the difference of flames is free from defect and is the sublator, while the perception of the unity of flames is rooted in the defect of similarity and is sublated — it is not like this in the present case: the apprehension of the difference of knower, known, and knowledge is not rooted in a defect. This is the collective purport. He justifies the continuity of the known causal defect in the perception of flame-unity, with
'tathāhi'

children.text:
tyādinā / acirapraśamitatvapunaruddīpitatvoktyā jvālayorvāstavabhedo jñāpyate / tadadarśanamekavartivṛttitvajñānaṃ caikyabhrame tayorheturityuktaṃ bhavati / nirvāpaṇapunaruddīpanadraṣṭuśca jvālayorbhedaprtyakṣaṃ vartata iti tena bādhitatvamapi nirvāpaṇādyadraṣṭṛniṣṭha jvālayokyapratyakṣe viva
kṣitam / niruktaṃ bhramahetumanirvāpitasthalepyupapādayati
children.translated_text: and so forth. By the statement that [the flame was] recently extinguished and re-lit, the real difference of the flames is indicated. And the non-observation of that [difference] — namely the knowledge that [the flame] subsists in a single wick — is stated to be the cause of the error of unity. And since for one who observes the extinguishing and re-lighting, there is direct perception of the difference of flames, the fact of being sublated by that [perception] is also intended regarding the perception of flame-unity for one who has not observed the extinguishing and the like. He justifies the stated cause of error even in the case where [the flame] has not been extinguished, with
'ataḥ'

children.text: iti / tailavartyavayavāgnisaṃyogasya dīpahetoranyānyatayā jvālābhedo 'ṅgīkāryo 'nirvāpaṇasthale 'pi / kāraṇadhārānuvṛttibalācca kāryadhārānuvṛttiḥ / pūrvapūrvajvālāyāstu kāraṇanivṛttyā nivṛttireva / taddheturhi tailavartyavayaviśeṣāgnisaṃyogaḥ / agnerāśrayāśitvādvartyavayavaviśeṣanāśe tadagnisaṃyogasya nāśo hyāvaśyakaḥ / evaṃ pūrvottaradīpajvālayorbhede siddhe sajātīyadīpadhārāyāṃ bhedāgrahātsādṛśyarūpadoṣadarśanāccaikyabhrama iti bhāvaḥ / nānābhūte aikyabhramaṃ pratyakṣarūpamudāhṛtyaikasminnānātvabhramamapi pratyakṣarūpamudāharati
children.translated_text: ('therefore'). Because the cause of a lamp — namely the conjunction of fire with a particular portion of the oil-wick — varies from moment to moment, the difference of flames must be accepted even where [the flame] has not been extinguished. And from the continuity of the causal stream, there is the continuity of the effect-stream. But the cessation of each preceding flame is from the cessation of its cause. For its cause is the conjunction of fire with a particular portion of the oil-wick. Since fire depends on its substrate, upon the destruction of the specific wick-portion, the destruction of the fire's conjunction with it is inevitable. Thus, when the difference of the earlier and later lamp-flames is established, the error of unity in the homogeneous stream of flames arises from the non-apprehension of difference and from the observation of the defect that is similarity — this is the sense. Having cited the error of unity regarding what is actually manifold as an example of a perceptual [error], he also cites the error of plurality regarding what is actually one as a perceptual [error], with
'tathā eke'

children.text: ti / svābhāvikacākṣuṣaraśmiprasaraṇasya viparyayo dvaitībhāvo 'ṅgulyavaṣṭambhādiprayuktaścandradvitvabhrame doṣaḥ / asya ca nirdeṣapuruṣīyacandraikyapratyakṣabādhitatvaṃ
children.translated_text: ('likewise some'). The defect in the error of seeing two moons is the bifurcation — the reversal of the natural spreading of the visual ray — caused by the pressing of the finger and the like. And that this [error] is sublated by the perception of the moon's unity by a person without the defect
'at the same time'
is stated with this and so forth. He justifies the dissimilarity from the example in the exemplified, with
'na caivam'

children.text: iti / jñātṛjñānajñeyabhedanirūpitalaukikaviṣayitāśālī ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmīti sākṣātkāraḥ doṣamūlaḥ, abhedapratyakṣabādhito vā naiva dṛśyate / tadabhedānumānabādhakatvaṃ susthitamiti bhāvaḥ / viparītaṃ kasmānna bhavatītyatrāha
children.translated_text: ('but not so [here]'). The direct perception 'I know the pot' — which is endowed with worldly objecthood determined by the difference of knower, knowledge, and known — is never observed to be rooted in a defect or to be sublated by a perception of non-difference. The sublation by the inference of non-difference is well-established [as untenable] — this is the sense. He says why the reverse [i.e., the inference of non-difference sublating the perception of difference] does not hold:
'na copalabdhī'
('nor is the apprehension'). 'Such-ness' — the non-difference of the knower and the known from knowledge. He recalls the previously stated purposelessness, with
'vipakṣa'

children.text: iti / vipakṣe bādhakatarkavirahādvyāptyasiddhyāsiddhamabhedānumānaṃ na jñānajñātṛjñeyabhedapratyakṣe bādhakatvena śakyaśaṅkamiti bhāvaḥ / jñānādibhedagraha indriyavṛttiprasṛtibhedarūpadoṣamūlo bhavedityatrāha
children.translated_text: ('in the counter-positive'). Because of the absence of a supporting argument (<s>bādhakatarka</s>) in the counter-positive, the inference of non-difference — being unestablished due to unestablished pervasion — is not capable of even being suspected as a sublator of the perception of the difference of knowledge, knower, and known. This is the sense. He addresses [the objection that] the apprehension of the difference of knowledge and the like is rooted in the defect of the different operation of the sense faculties, with
'anaindriyikatvena'

children.text: ti / bāhyendriyāgrāhyatvena jñānajñātrostadbhedagrahasya nendriyavṛttibhedaprayuktatvaṃ saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ / atra bādhakapratyayo 'pi nāsti candradvitvabhrama ivetyāha
children.translated_text: ('because of not being sensory'). The meaning is: because the knowledge and the knower are not graspable by the external senses, the apprehension of their difference cannot be caused by a difference in the operation of the sense faculties. He also says that there is no sublating cognition here, as there is in the error of two moons:
'yogyānupalambhe'

children.text: ti / na caivamihe ti vākyābhipretamanena vākyadvayena vivṛtam /
children.translated_text: ('in the non-apprehension of what is fit [to be perceived]'). The two sentences elaborate the intended meaning of the sentence 'na caivam iha.'
'saṃvidadhīne'
— the [following] sentence elaborates what was stated in the [previous] sentence, with
'api ca'

children.text: ti / tathāniyamaḥ-saṃvidā sahopalambhaniyamaḥ / avarjanīyaḥ-abhedasyānupagame 'pi durvāraḥ / nanu saṃvidamantarāpi viṣayādiḥ sidhyatvityatrāha
children.translated_text: ('moreover'). 'Such an invariable rule' — the invariable rule of co-perception with awareness. 'Unavoidable' — irresistible even if non-difference is not accepted. [Objection:] But let the object and the like be established even without awareness — to this he says:
'na ca bhedo 'pi'

children.text:
ti / bhedaḥ-grāhyagrāhakabhedaḥ / siddhiṃ-jñānam / apasiddhāntaścaivaṃ kathana iti bhāvaḥ / yadvā sahopalambhaniyamasyābhedasādhakatve
svavyāghātamapyāha
children.translated_text: ('nor is even difference'). 'Difference' — the difference of apprehended and apprehender. 'Establishment' — knowledge. And such a statement is a deviation from one's own doctrine — this is the sense. Or alternatively, he also states the self-contradiction when the invariable rule of co-perception is [used as] a proof of non-difference:
'na ca bhedopi'

children.text: ti / bhedapratibhāso 'pi saṃvidaiva vācya iti niruktahetorbhedasyāpi saṃvidabhede bhedaghaṭito heturapi na sidhyediti yāvat / yadvā bhavadabhimataḥ saṃvidāṃ bhedopi na sidhyediti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: ('nor even difference'). Because even the appearance of difference must be said to belong to awareness alone, if the stated reason [proves] the non-difference of everything from awareness, then even the reason constituted by difference would not be established — this is the meaning. Or alternatively: even the difference of awarenesses accepted by you would not be established — this is the sense.

body.translated_text: He also states the perceptual contradiction in proving the non-difference of knowledge and the knower with

body.text: evaṃ prakaṭasaugatābhimataṃ saṃvidabhedasādhakaṃ sahopalambhaniyamaṃ pradūṣya pracchannasaugatābhimataṃ prakāśasvabhāvatvamapi dūṣayati

children.translated_text: 'aprakāśe'

children.text:
ti / aprakāśātmanaḥ-aprakāśasvabhāvasya jñānabhinnasya ca / anena jñeyasya jñānābhedānumāne pratyakṣabādho, hetoḥ pakṣe 'siddhiśca prādarśiṣātām /
yadyapi jaḍatvānna prakāśasvabhāvatvaṃ jñeyasya, athāpi svayaṃprakāśajñānasaṃbandhātkādācitkaprakāśo ghaṭate ghaṭāderiti bhāvaḥ / jñātā jñānābhinnaḥ prakāśasvabhāvatvādityatra tu heturupagamyate, na sādhyamityāha
children.translated_text: ('in what is non-luminous'). 'Of non-luminous nature' — of a nature that is non-luminous and different from knowledge. By this, both the perceptual contradiction in the inference of non-difference of the known from knowledge, and the unestablishedness of the reason in the subject, have been indicated. Although the known does not have luminosity as its essential nature because of its inert nature, nevertheless occasional luminosity is possible for a pot and the like through the connection with self-luminous knowledge — this is the sense. As for [the argument] 'The knower is non-different from knowledge because of having luminosity as its essential nature' — there the reason is accepted, not the provable — he says:
'na ca tāvata'

children.text: ti / jñānatvaṃ- viṣayaprakāśakadhītvam / jñādhātvarthasya hi kartṛdharmatvaṃ jñānasya / ātmanastu dharmitvānna tathātvamiti bhāvaḥ / jñānasvabhāvaṃ tāvadāha
children.translated_text: ('not from that alone'). 'Knowledge-hood' — being a cognition that illuminates objects. For the agent-hood is a property of the root-meaning of 'jñā' (to know) [and belongs to] knowledge. But for the self, because of being the substance (<s>dharmin</s>), it is not so — this is the sense. He states the essential nature of knowledge, with
'paratantram'

children.text: iti / prakārataikasvabhāvatvaṃ, kādācitkatvaṃ, viṣayāvagāhitvaṃ ceti jñānadharmāḥ / avatiṣṭhamānam-anuvartamānaṃ dhārārūpatayā /
children.translated_text: ('dependent'). Having the sole essential nature of being a mode (<s>prakāratā</s>), being occasional, and being immersed in objects — these are the properties of knowledge. 'Continuing' — persisting in the form of a stream.
'Streaming cognition is regarded by us as one knowledge'

children.text: iti pakṣe tu svarūpata evānuvartamānaṃ yāvadviṣayāntarasaṃcāramiti vivekaḥ / ātmasvabhāvamāha
children.translated_text: — in this position, [it means] continuing in its own essential nature until the transfer to another object. This is the distinction. He states the essential nature of the self, with
'ātmā'

children.text: ti / dharmitvaṃ jñātṛtvamahantvena bhānaṃ cātmano dharmāḥ / nanvevaṃ jñānabhinnatve ātmano jñānamiti vyapadeśaḥ kathaṃ ghaṭata ityatrāha
children.translated_text: ('the self'). Being a substance (<s>dharmitva</s>), being a knower (<s>jñātṛtva</s>), and appearing as 'I' — these are the properties of the self. [Objection:] But if the self is different from knowledge, how does the designation 'the self is knowledge' hold? — to this he says:
'yadi'

children.text: ti / ananyat-svam / ātmani jñānaśabdo jñānasādṛśyāt / tacca svādhīnaprakāśatvarūpaṃ svayaṃprakāśatvaṃ svanirūpitaviṣayatāvattvatādātmyobhayasaṃbandhena kiñcidviśiṣṭatvalakṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: ('if'). 'Non-different' — one's own. The word 'knowledge' regarding the self is [used] because of similarity to knowledge. And that [similarity] is self-luminosity — having the nature of self-dependent luminosity — [which is] the form of being qualified by something, through the dual relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and having the character of a <s>viṣayatā</s> (objecthood) delimited by itself. This is the sense.
'tathāpi'

children.text:
ti / jñānaśabdenābhilapyamānamātmasvarūpaṃ jñānatulyameva, na tu jñāptimātratayā mukhyaṃ jñānamityarthaḥ / yadvā jñānāyatanameva mantavyaṃ natu jñaptimātratayeti / mantavyamiti śeṣaḥ / tataśca jñāturātmano jñānābhedānumānaṃ parābhimataṃ prabalapratyakṣabādhitamiti bhāvaḥ /
pratyakṣatarkasiddhamātmano jñātṛtvamāgamato 'pi pratiṣṭhāpayati
children.translated_text:
('nevertheless'). The essential nature of the self, denoted by the word 'knowledge,' is merely similar to knowledge — not knowledge in the primary sense as mere cognition. This is the meaning. Or alternatively: it should be understood as the locus of knowledge — not as mere cognition. 'Should be understood' is the supplement. And therefore, the inference of the non-difference of the knower-self from knowledge — accepted by the opponent — is sublated by strong perception. This is the sense.
He establishes from scripture (<s>āgama</s>) too the knower-hood of the self that has been established through perception and reasoning, with
'ata eva'
('for this very reason').
'atha'
— this sentence pertains to the selfhood of the 'I'-object as the knower.
'yo 'yam'

children.text:
iti aindriyikajñānapracurasyendriyādhiṣṭhāturātmano hṛdayāntaḥsthatvasvaprakāśatvaparam /
indriyādipravṛttyanuguṇasaṅkalpaprayatnavattvarūpādhiṣṭhānalabhyaṃ kartṛtvaṃ, jñātṛtvaṃ ca svayaṃprakāśatvājjñānaśabditasyātmanaḥ pratipādayadvākyam
children.translated_text: — pertains to the self, which is the superintendent of the senses, being predominantly possessed of sensory knowledge, residing within the heart, and being self-luminous. The sentence that teaches the agency — obtainable through the superintendence characterized by possessing volition (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) and effort (<s>prayatna</s>) conforming to the operation of the senses and the like — and the knower-hood of the self, which is designated by the word 'knowledge' because of its self-luminosity, is:
'eṣa hi'
and so forth. The sentence that teaches that the essential nature of the self — which is to be known by those who seek liberation — is qualified by knower-hood, is:
'vijñātāram'

('the knower'). The meaning is: the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) who has the knower — the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) — as his body. The sentence pertaining to the possession of knowledge in liberation:
'na paśyaḥ'

('the seer does not [see]'). 'The seer' — the all-seeing liberated self. The scriptural statement about the absence of knowledge in the state of liberation pertains to the absence of the vision of what is to be rejected. He establishes this with
'na paśya'

children.text: ityādi vyavasthāpayati / duḥkhatāṃ-kutrāpi vastuni pratikūlatvam / bhagavadvibhūtitayā hi sarvasya svānukūlatvena darśanaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Suffering' — unfavorableness toward anything whatsoever. For at that time, everything is seen as favorable to oneself, by virtue of being the glory (<s>vibhūti</s>) of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
'He who is the seer sees all'
— the second half [of the verse] should also be cited here. Of the nature of an elaboration of this [is]:
'sa uttamaḥ'
('he is the highest') and so forth.
'sa tatra paryeti'
('he moves about there') and so forth,
'not recollecting birth'

— up to this [should be cited] here. Pertaining to the non-cessation of the attributive knowledge (<s>dharmabhūtajñāna</s>) that defines the essential nature [of the self] even upon the cessation of the sixteen parts [of the person] in liberation:
'evam eva'
('just so'). And pertaining to the distinctness of the self — by virtue of possessing knowledge — from body, senses, mind, vital breath, and cognition:
'tasmāt'

children.text:
tīti vivekaḥ /
evaṃ jñātṛtvamātmano vyavasthāpya paramātmano 'pi tadvyavasthāpayati
children.translated_text:
('therefore') — this is the distinction.
Having thus established the knower-hood of the [individual] self, he also establishes that of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), with
'satyam'

children.text: iti / tadvadvacanaḥ-jñānavadvācī / tadvacanatve-jñānavācitve / jñānavācī bhāvalyuḍanto jñānaśabdo litsvareṇādyudātto bhavet / ayaṃ tu antodāttaḥ / tadacpratyayānto 'yaṃ jñātṛvācī svīkārya iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: ('truly'). 'One whose words are such' — one whose words denote possession of knowledge. 'In its denoting knowledge' — in its being a word denoting knowledge. A word denoting knowledge, formed with the <s>bhāvalyuṭ</s> suffix, would have initial accent (<s>ādyudātta</s>) by the accent-rule for <s>lit</s>. But this [word] has final accent. Therefore, this [word], formed with the <s>ac</s>-suffix, should be accepted as denoting the knower — this is the sense.
'In the Aitareya'

children.text: ti / prakaraṇabalāt prajñānaśabdaḥ prajñānavatpara iti bhāvaḥ / prājñena-prajña eva prājñaḥ / svārthe 'ṇ / tena / sarvajñena paramātmanetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: — by the force of the context, the word <s>prajñāna</s> means 'one who possesses <s>prajñāna</s> (supreme knowledge)' — this is the sense. '<s>Prājña</s>' — <s>prajña</s> itself is <s>prājña</s>. The <s>aṇ</s>-suffix is in its own sense. By that [<s>prājña</s>] — meaning by the omniscient Supreme Self — this is the meaning.
'Other than body, senses, mind, vital breath, and cognition'
— he concludes the determination of the essential nature of the self that was proposed:
'tatsiddham'
('that is established').

body.translated_text: Having thus refuted the invariable rule of co-perception — which proves the non-difference of awareness — as accepted by the overt Buddhists (<s>Yogācāras</s>), he also refutes the [reason of] having luminosity as essential nature, accepted by the covert Buddhists (<s>Māyāvādins</s>/Advaitins), with

body.text: atha

children.translated_text: 'self-established' (<s>ananyasādhana</s>)
— to justify the self-luminosity (<s>svayaṃprakāśatva</s>) of the self that was proposed, he commences the examination of the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇaparīkṣā</s>),
'kiṃ punaḥ'
('what then') and so forth.
'Inference'

children.text: iti / yadyapyahaṃ jānāmīti pratyakṣameva tatra pramāṇaṃ sambhavati / tasya dehādiviṣayatvāyogāt / athāpi vilakṣaṇātmaviṣayatvaṃ pratyakṣasyedaṃ pramāṇamatraivaṃ pravartitumarhatītyevaṃ sāmagrīnirūpaṇādyātmakena tarkeṇaiva vyavasthāpyamityāśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: — although the perception 'I know' is indeed the valid means of knowledge there, since [the perception] cannot have the body and the like as its object, nevertheless the [fact] that this perception is capable of operating in this way — having as its object a self distinct [from the body] — is to be established precisely through reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) that consists in the determination of the causal complex and the like. This is the purport.
'yad āha'

children.text:
ti / icchādi vilakṣaṇātmano 'numāpakaṃ yadāha, ato 'numānameva pramāṇaṃ tatretyakṣapādāśayo vijñāyata ityāśayaḥ /
codayati
children.translated_text: ('what he stated'). The purport is: since what he [<s>Gautama</s>] stated is an inferential proof for the self that is distinct from desire and the like, it is understood that <s>Akṣapāda</s>'s [<s>Gautama</s>'s] view is that inference alone is the means of valid knowledge there. He raises an objection:
'kim amīṣām'
('what is [the relation] of these?'). '<s>Dhūmadhvaja</s>' — fire.
The purport is this:

children.text: vyāptigrahasya sahacāradarśanamūlakatvena vilakṣaṇātmanā sahacāradarśane icchādīnāṃ pratyakṣeṇaiva tasya siddheḥ kṛtamanumānena / sahacārādarśane ca kathaṃ tena vyāptirgṛhyeta / agṛhītavyāptikena cecchādinā kathantarāṃ tadanumānamiti / pariharati
children.translated_text: Since the grasp of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is rooted in the observation of co-occurrence, and since in the observation of co-occurrence with the self that is distinct [from the body], desire and the like are established through perception itself — inference is superfluous. And when co-occurrence is not observed, how can pervasion be grasped through that [inference]? And if desire and the like, whose pervasion has not been grasped, [are used as reasons] — how can there be inference of that [self] by another route? He resolves [the objection], with
'mābhūt'

children.text: dityādinā / siṣādhayiṣita- sādhyaviśeṣeṇecchādiviśeṣasya sahacāragraho māstu / āśrayitvaguṇatvābhyāṃ sahacāradarśanādevātmānumānaṃ pravartate / etacca sāmānyato dṛṣṭamiti bhāvaḥ / etadevopapādayati
children.translated_text: ('let it not be') and so forth. Let there be no grasp of co-occurrence of the specific [quality such as] desire and the like with the specific provable [i.e., the self]. The inference of the self operates from the very observation of co-occurrence through [the properties of] being a substrate (<s>āśrayitva</s>) and being a quality (<s>guṇatva</s>). And this is a 'generally perceived' inference (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>) — this is the sense. He justifies this very [point], with
'tathāhi'

children.text: ti / kāryatvam-utpattimattvam / anityatvaṃ-vināśitvam / guṇatvaṃ-guṇatvajātimattvam, viśeṣaṇataikasvabhāvatvaṃ vā / etāni vyāpyānyāśritatvasya / icchādaya āśritāguṇatvādrūpavadityanumānamatra vivakṣitam / atra hetuṃ sādhayati
children.translated_text: ('for thus'). 'Being an effect' (<s>kāryatva</s>) — possessing origination. 'Non-eternality' — being destructible. 'Quality-hood' (<s>guṇatva</s>) — possessing the universal of quality-hood, or having the sole essential nature of being a qualifier. These are [properties] pervaded by being-a-substrate (<s>āśritatva</s>). The inference intended here is: desire and the like have a substrate, because of being qualities — like form and the like. He establishes the reason here, with
'guṇatvaṃ ca'

children.text: ti / padārthatvena dravyādyanyatamatve prāpte dravyādibhedakānumānato dravyatvādivyudāse dravyādibhedaviśiṣṭaṃ padārthatvameva pariśiṣyamāṇaṃ guṇatvaṃ vyavasthāpayatītyarthaḥ / itarabhedānumānānyāha
children.translated_text: ('and quality-hood'). When, being a category (<s>padārtha</s>), the status of being one of substance, quality, etc., is possible, [and when] through inferences that distinguish substance and the like, substance-hood and the like are eliminated — the quality-hood that remains as category-hood qualified by distinction from substance and the like is what is established. This is the meaning. He states the inferences that distinguish the other [categories]:
'na sāmānye'

children.text: ti / abhāvabhedasādhane 'nityatvamutpattivināśavattvarūpaṃ vācyam / nātaḥ prāgabhāve pradhvaṃse vā vyabhicāraḥ /
children.translated_text: ('not in the universal'). In the proof of the distinction from non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), non-eternality — in the form of possessing origination and destruction — is to be stated. Therefore, there is no deviation in prior non-existence or in destruction.
'vyāpake'

children.text: ti / vibhusamavetatvādityarthaḥ / naiyāyikamatenāyaṃ hetuḥ siddhaḥ / na karma, saṃyogavibhāgayoranapekṣakāraṇatvābhāvāt, na dravyaṃ asaṃyogitvāditi vā heturvācyaḥ / guṇatvaṃ prasādhya viśeṣaguṇatvaṃ prasādhayati
children.translated_text: ('in the pervader'). The meaning is: because of inhering in what is all-pervading. This reason is established according to the <s>Naiyāyika</s> doctrine. 'Not an action, because of the absence of independent causality with respect to conjunction and disjunction' — or: 'not a substance, because of not being a conjunct' — these are alternative reasons to be stated. Having established quality-hood, he establishes specific-quality-hood:
'viśeṣe'

children.text:
ti/ rūpatvādau vyabhi
cārasya vāraṇāyānityatve satīti / saṃyogādau tadvāraṇāya viśeṣyadalam / evamapi prabhāyāṃ vyabhicāraḥ syāt, cakṣurmātragrāhyatvāttasyāḥ / ato guṇatve satīti vācyam / evamapi prabhābhittisaṃyoge tatprasaṅgaḥ / ata ekondriyamātragrāhyajātimattvaṃ viśeṣyaṃ vaktavyam / evaṃ cānityatvaviśeṣaṇasya vaiyarthyam / guṇatvadalasyāpi / prabhātvajātau mānābhāvāt, tejastvādeśca dvīndriyagrāhyatvāt / parantu prabhātvajāteḥ prāmāṇikatve vāyoḥ spārśanopagame vā guṇatvadalamāvaśyakameveti bodhyam / yogināṃ manasāpi rūpādergrahādasmadādīti viśeṣaṇam ayogyabhiprāyam / sāmānyato- dṛṣṭānumānasyāśrayaviśeṣaparyavasānasiddhaye pariśeṣānumānānyāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'When non-eternal' (<s>anityatve sati</s>) — to prevent deviation [of the reason] in color-hood (<s>rūpatva</s>) and the like. 'When being a special quality' (<s>viśeṣya</s>) — to prevent deviation in conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and the like. Even so, there would be deviation in radiance (<s>prabhā</s>), because that [radiance] is apprehensible solely by the eye. Therefore, 'when being a quality' (<s>guṇatve sati</s>) should be stated. Even so, the consequence would arise in the conjunction of radiance with a wall. Therefore, 'possessing a universal apprehensible solely by one sense organ' must be stated as the qualifier. And thus the qualifier 'non-eternal' would be purposeless, as would the qualifier 'being a quality.' Because there is no means of valid knowledge for the universal 'radiance-hood,' and because 'substance-of-light-hood' and the like are apprehensible by two sense organs. However, if the universal 'radiance-hood' is authoritative, or if wind is accepted as [apprehensible] by touch alone, then the qualifier 'being a quality' is indeed necessary — this should be understood. Because of the apprehension of color and the like even by the mind for <s>yogins</s> (meditators), the qualifier 'for us ordinary [people]' and the like is intended [as specifying the non-yogic context]. For the <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (general inference) to terminate in a specific substrate, he states elimination inferences with
'thus' (<s>evam</s>)

children.text: iti / pratyācakṣāṇaiḥ-pratikṣipadbhiḥ / sāmānyatodṛṣṭamanvayyanumānamevetarabhedānumānasahakṛtaṃ viśeṣānumāpakamityekaḥ pakṣaḥ / sāmānyatodṛṣṭetarabhedānumānato 'gre prasidhyan viśiṣṭahetuḥ kevalavyatirekirūpastatheti cāparaḥ / anena ca vākyenādyaḥ pakṣaḥ sphoryate /
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'By those who refute' (<s>pratyācakṣāṇaiḥ</s>) — by those who reject [other substrates]. One position is: the <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> inference is itself — being a positive (<s>anvaya</s>) inference, when assisted by the inference of difference from other [candidates] — capable of inferring a specific [substrate]. Another position is: a specific reason — which comes to be known subsequently through the inference of difference from other [candidates] as applied to the <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> — has the form of a purely negative (<s>kevalavyatirekin</s>) inference. And by this statement, the first position is made explicit.
'Those qualities of the elements' (<s>ye bhūtaguṇā</s>)
and so forth. Here the word 'suitable' (<s>yogyā</s>) should also be considered. The negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) subsumption and conclusion [are as follows]:
'not so' (<s>na tathā</s>)
and so forth.
'Space and time' (<s>dikkāla</s>)

children.text: ti / icchādayo na dikkālamanoguṇāḥ, viśeṣaguṇatvāt, pratyakṣatvādvā; ye punardigādiguṇāḥ saṅkhyādayaḥ, na te pratyakṣā, viśeṣaguṇā vā /
children.translated_text: and so forth. Desire and the like are not qualities of space, time, or mind — because they are specific qualities (<s>viśeṣaguṇa</s>), or because they are perceptual. But number and the like, which are qualities of space and the like, are neither perceptual [in the relevant way] nor specific qualities.
'In what is not a cause' (<s>akāraṇa</s>)
and so forth. 'To be drawn' (<s>anukraṣṭavyāḥ</s>) — to be attracted, included. He states the general formal argument resulting from the various inferences, with
'therefore' (<s>tena</s>)
and so forth. He also presents an alternative position with
'in the locus of disagreement' (<s>vimatipadā</s>)

children.text:
ti /
vimatipadam-vipratipatteḥ sthānam-nimittaṃ-nānāvādaḥ, tadāspadebhyaḥ- tadviṣayebhya ityarthaḥ / atrāyaṃ prayogaḥ-icchādayaḥ tadāśrayatvena vipratipannaśarīrādivyatiriktaguṇāḥ tadguṇatvabādhakapramāṇaviṣayaguṇatvāditi /
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Locus of disagreement' (<s>vimatipadam</s>) — the ground, i.e., the cause, of the conflicting views — [meaning] the various doctrines; 'from the objects of that' — from the objects of those [doctrines]. This is the meaning. Here the formal argument is: desire and the like, regarding whose substrate there is conflicting opinion, are qualities residing in [a substance] distinct from the body and the like, because they are qualities that are the objects of means of valid knowledge that defeat [their] being qualities of that [body, etc.].
'And the example' (<s>udāharaṇaṃ ca</s>)

children.text: ti / vyatirekītyādiḥ / prasiddhadravyabhinnasyādravyasya prasiddhāvapi tadguṇatvasyāprasiddhyā nānvayyudāharaṇaṃ sambhavati / na caivaṃ sādhyavyatirekasyāpyanumānātpūrvamaprasiddhyā vyatirekyudāharaṇaṃ vā kathaṃ ghaṭata iti vācyam / prasiddhadravyavyatiriktasamavetatvasyaiva sādhyatvāt tadvyatirekasya rūpādau prasiddhisambhavācceti hṛdayam / anvayavyāptirvā sāmānyamukhī sambhavatītyāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. [Starting with] 'purely negative' (<s>vyatirekī</s>) and so forth. Since, even when the existence of a substance different from the well-known substances is established, the [reason's] being a quality of that [substance] is not established — no positive (<s>anvaya</s>) example is possible. Nor should it be said: 'Since the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) of the provable is also not established prior to the inference, how can a purely negative example be appropriate?' — because the provable is precisely 'inhering in [a substance] distinct from the well-known substances,' and the negative concomitance of that is establishable in color and the like. This is the essential point. Or, he says that the positive pervasion (<s>anvayavyāpti</s>) is possible through the general [route], with
'through the general [inference]' (<s>sāmānyato va</s>)

children.text:
ti / vilakṣaṇaśabdāśrayasiddhyupajīvanenedam / tadanumāne ca gandhādyantarbhāveṇa vyāptigrahaṇamiti bhāvaḥ / evaṃ ca kevalavyatirekyanupagame 'pi na kṣatiriti dhyeyam /
naiyāyikābhimatāṃ vilakṣaṇātmasiddhimānumānikīṃ pratikṣipanti śrotriyāḥ
children.translated_text:
and so forth. This relies on the establishment of the substrate through the inference from the different character [of the self]. And in that inference, the apprehension of pervasion is through the inclusion of smell and the like [as instances]. This is the purport. And thus, even without accepting the purely negative [inference], there is no harm — this should be reflected upon.
The scriptural scholars (<s>śrotriya</s>) reject the Naiyāyika inferential proof of a self of distinct character, with
'this too' (<s>idamapi</s>)
and so forth. Even if the substrate in general is established, the specific substrate [viz., the distinct self] would be established by the purely negative [inference] — to this he says:
'in the purely negative [inference]' (<s>kevala</s>)

children.text: ti / sādhanadaśām-anumāpakatvāvasthām, nāsādayati na prāptoti, sapakṣānvayavirahāt-sādhyena sahacāradarśanasthalasambandhābhāvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. '[The purely negative inference] does not attain the state of being a proof' (<s>sādhanadaśām nāsādayati</s>) — does not reach the state of being a prover — because of the absence of positive concomitance with the thesis-similar (<s>sapakṣa</s>), i.e., because of the absence of a connection with a locus where co-occurrence with the provable is observed. This is the meaning.
'Like the uncommon [reason]' (<s>asādhāraṇavat</s>)

children.text:
diti / pakṣamātravṛttihetorasādhāraṇasya
sādhyasahacāragrahavirahādagṛhītavyāptikasya yathā na gamakatvam, evaṃ kevalavyatirekiṇo 'pi vyāptigrahāyogāt na gamakatvamiti bhāvaḥ / nanu sati sapakṣe hetoravṛtterasādhāraṇasya sadoṣatvam / kevalavyatirekiṇi tu sapakṣasyaiva virahānna doṣa iti cet; maivam; kevalavyatirekiṇi sādhyasya prasiddhirasti na vānumānātpūrvam / asti cedyatra prasiddhiḥ tatra hetoḥ sattve 'nvayitvam, asattve tu asādhāraṇatvameva / nāsti cet sādhyavyatirekasyāpyaprasiddheḥ kevalavyatirekitvamapi durghaṭamiti dik / vistarastu nyāyapariśuddhyādāvanusandheyaḥ / śaṅkate na caivam iti / vipakṣavyatirekaḥ-vipakṣāsattvam / sādhāraṇavat-pakṣatrayavṛttihetuvat / sādhāraṇe yathā vipakṣesattvāddhetorasādhakatvam, kevalānvayinyapi vipakṣasyaivāprasiddheḥ tatsattvābhāvasyāpyaprasiddhestathāgamakatvaṃ syādityarthaḥ / anvayavyatirekiṇi ubhayavidhasahacāradarśanādvyāptigrahasya dṛṣṭeḥ sādhyahetvo sahacārādarśanātkevalavyatirekiṇo 'sādhakatvaṃ cedabhimatam, tarhi sādhyābhāvasādhanābhāvayoḥ sahacārādarśanātkevalānvayino 'pyasādhakatvaṃ syāditi cākūtam / pariharati
children.translated_text: and so forth. Just as the uncommon [reason] — which occurs only in the thesis — is not probative because of the absence of apprehension of co-occurrence with the provable, i.e., because its pervasion is not grasped — so too the purely negative [reason], because the apprehension of pervasion is impossible, is not probative. This is the purport. [Objection:] In the case of the uncommon [reason], the fault is that the reason does not occur in the thesis-similar [loci] when they exist. But in the purely negative [reason], since the thesis-similar [loci] themselves are absent, there is no fault. [Reply:] Not so. In the purely negative [reason], is the provable established prior to the inference or not? If it is established, then where it is established, [the reason] — if present — would be a positive [reason]; if absent, it would be uncommon. And if not [established], then since the negative concomitance of the provable is also not established, even the purely-negative character is untenable. This is the direction [of the argument]. The details should be sought in the <s>Nyāyapariśuddhi</s> and the like. He raises a doubt [expressed as] 'nor is it the case' and so forth. 'Negative concomitance with the counter-thesis' (<s>vipakṣavyatireka</s>) — the absence [of the reason] from the counter-thesis. 'Like the common [reason]' (<s>sādhāraṇavat</s>) — like a reason that occurs in all three [classes of loci]. Just as the common [reason] is non-probative because of the reason's presence in the counter-thesis, so too the purely positive (<s>kevalānvayin</s>) — since the counter-thesis itself is not established, the absence of [the reason from] it is also not established — would be non-probative. This is the meaning. If it is maintained that since the co-occurrence of the provable and the reason is observed in the positive-and-negative [inference], the pervasion is grasped — [then] since the co-occurrence of the provable and the reason is not observed in the purely negative [inference], it should be non-probative — and conversely, since the co-occurrence of the absence of the provable and the absence of the reason is not observed in the purely positive [inference], that too should be non-probative. This is the purport. He resolves [this] with
'place, time, and the like' (<s>deśakālādī</s>)

children.text: ti / kasmiṃściddeśe kāle vā hetuḥ sādhyamantarāpi prayojakāntarāt syāditi deśakālaviśeṣāntarbhāveṇa śaṅkitopādheranukūlatarkeṇa nivartane sati sādhyahetvoḥ sahacāradarśanamātrato 'pi anvayavyāptirniścīyata ityarthaḥ / apirbhinnakramaḥ / anvayadarśanenetyanantaraṃyojyaḥ / sādhyānvitasvabhāvatayā-sādhyavyāpyatayā / vyatirekavyāptigraha eva vyatirekasahacāragrahasyāpekṣayā kevalānvayini anvayavyāptigrahasya vyatirekāprasiddhāvapi nānupapattiriti ca bhāvaḥ / vipakṣasattksyaivāprasiddhyaiva rūpapañcakasampattiḥ kevalānvayina iti cāśayaḥ siddhāntinām / nanvevaṃ sādhyasādhanavyatirekayoḥ sahacāradarśanata eva vyatirekavyāptigraha upapadyata iti śaṅkate
children.translated_text: and so forth. The meaning is: somewhere, at some time, the reason might exist even without the provable due to some other productive factor — when the suspected limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), included in the specifics of place, time, etc., is eliminated by a supportive reasoning (<s>anukūlatarka</s>), the positive pervasion (<s>anvayavyāpti</s>) is ascertained even from the mere observation of co-occurrence of the provable and the reason. The word '<s>api</s>' is in a different sequence. It should be connected after 'through the observation of positive [co-occurrence].' 'As having a nature concomitant with the provable' (<s>sādhyānvitasvabhāvatayā</s>) — as being pervaded by the provable. The purport is also: in the apprehension of the negative pervasion alone — compared to the apprehension of the co-occurrence of negative [instances] — in the purely positive [inference], the apprehension of the positive pervasion is not impossible even when the negative concomitance is not established. And the view of the Siddhāntins is that the purely positive [reason] has the five-fold conformity (<s>rūpapañcakasamapatti</s>) precisely through the non-establishment of [the reason's] presence in the counter-thesis. [Objection:] If so, the apprehension of the negative pervasion would be possible from the mere observation of the co-occurrence of the absence of the provable and the absence of the reason — he raises the doubt with
'nor the absence of the proof' (<s>na ca sādhanābhāva</s>)

and so forth. 'Having a nature concomitant with the provable' (<s>sādhyānvitasvabhāvatva</s>) — the reason's possession of negative pervasion as defined by the provable, having the defining characteristic of being the counter-correlate of an absence that pervades the absence of the provable. He states the reason for the impossibility of the ascertainment of pervasion with
'of the absence' (<s>abhāvasya</s>)

children.text:
ti / vyatirekiṇoḥ sādhyasādhanayoradhikaraṇapekṣayā tadabhāvādhikaraṇānāmānantyāt kalayāṃ'śena kkacidapi sādhyābhāvavati hetorvṛttau vyatirekasāhacaryaniyamalakṣaṇavyatirekavyāpterasambhavādityarthaḥ / vyatirekisādhyasādhanavataḥ parimitatvena kvacitkārtsnyena
grahaṇamapi sambhavediti ca hārdam / nanu yāvatsu pratyakṣeṣvadhikaraṇeṣu vyatirekayoḥ sahacāradarśanata eva vyāptirniścīyetetyatrāha
children.translated_text:
and so forth. Because of the infinity of the substrates of the absences of the provable and the reason relative to their positive substrates — even a fractional grasp of the reason's occurrence in [a locus possessing] the absence of the provable [would not suffice for] the invariable co-occurrence of the negative concomitance — the negative pervasion having the defining characteristic of invariable co-occurrence is impossible. This is the meaning. The essential point is also: because the substrates of the positive provable and the reason are limited, comprehensive grasp somewhere is possible.
[Objection:] The pervasion should be ascertained from the observation of co-occurrence of the two negatives in as many perceptual substrates [as are available] — to this he says:
'in doubt' (<s>sandehe</s>)

children.text:
ti / vyatirekavyāptirhi sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvavyāptigarbhitā / sādhyābhāvo 'stu, hetvabhāvo māstviti śaṅkāyāṃ ca na sādhanābhāvavyāpyatvaṃ sādhyābhāve gṛhyetānukūlatarkavirahe / sādhyasyā
sādhananīmittatvasādhananiyatasvabhāvatvādyanyathānupapattilakṣaṇatarkabalācchaṅkānivāraṇaṃ ca sādhyasādhanayoḥ sahacāradarśanamūlahetuhetumadbhāvādyavadhāraṇamantarā na ghaṭata iti kevalavyatirekyasiddhiriti ca hārdam / viśiṣṭahetunā pṛthivyādivyatiriktaguṇatvānumāne ca sādhyāprasiddhimāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. The negative pervasion implies the pervasion of the absence of the reason by the absence of the provable. When there is a doubt — 'let there be the absence of the provable, but perhaps the absence of the reason does not hold' — the pervasion of the absence of the provable by the absence of the reason is not grasped in the absence of a supportive reasoning. And the elimination of the doubt through a reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) of the nature of impossibility-of-being-otherwise (<s>anyathānupapatti</s>) — [viz.,] that the provable is not produced by anything other than the reason, that the provable has a nature restricted to the reason, and the like — is not possible without the ascertainment of the cause-effect relation and the like that is based on the observation of co-occurrence of the provable and the reason. This is the essential point: the purely negative [inference] remains unestablished. He states the non-establishment of the provable in the inference of being-a-quality-residing-in-[a-substance]-distinct-from-earth-and-the-like, by means of the specific reason, with
'from earth and the like' (<s>pṛthivyādibhyaḥ</s>)

children.text:
iti / arthāntarasya guṇādeḥ prasiddhāvapi tadvṛttiguṇatvalakṣaṇaṃ sādhyamaprasiddhameva / na ca pṛthivyādyarthāntarasamevatatvameva sādhyate / tacca rūpatvādau prasiddhameveti vācyam / niruktasamavetatvasya guṇakriyābhinna eva prasiddherguṇe jñānādau tatsādhanāyogaḥ / arthāntaradravyasamavetatvaṃ cānumānātprāgaprasiddhameveti hārdam /
naiyāyikoktātmānumānadūṣaṇāni sāṅkhyoktātmānumāneṣvapyatidiśati
children.translated_text:
and so forth. Even if the existence of something else — a quality and the like — is established, the provable — namely being a quality residing in that [distinct substance] — is simply not established. Nor should it be said: 'What is being proved is merely the inhering-in-a-substance-different-from-earth-and-the-like; and that is well-established in color-hood and the like.' Because the stated inherence is established only in quality, action, and the like that are distinct [from substance] — [whereas] establishing it in knowledge and the like, which [for the Naiyāyikas] are themselves qualities, would [require proving] something different. And the inherence in a distinct substance is simply not established prior to inference. This is the essential point.
He extends the refutations of the Naiyāyika inferences for the self to the Sāṃkhya inferences for the self as well, with
'by this' (<s>etena</s>)
and so forth.
'and thus' (<s>tathā ca</s>)

children.text: ti / vilakṣaṇātmasādhakatvena sāṅkhyābhimatāneva hetūn prathamaṃ vivṛṇumahe śiṣyavaiśadyāya kṣepasaukaryāya ceti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. The purport is: we first elaborate the very reasons accepted by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> as proving a self of distinct character — for the sake of the student's clarity and for the ease of refutation.
'Because of the composite being for the sake of another' (<s>saṅghātaparārthatvāt</s>)
— and so forth is a <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s>. He explains it with
'this is the meaning' (<s>ayamartha</s>)

children.text: ityādinā / śaraṇaṃ gṛham / saṅghātatvam-avayavasamudāyātmakatvam / bhūtānāṃ-pañcānāṃ mahābhūtānām /
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Refuge' (<s>śaraṇa</s>) — a house. 'Composite-hood' (<s>saṅghātatva</s>) — being constituted as an aggregate of parts. 'Of the elements' (<s>bhūtānām</s>) — of the five great elements.
'In the unmanifest' (<s>avyakta</s>)

children.text: ti / sukhaduḥkhamohātmatvaṃ sukhādisvarūpatvam, sukhādijanakatvarūpaṃ vā / tena tathātvaṃ-sattvarajastamorūpaguṇatrayasaṅghātātmakatvam anumeyaṃ kāryarūpeṇa śarīrādivadevetyarthaḥ / saṅghātatvahetorviruddhatvaṃ śaṅkate
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion' — either having pleasure and the like as its own nature, or having the form of producing pleasure and the like. 'Its being so' — its being constituted as an aggregate of the three <s>guṇas</s> (<s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, <s>tamas</s>) — is to be inferred in the form of an effect, just like the body and the like. This is the meaning. He raises the doubt that the reason of composite-hood is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) with
'not [so, because] of the sense organs' (<s>na cendriyāṇām</s>)

children.text: iti / ubhayaviśeṣaviruddhatvam-pakṣasādhyayorabhimataviśeṣaviruddhākārāpādakatvam / anāhaṅkārikatvena saṅghātatvasya bhūtabhautikeṣu, saṃhataparārthatvena ca gehaśayyādiṣu bhūyaḥsahacāradṛṣṭervyāptergṛhītatayā pakṣāntargatendriyāṇāmabhimatāhaṅkārikatvaviruddhasyānāhaṅkārikatvasya, sādhyaghaṭakasya ca parasyābhimatāsaṃhatatvaviruddhasya saṃhatatvasyā'pādakatvādviruddhatvaṃ saṅghātatvahetoriti bhāvaḥ / hetorubhayaviśeṣaviruddhatvaṃ ca netyanvayaḥ / aviruddhatvamupapādayati
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Contradictoriness to the specific [features] of both' (<s>ubhayaviśeṣaviruddhatva</s>) — leading to forms contradicting the accepted specific [features] of the thesis and the provable. Because composite-hood — not [being] a product of the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — is observed in close co-occurrence with being for the sake of what is composite in the [case of] the elemental and the physical [objects]; and because [composite-hood] as 'being for the sake of what is composite' is observed in houses, beds, and the like — the pervasion being grasped [there] — therefore, the reason of composite-hood leads to: for the sense organs included in the thesis, the non-<s>āhaṅkārika</s> character that contradicts the accepted <s>āhaṅkārika</s> character; and for the 'other' [i.e., the self] that is a component of the provable, the composite character that contradicts the accepted non-composite character. Hence the reason of composite-hood is contradictory. This is the purport. The syntax is: 'The contradictoriness of the reason to the specific [features] of both is not [a problem]' — this is the positive continuation. He demonstrates the non-contradictoriness with
'in the <s>ahaṅkāra</s>' (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>)

children.text: tyādinā / ahaṅkāravṛttau satyāmevendriyāṇāṃ manaḥparyantānāṃ vṛtterdarśanāttadabhāve ca svāpe 'darśanādāhaṅkārikatvaṃ teṣāmavasīyate / tatrāpi sattvaṅkāryalāghavaprakāśayogātsātvikāhaṅkārakāryatvamiti bhāvaḥ / āgamaśca
children.translated_text: and so forth. Since the activity of the sense organs up to the mind is observed only when the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> functions, and is not observed in deep sleep when it does not [function], the <s>āhaṅkārika</s> character of those [sense organs] is ascertained. Moreover, because of the <s>sāttvika</s> qualities of lightness, capacity for effects, and luminosity, [their] being effects of the <s>sāttvika ahaṅkāra</s> [is established]. This is the purport. And the scripture:
'The gods are from the <s>vaikārika</s> [ahaṅkāra] — ten, and the mind is the eleventh'

children.text: ti smṛtirūpaḥ / devāḥ-indriyāṇi prakāśayogāddevādhiṣṭhitatvādvā / vaikārikasya sāttvikāhaṅkārasyeme kāryabhūtā iti vaikārikāḥ / apavādānupapatteḥ-bādhanānupapatteḥ / saṅghātatvasyānuhaṅkārikatvena na vyāptiḥ / traiguṇyātmakasyendriyajātasyā'haṅkārikatvena pramāṇapratipannatvenānaikāntyāditi bhāvaḥ / pakṣaviśeṣaviruddhatvaṃ parihṛtyasādhyaviśeṣaviruddhatvaṃ pariharati
children.translated_text: — is in the form of a <s>smṛti</s> (traditional text). 'Gods' (<s>devāḥ</s>) — the sense organs, either because of [their] association with luminosity, or because they are presided over by deities. 'Of the <s>vaikārika</s>' — of the <s>sāttvika ahaṅkāra</s>; these are its effects, hence '<s>vaikārika</s>.' 'Because of the impossibility of an exception' (<s>apavādānupapatteḥ</s>) — because sublation is impossible. Composite-hood is not pervaded by non-<s>āhaṅkārika</s> character. Because the class of sense organs — which is constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s> — is established through valid means of knowledge as <s>āhaṅkārika</s>, and hence [the reason is] inconclusive. This is the purport. Having resolved the contradictoriness with respect to the specific [features] of the thesis, he resolves the contradictoriness with respect to the specific [features] of the provable, with
'but of the self' (<s>ātmanastvi</s>)
and so forth.
'and because of non-probativeness' (<s>aprayojakatvācca</s>)

children.text: ti / asaṃhatasyāpyātmanaścetanatvādeva bhoktṛtvasyopapatteḥ bhoktatvalakṣaṇe paratve prādhānye saṅghātatvasyāprayojakatvamiti bhāvaḥ / yadi saṅghātatvasya paratve prayojakatvaṃ syāttarhi saṃhataparārthatvena vyāptiḥ sambhavennāma saṅghātatvasya / vyāptibalādanekasaṅghātakalpanāpi soḍhavyā bhavet / na caivam / tathā ca saṃhataparārthatve saṅghātatvasya vyāpyatvāsiddhatvamiti hārdam / saṅghātaparatvenānumitasyātmanaḥ saṅghātatvaṃ yogyānupalabdhibādhitañceti bodhyam / saṅghātatvasya parārthatvena vyāptistu pramāṇāntaravirodhābhāvātprasetsyatītyāha
children.translated_text: and so forth. Since even the non-composite self has enjoyership (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) simply because of being conscious, composite-hood is non-probative for the 'other-ness' (<s>paratva</s>) that has the defining characteristic of enjoyership. This is the purport. If composite-hood were probative for 'other-ness,' then the pervasion of composite-hood by 'being for the sake of what is composite' would be possible. By the force of pervasion, even the postulation of multiple composites would have to be tolerated. But this is not [the case]. And so, the non-establishment of composite-hood as pervaded by being-for-the-sake-of-what-is-composite is the essential point. And it should be understood that composite-hood for the self inferred through 'being-for-the-sake-of-the-composite' is defeated by the competent non-apprehension (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>). But the pervasion of composite-hood by 'being for the sake of another' will be established because of the absence of contradiction from another means of valid knowledge — he says with
'nor from another means of valid knowledge' (<s>na ca pramāṇāntara</s>)
and so forth. He concludes the non-establishment of the self through the inference from 'being-for-the-sake-of-the-composite,' with
'and thus' (<s>evaṃ ca</s>)

children.text: ti / saṅghātatvavyāpakaparārthatvavatsattvādiguṇatrayatatkāryarahita iti saṃhatatve tyāderarthaḥ / parasya saṃhatatve 'navasthāprasakteḥ traiguṇyaviparyayaḥ atraiguṇyātmakatvarūpo mantavya ityuktam
children.translated_text: The meaning of 'when composite' and the like is: devoid of the triad of qualities such as <s>sattva</s> and their effects, just as being-for-another pervades being-an-aggregate. Since there is the danger of infinite regress if the other too is composite, the contrariety regarding the three <s>gunas</s> should be understood as having a nature that is not of the three <s>gunas</s>. Thus it was said
'non-composite' (<s>asamhata</s>).

children.text:
iti / triguṇādiviparyayādityantaḥ kārikāṃśo vivṛtaḥ /
athādhiṣṭhānādityaṃśaṃ vivṛṇoti
children.translated_text: The portion of the verse up to 'from the contrariety regarding the three <s>gunas</s> and the like' has been elaborated. Now he elaborates the portion beginning with 'controllership' and the like.
'tatha dehAdayah' ('likewise the body and the like')

children.text: iti / sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatayā-sukhādyātmakasattvādisaṅghātarūpatayā / pareṇa-svabhinnena cetanena / adhiṣṭhīyante-kāryānuguṇatayā preryante / yantrādibhiḥ sārathiprabhṛtibhiḥ / bhoktṛbhāvādityetadvivṛṇoti
children.translated_text: Because of being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion — because of having the form of an aggregate of <s>sattva</s> and the like whose nature is pleasure and the like — [the body and the like] are controlled, i.e., directed in accordance with the task, by another — a conscious being distinct from them. By machines and the like, by a charioteer and the like. He elaborates the [reason from] being an enjoyer with
'api cAnukUle' ('moreover, regarding what is favorable')

children.text: ti / anukūlanīyaḥ-anukūlabuddhibhāk / anukūlavedanīyaḥ-anukūlatvaprakārakabuddhiviṣayaḥ / evaṃ pratikūlanīyapratikūlavedanīyāvūhyau / bhrātṛvyaḥ-śatruḥ / bhoktṛbhāvādityasya draṣṭṛtvaparatayā yojanāntaraṃ
children.translated_text: 'Anukulaniya' — one who partakes of favorable cognition. 'Anukulavedaniya' — the object of a cognition having the form of favorableness. Similarly, 'pratikulaniya' and 'pratikulavedaniya' are to be construed. 'Bhratrya' — enemy. Another construal of 'from being an enjoyer,' taking it as referring to seer-hood:
'drsyatvA' ('because of being visible')
thus.
'adhiShThAtu' ('of the controller')

children.text: rityādi / saṅghātapravṛtteradhiṣṭhātrantarādhīnatayādhiṣṭhātuḥ saṅghātatve tatpravṛtterapyadhiṣṭhātrantarādhīnatvaṃ syāt, evamagre 'pītyanavasthāprasaṅgādadhiṣṭhāturasaṅghātatvameṣṭavyam / evaṃ sukhenānukūlanīyasya duḥkhena pratikūlanīyasya vā bhoktuḥ triguṇatve tasyāpi anukūlapratikūlavedanīyatvasya prāpteranukūlanīyapratikūlanīyāntarāpādakatvādanavasthāprasaṅga ityatriguṇatvameṣṭavyam / dehādipakṣakavilakṣaṇadraṣṭranumānena cātmano dehādivailakṣaṇyamapi siddhamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. Since the activity of the aggregate depends on another controller, if the controller too were an aggregate, its activity too would depend on yet another controller, and so on further — because of the danger of infinite regress, the controller must be accepted as non-composite. Similarly, if the enjoyer — who finds [something] favorable through pleasure and unfavorable through pain — were of the three <s>gunas</s>, then because the attainment of being-favorable-and-unfavorable-to-be-experienced would lead to positing yet another [enjoyer] who finds [the first one] favorable or unfavorable, there is the danger of infinite regress — hence non-possession of the three <s>gunas</s> must be accepted. And through the inference of a seer distinct from the class of the body and the like, the distinctness of the self from the body and the like is also established. This is the purport.
'kaivalyArthaM pravRttesce' ('and from the engagement for the sake of absolute isolation')
He elaborates that portion with
'tathA dehAde' ('likewise, from the body and the like').

children.text: riti / atrāyaṃ prayogaḥ-kaivalyasādhanapravṛttiḥ kaivalyadaśāprāptiyogyātmatattvajñānapūrvikā,kaivalyasādhanapravṛttitvāt, yā yā phalaviśeṣasādhanaprekṣāvatpravṛttiḥ sā sā tattatphalaprāptiyogyātmatattvajñānapūrvikā, yathā svargasādhanapravṛttiriti / dehādeḥ pradhānaparyantasya pariṇāmasvabhāvasya triguṇasya kaivalyānupapattijñānācca vilakṣaṇātmasiddhiriti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: Here the formal argument is: the engagement in the means to <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation) possesses the reality of a self fit for attaining the state of <s>kaivalya</s>,

body.translated_text: Now,
