body.text: vilakṣaṇātmasādhakatayā sāṅkhyairupakṣiptaṃ saṅghātaparārthatvānumānaṃ tāvaddūṣayati

children.translated_text: 'atrApi' ('here too')
and so forth.
'parApare' ('successive')

children.text: ti / anyānyetyarthaḥ / pūrvāparībhūteti vā / parāparasaṅghāteti vā samastapāṭhaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: means 'one after another.' Or 'having become prior and subsequent.' Or 'the successive aggregate' may be a compound reading.
'kAryatayaiva' ('through being an effect alone')

children.text: ti / kāryātkāraṇamanumeyam / kāraṇasyāpi kādācitkatvena kāryatvāttatkāraṇamapyanyat, evamuparyuparīti kāraṇaparamparākalpanā yathā prāmāṇikī na doṣāya, evamavinābhāvabalādāpatantīsaṅghātaparamparākalpanāpīti bhāvaḥ / nanu saṅghātatvasya bhoktṛtvalakṣaṇe paratve 'hetutvānna saṅghātaparārthatvena saṅghātatvasya vyāptigraha ityatrā'ha
children.translated_text: From the effect, the cause is to be inferred. And since the cause too, being occasional, is an effect, its cause too is to be inferred —
'na ca' ('but not')

children.text:
ti /
saṅghātaparatvaṃ tadadhīnātiśayabhāji sambhavet / tadadhīnātiśayaścāsaṃhate nirlepe nirvikāra'ta evātiśayādhānānarhe sāṅkhyābhimatepuruṣe na sambhavatīti saṃhatasyaiva kasyacitsaṅghātaśeṣiṇo 'numānena siddhirnāsaṃhatasya sāṅkhyamatapuruṣasyeti bhāvaḥ / bhogarūpo 'pyatiśayo na sāṅkhyapuruṣasya sambhavediti hārdam / etena
children.translated_text: The being-for-another of the aggregate is possible in what partakes of an excellence dependent on it. But the excellence dependent on it [is not possible] in the non-composite
'puruSho 'sti bhoktRbhAvA' ('the purusa exists because of being an enjoyer')

children.text: dityapi parāstam / dṛśyate ca khaṭvādeḥ śarīrārthatvam, śarīrasya ca śarīrāntarārthatvam / atastadadhīnātiśayabhāktvarūpe tatparatve saṅghātatvasya prayojakatvena tadavacchinnaparārthatvena vyāptigrahaḥ sambhavatyeveti cābhimatam /
children.translated_text: — this too is refuted. And it is observed that a bedstead and the like serve the purpose of the body, and the body serves the purpose of another body.
'taddhi' ('for that')

children.text: ti / yadyenopakriyate kriyate vā tattasya śeṣi pradhānamaṅgi bhavati, yattūpakaroti karoti vā tattadarthaṃ taccheṣaḥ tadaṅgamityanvayārthaḥ / upakriyate-atiśayavān kriyate, strakūcandanādineva dehādiḥ, prayājādineva ca yāgādiḥ / kriyate-niṣpādyate, daṇḍādineva ghaṭādiḥ, puroḍāśādineva ca yāgādiḥ / tatra upakriyamāṇaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ vā aṅgi, upakārakaṃ kārakaṃ vā aṅgamiti vivekaḥ /
children.translated_text: That by which [something] is benefited or served — that [benefiter] is its <s>sesin</s> (principal), <s>pradhana</s> (chief), <s>angin</s> (whole). But that which benefits or serves [is the accessory].
'na ca tathA' ('but not so')

children.text:
ti / tathā-atiśayādhānārhaḥ / sāṅkhyapuruṣaḥ-kāpilābhimata ātmā /
nanvanupakāryatve 'pyātmana etairupakṛto 'hamityupakṛtatvabhramalakṣaṇa evopakāro dehādibhiḥ sādhya iti tatparatvamupapadyata iti cettatrāha
children.translated_text: 'Tatha' — capable of receiving excellence. '<s>Sankhya purusa</s>' — the self as maintained by the <s>Kapila</s> school. [Objection:] Even though not [actually] benefited,
'api ca' ('moreover')

children.text: ti / citiśakteḥ-caitanyasvarūpasya puruṣasya / śaktiśaktimatorabhedābhiprāyeṇaivamuktiḥ / buddhyaparaparibhāṣābhidhānam-buddhirityaparaṃ svīyatantrasaṅketitaṃ yasya nāma tadityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: of the power of consciousness (<s>citisakti</s>) — of the <s>purusa</s> whose nature is consciousness. With the intention of the non-difference of power and the power-possessor.
'does not err'
The internal organ is not the locus of error, because it is non-conscious, like a pot and the like. This is the meaning.
'acidapi' ('even the non-conscious')

children.text: ti / acetanamapi caitanyapratibimbāśrayatayā cetanavadbhātītyarthaḥ / ciccetanaśabdau svayamprakāśābhiprāyāvatra /
children.translated_text: Even the non-conscious appears as if conscious through being the substrate of the reflection of consciousness. This is the meaning. 'Cit' and 'cetana' —
'nirUpAyAH' ('formless')

children.text: iti / chāyāyāḥ kāntilakṣaṇāyā ujjavalarūpavaddharmabhūtāyā nīrūpe caitanye 'sambhavānnīrūpe cāntaḥkaraṇe tatpratiphalanalakṣaṇasaṅkrānterayogādityarthaḥ / rūpavatyeva hi sphaṭikādau japākusumalohitādipratiphalanaṃ dṛṣṭamiti bhāvaḥ / śaṅkate
children.translated_text: The impossibility of the reflection (<s>chaya</s>) — characterized by radiance — which is an attribute-property having a brilliant form — in consciousness that is formless.
'chAyeva' ('like a reflection')

children.text: ti / na chāyāśabdena mukhyā kāntirvivakṣitā / api tu sādṛśyam / citsādṛśyāpattiścetanāyamānatvamiti cedityarthaḥ / prativakti
children.translated_text: The word 'reflection' (<s>chaya</s>) is not intended in its primary sense of radiance. Rather, [it means] similarity. The attainment of similarity with consciousness —
'kah kha-'
('what indeed'). The meaning is: in what form is the similarity? Here he says
'citisarUpatvam' ('similarity of form with consciousness').
The meaning is: similarity through possessing the absence of all transformation-modifications in general. He refutes:
'hantaivam' ('alas, if so')

children.text: iti / bhramādayo hi vṛttayo 'ntaḥkaraṇasya nirvṛttikatve nopapadyanta ityarthaḥ / bhramopapādanārthaṃ hi pariṣkriyate cetanāyamānatvam, taccennirvṛttikatvarūpam, naiva prasaṅgo bhramādyudayasya, tathā ca yadarthamayamārambhaḥ tatkāryamavasāditamiti bhāvaḥ / prakārāntaraṃ śaṅkate
children.translated_text: For the modifications such as error and the like of the internal organ would be untenable if it were without any activity. This is the meaning.
'cetanatvena' ('through being conscious')
means 'through being a knower.' Another interpretation:
'ajaDayamAnatvam' ('becoming as if non-inert').
He replies:
'ajaDatvam' ('non-inertness')

children.text: iti / jñāturahamarthasyātmana evetarānapekṣaprakāśatvalakṣaṇamajaḍatvaṃ sambhavatīti jñātrātmasamarthanāvasare proktam / tathā caivaṃvidhājaḍatvasya jñātṛtvasamānāśrayatvājjñātṛtvenaiva jñātṛtvasamanarthanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavediti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-inertness, characterized by illumination that is independent of anything else, is possible only for the self, the 'I'-object, which is the knower.
'tenaiva' ('by that very')

children.text: ti / jñātṛtvaikāśrayeṇājaḍatvenaivetyarthaḥ / etat-ajaḍāyamānatvam, na kiñcit-nārthasādhakam, vivakṣitabhramavattopapādakaṃ na bhavati / asiddhamasiddhena sādhyata iti yāvat / yadvā na kiñcidetat-anatiprasaktaṃ prakṛtārthopapādakaṃ durnirūpamiti bhāvaḥ / antaḥkaraṇasyājaḍatvopagame sāṅkhyasyāpasiddhāntaṃ cāha
children.translated_text: means 'by non-inertness alone, which has its sole locus in the knower.' 'This' — the becoming-as-if-non-inert. 'Amounts to nothing' — is not anything [significant].
'api ca' ('moreover')

children.text: ti / nanvantaḥkaraṇasya citisārūpyāsambhave 'pi tasmin citipratibimba eva jñātṛtvādimānastu ityatrāha
children.translated_text: Objection: Even though the similarity of form of the internal organ with consciousness is impossible, knower-hood [may reside] in the reflection of consciousness in it.
'na ca citi-' ('but not consciousness')

children.text: ti / bimbatvenābhimatācit, pratibimbādhāratvenābhimatamantaḥkaraṇam / dvandvasyābhimataśabdena karmadhārayaḥ / bimbagatasya vakratādeḥ pratibimbādhāragatasya vā mālinyādeḥ pratibimbe āropasambhavaḥ / na ca jñātṛtvaṃ bhramo vā prakṛte 'nyatarasminnapyasti, yasya citpratibimbe āropaḥ syāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Consciousness is what is intended as the original image; the internal organ is what is intended as the substrate of the reflection. Of this pair,
'pratyuktasca' ('and it has been replied')

children.text:
ti / nyāyatattvaśāstrādāviti śeṣaḥ /
nanvantaḥkaraṇa eva viṣayākārapariṇāmalakṣaṇajñānavṛtterupagamādanyatarasminnapyavṛtti tvamasiddham / tataśca citibuddhyorvivekāgrahācciti jñātṛtvapratibhāso yujyata eveti śaṅkate
children.translated_text: in the <s>Nyayatattva</s> treatise and elsewhere — is to be supplied. Objection: In the internal organ itself, there is a modification in the form of the object,
'yaducyate' ('as for what is said')

children.text: ityādinā / nirvikārāyā api citiśakteḥ sannidhānabalādevāntaḥkaraṇasya pratyakṣādipramāṇajñānabhrāntyādilakṣaṇā vṛttibhedāḥ samudayante / prādhānyāt citeḥ tāsāṃ sākṣitvaṃ bhoktatvaṃ ca, yathā niśceṣṭasyāpi sārvabhaumasya prādhānyāt prabalasāmantacakrakartṛkayuddhaparākramavijayabhāktvaṃ tadvaditi śaṅkiturāśayaḥ / parākramīyaḥ-atiśayena parākramavat / pariharati
children.translated_text: and so forth. Even though the power of consciousness is without modification, by the very force of [its] proximity, the internal organ — whose variegated modifications of perception and the like [are raised] —
'tadanupapannam' ('that is untenable')

children.text:
iti / sākṣitvaṃ hi na caitanyamātratvam, kintu sākṣāddraṣṭṛtvam / na tacciteḥ, draṣṭṛtvaṃ kalpitamiti cet nirvikāre nirdharmake kūṭasthe caitanye draṣṭṛtvabhramo 'pi na sambhavatītyuktameva / dṛṣṭānte tu na nirvyāpāratvaṃsārvabhaumasya nirdharmakatvaṃ vā / svasvāmibhāve hetavaśca krayapratigrahotpādanabharaṇādayaḥ prasiddhāḥ / rājñaśca bharaṇādihetukaṃ svāmitvamupapannam / na tu sāṅkhyābhimatasya puruṣasyeti
samuditāśayaḥ / nanu sāṅkhyābhimatasyātmano 'numānāsambhave 'pi naiyāyikādibhirādheyātiśayatvena bhoktatvena cābhimatasyātmanaḥ saṅghātaparārthatvānumānena sādhanaṃ syāditi cet, na / saṅghātasya saṃhataparārthatvena vyāprerasaṃhatasya parasya siddherayogāt / naca
bhoktrarthatvenaiva saṅghātatvasya vyāptirastu / tathā cāsaṃhatātmasiddhirapratyūheti vācyam / śarīrasyāpi śarīrāntararūpabhoktrarthatvasādhanaparyavasānādvivakṣitāsiddheḥ / śarīrādivyatiriktasya bhoktaranumānātpūrvamasiddhyā ca vilakṣaṇabhoktrarthatvena vyāpteragrahādvilakṣaṇātmasādhanāyoga iti dik /
ātmani dehādibhedasādhakānumānānāṃ pratyakṣabādhamapyāha
children.translated_text: For witness-hood (<s>saksitva</s>) is not mere consciousness-hood, but rather direct seer-hood. And that is not [possible] for consciousness, because seer-hood [requires an agent],
'sthUlo 'ham' ('I am stout')

children.text:
iti / pratyakṣamṛditaviṣayatayā-pratyakṣabādhitasādhyakatayā / atītakālatābādhitahetvābhāsatā / vyatirekānumānabhedānāṃ-vilakṣaṇātmānumānānāṃ kāpilanaiyāyikābhimatānām /
dehādibhede ātmanaḥ śrutimeva pramāṇatayopanyasyanti śrotriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Because of being a subject-matter that has been crushed by perception — because of the provable being sublated by perception. Having a past-ness sublated [from the perceptual evidence] —
'sa eSha' ('that is')
'neti neti' ('not this, not this')
is the negation of the modes belonging to the body and the like, of the self. [The self is] distinct from the body, devoid of wound and the like which are properties of the body,
'yonim' ('a womb')

children.text: iti / atra śarīraprāpakayonisambandhapratipādanenātmanaḥ śarīrabhinnatvaṃsidhyati / śarīratvāya-śīryamāṇatvāya / idaṃ ca na svarūpeṇa, kintu śarīraviśiṣṭaveṣeṇa / tathāca dehāderevotpattyādi nātmana ityatra śrutirna jāyata iti / śarīrabhinnatvamuktamātmanaḥ / śarīrasaṃsṛṣṭatvamapyaupādhikameva, muktautvaśarīratvamevetyatra śrutimupādatte
children.translated_text: Here, through the teaching of the connection with a womb that leads to the attainment of a body, the distinctness of the self from the body is established.
'<s>na ha vai</s>' (indeed not)

children.text: iti / śrutiṃ pramāṇamuktvā vilakṣaṇātmani śrutyarthāpattimapi pramāṇamāha
children.translated_text: Thus. Having stated <s>śruti</s> (scripture) as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) regarding the self that is distinct [from the body], he also states <s>śrutyarthāpatti</s> (presumption from the meaning of scripture) as a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
'<s>kālāntare</s>' (at another time)
Thus.
'<s>tadanupapattī</s>' (the impossibility of that)

children.text:
ti / śrutyarthānyathānupapattītyarthaḥ / vidhyanyathānupapattīti vā / dehavināśordhvabhāvisvargādisādhanakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ tadvidhānaṃ vā bhoktarātmano dehātirekaṃ nityatvaṃ ca vinā hi na ghaṭate / nanveva dehavyatireke siddhe 'pīndriyādibhedo na sidhyatīticet; atrocyate-golakātiriktendriyasyāpi na śāstramantarā siddhiḥ / śāstratastu vilakṣaṇātmana upakaraṇatvenaiva tatsiddhiriti vilakṣaṇātmasiddhiḥ śāstrato niṣpratyūheti /
vilakṣaṇātmani anumānaikapramāṇakatvamāgamaikapramāṇakatvaṃ ca matabhedenopapādya pratyakṣatvaṃ mīmāṃsakamatena nirūpayitumupakramate
children.translated_text:
Thus. The meaning is: the impossibility of the meaning of scripture being otherwise (<s>śrutyarthānyathānupapattiḥ</s>). Or alternatively, the impossibility of the injunction being otherwise (<s>vidhyanyathānupapattiḥ</s>). For the performance of <s>karma</s> (ritual action) that is a means to <s>svarga</s> (heaven) and other [results] occurring after the destruction of the body, or the injunction thereof, is not possible without the difference of the self — the enjoyer — from the body, and its eternality. Now, if it be objected that even when the difference from the body is established, the distinction from the sense organs and so forth is not established — to this it is replied: even the sense organ that is distinct from the eye-socket is not established without <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative teaching). But from <s>śāstra</s>, the establishment of that [sense organ] is precisely through its being an instrument of the self that is distinct [from the body] — thus the establishment of the distinct self from <s>śāstra</s> is unobstructed.
Having demonstrated through difference of doctrinal positions that regarding the distinct self, some hold it to be knowable only through <s>anumāna</s> (inference) and others only through <s>āgama</s> (scripture), he begins to determine its perceptibility according to the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> position.
'<s>nanu hitāhite</s>' (but regarding what is beneficial and harmful)

children.text:
ti / hitaṃ balavadaniṣṭānanubandhīṣṭasādhanaṃ śāstraikasamadhigamyam / ahitaṃ-balavadaniṣṭānubandhi / hitāhitapravartananivartanaikaparasya śāstrasyopari tattvaparatvasyāpi parikalpanaṃ mahābhāranikṣepalakṣaṇameva / sahyetavānanyalabhye tattvāṃśe 'pi kāryopayogini śāstrasya tātparyakalpanam / na tvanyalabhye / dehādivilakṣaṇaścātmā
pratyakṣeṇaiva sphuṭamadhigamyata iti nātra purovāditālakṣaṇaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ śāstrasya sambhavatīti śrotriyopari pratyavasthānaṃ mīmāṃsakasya /
ātmana indriyāgrāhyatvaṃ śaṅkate 'tra śrotriyaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus. The beneficial (<s>hita</s>) is the means to what is desired, not accompanied by a preponderance of the undesired, and is knowable only through <s>śāstra</s>. The harmful (<s>ahita</s>) is that which is accompanied by a preponderance of the undesired. To impose upon <s>śāstra</s> — whose sole concern is prompting engagement with the beneficial and disengagement from the harmful — an additional concern with reality (<s>tattva</s>) is nothing but casting the burden of the entire <s>Mahābhārata</s> [onto it]. For one should accept the imputation of purport to <s>śāstra</s> regarding the aspect of reality only when it is not obtainable otherwise and is useful for action — but not when it is obtainable otherwise. And the self, which is distinct from the body and so forth,
is clearly apprehended by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) itself — therefore the validity of <s>śāstra</s> characterized by what was previously stated does not apply here — thus is the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>'s counter-position against the <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedāntin).
Here the <s>Śrotriya</s> raises the objection of the self being ungraspable by the sense organs.
'<s>maivaṃ voca</s>' (do not speak thus)

children.text: ityādinā / rūpādivyatirekiṇi-rūpasparśarahite / dravyapratyakṣe hi udbhūtarūpasparśānyatarasya kāraṇatvam / tadabhāvānnātmanaḥ pratyakṣatvaṃ sambhavati / niratiśayasūkṣma ityanena indriyagrahaṇāyogyatvaṃ vivakṣitam / yogya eva hi pratyakṣaṃ prabhavati nāyogya iti bhāvaḥ / indriyāgrāhyatve ātmanaḥ śrutimudāharati
children.translated_text: By this and what follows. [The self] is devoid of form, touch, and the like — that is, it lacks <s>rūpa</s> (form) and <s>sparśa</s> (touch). For in the perception of a substance, the cause is either manifest form or touch. Since those are absent, the perceptibility of the self is not possible. By [the phrase] 'supremely subtle' (<s>niratiśayasūkṣma</s>), the unfitness for sense-organ apprehension is intended. The purport is: perception functions only with respect to what is fit, not what is unfit. He cites <s>śruti</s> (scripture) in support of the self's ungraspability by sense organs.
'<s>parāñcī</s>' (directed outward)
Thus. The meaning is: the sense organs are capable of grasping only external objects.
And every object of the sense organs is bound by non-sentience (<s>acittva</s>);
Therefore, sensory cognition (<s>aindriyaka jñāna</s>) is not capable of reaching the self. [verse 17]

children.text: syānmatam-bhautikatvādbahirindriyāṇi mā nāmātmani pravartiṣata / manastu pravartiṣyate abhautikatvāditi; tanna; tasyāpīndriyatve bhautikatvasyāparihāryatvāt / yathā'mnāyate 'annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ' iti / prapañcitaṃ caitannirūpaṇe /
children.translated_text: One might think: since the external sense organs are material (<s>bhautika</s>), let them indeed not operate with respect to the self; but the mind (<s>manas</s>), being non-material, will operate [upon it]. That is not so, because even if it is a sense organ, materiality cannot be avoided for it. As the scripture declares: 'The mind is indeed made of food (<s>annamaya</s>), O <s>Somya</s>.' And this has been elaborated in the examination of that [topic].
(Thus the objection regarding the non-perceptibility of the self.)

children.text: athocyeta-asti tāvadahamityaparokṣāvabhāsaḥ pratyayaḥ / na caindriyikatvamantareṇāsau sambhavati / kḷptaṃ ca bahirindriyāgocare 'pi sukhādau svāntasvātantryamiti tannimitta evāyamahaṃpratyayo yuktaḥ / prayogaśca bhavati-ātmā mānasapratyakṣagrāhyaḥ bahirindriyāyogyatve sati pratyakṣatvātsukhādivat iti /
children.translated_text: Now it may be said: there exists, to be sure, a cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>) that manifests as immediately apparent in the form 'I' (<s>aham</s>). And that is not possible without being sensory. And it is established that even with respect to pleasure and the like, which are beyond the range of the external sense organs, the mind has independent capacity — therefore this <s>ahaṃpratyaya</s> (I-cognition) is properly grounded in that [mind]. And the formal argument is: the self is graspable by <s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s> (mental perception), because while being unfit for external sense organs, it is nevertheless perceptible — like pleasure and the like.
(Thus the introduction of the inference for <s>mānasa-pratyakṣatva</s> (mental perceptibility) of the self, presented through the voice of the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> [Mīmāṃsaka].)

children.text: tanna; saṃvedanena vyabhicārāt / na ca tadapratyakṣam / jānāmītyananyopādhikatayā pratibhānāt / apratyakṣatve ca saṃvedanasyāsiddhireva syādityuktameva / naca tadapi mānasapratyakṣatayā sapakṣe nikṣepamarhati; vimardāsahatvāt / yadā khalu kutaścidātmamanaḥsaṃyogādviṣayasaṃvit udayamāsādayati, tadaiva kiṃ tata eva tadgocaramapi vedanaṃ janyate, utānyadānyeneti vācyam / naca yugapadubhayajananaṃ sambhāvyate / tathā hi sati
children.translated_text: That is not so; because of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) with respect to <s>saṃvedana</s> (awareness). And that [awareness] is not non-perceptible. Because it manifests as 'I know' without any other qualifying condition. And if it were non-perceptible, even the establishment of awareness would be impossible — this has already been stated. Nor can that [awareness] be included in the corroborating instance as being of the nature of mental perception, because it cannot withstand critical scrutiny. For when, from some contact of the self with the mind, cognition of an object arises, then one must state: is the awareness of that [cognition] also produced from the same [contact] at that very time, or at another time from another [contact]? And the simultaneous generation of both is not conceivable. For if that were so,

children.text: parāparatattadgocaraniravadhikadhīnikurumbajanma tatkālamevāpadyeta / naca tadasti / yugapadutpattau viṣayaviṣayitvaniyamaśca nirnibandhanaḥ / asamasamayajanmanā jñānena vedyatve na pratyakṣatvaṃ; kṣaṇikatvenāgrimajñānasya āgrāhakajñānodayamavasthānābhāvāt / bhāve ca
children.translated_text: an unlimited swarm of cognitions — higher and lower, each having its own object — would arise at that very moment. But that is not the case. And the rule that one be the object and the other the cognizer would be groundless in the case of simultaneous origination. If [awareness] is cognized by a cognition arising at a different moment, there is no perceptibility, because the cognition to be grasped, being momentary, does not persist until the arising of the subsequent grasping cognition. And if it did persist,

body.translated_text: He first refutes the inference from the being-for-another of the aggregate, which was introduced by the <s>Sankhyas</s> as proving a distinct self, with

body.text: sarvajñānānāṃ sarvadāvasthānaprasaṅgāt / kāryavirodhitve cānantarameva saṃskārodayānna kālāntare sthitiriti saṃvido na mānasapratyakṣavedyatvam / na cāpratyakṣā saṃviditi sphuṭo vyabhicāraḥ / aindriyikatvasyānātmatvapratibaddhatvādviruddhatā ca / sādhyavikalaśca dṛṣṭāntaḥ, sukhaduḥkhayoḥ pratyakṣatvānabhyupagamāt / anabhyupagamaścendriyapauṣkalyanāśayoreva sukhaduḥkhatvāt / na hi tasminnapratyakṣe tatpauṣkalyaṃvaikalyaṃ vā pratyakṣaṃ bhavati / indriyasvarūpa ivābhyāsapāṭavāttayoraparokṣatvābhimānaḥ, mano 'vasthābhedeṣviva cānumeyamanovādinām /
body.translated_text: there would be the absurd consequence that all cognitions persist at all times. And if [non-persistence is maintained because of] incompatibility with the effect, then since a <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) arises immediately after, there is no persistence at a later time — therefore awareness is not cognizable through mental perception. And awareness is clearly not non-perceptible — thus the deviation is evident. And there is <s>viruddhatā</s> (contradiction), because being sensory is invariably concomitant with being non-self. The example too is deficient with respect to the <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved), since the perceptibility of pleasure and pain is not accepted [by the <s>Prābhākara</s>]. And the non-acceptance is because pleasure and pain consist precisely in the flourishing and destruction of the sense organ. For when that [sense organ] is not perceptible, neither its flourishing nor its deficiency is perceptible. Just as with the nature of the sense organ itself, the impression of immediacy regarding those [pleasure and pain] arises from habitual practice — and for those who hold the mind to be inferred, [pleasure and pain] are to be inferred from differences in mental states.

body.text: yastu sugatamatāvalambī vijñānābhinnahetujatayā tayorapi tadantarbhāvamabhimanyate; kaṇabhakṣapakṣāśrayaṇena vā tayorātmaviśeṣaguṇatvam;tābhyāṃ sukhaduḥkhādhikaraṇaṃ vyācakṣīta; svataḥsukhītyetadvimarśaṃ vātratyam / rāgadveṣādayastu caitanyasyaivāvasthāviśeṣāstadvadeva pratyakṣībhavantīti na tannidarśanenānumānodayaḥ / sukhaprayuktaviṣayīkāracaitanyaṃ rāgaḥ, tadvirodhaprayuktaviṣayīkāraṃ tadeva dveṣaḥ, bhūtaduḥkhajñānena cetaścalanaṃ śokaḥ, āgāmitajjñānena cetaścalanaṃ bhayamityādi lakṣaṇagranthādevāvagantavyamityalaṃ pravistareṇa /
body.translated_text: As for one who, relying on the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddhist) doctrine, considers that pleasure and pain, being of a nature inseparable from <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), are subsumed within it; or who, taking recourse to the position of <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (<s>Kaṇāda</s>), [holds] them to be particular qualities of the self; [such a one] might explain the substratum of pleasure and pain through those [doctrines]; or [might cite] the reflection 'I am happy by nature' (<s>svataḥsukhī</s>) as belonging to this [context]. But <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) and the like are particular states of consciousness itself and become perceptible just as [consciousness does] — hence no inference arises from citing them as examples. <s>Rāga</s> is consciousness in the mode of objectification impelled by pleasure; <s>dveṣa</s> is that very [consciousness] in the mode of objectification impelled by what is contrary to that; <s>śoka</s> (grief) is the agitation of the mind caused by cognition of past suffering; <s>bhaya</s> (fear) is the agitation of the mind caused by cognition of future [suffering] — and so forth, these are to be understood from the definitional treatises themselves. Enough with prolixity.

body.text: (iti gurumukhenātmano mānasapratyakṣatvānumānadūṣaṇam)

children.text: ekasya cātmano niraṃśasya na svāpekṣayā grāhyagrāhakabhāvaḥ, virodhādityapyuktameva / aṃśabhedāśrayaṇe tatsiddhaye cāṃśāntaramāśrayitavyam, tathā tatra tatretyanavasthā; saṅghātatvaṃ cātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And for a single, partless self, the relation of grasped and grasper with respect to itself is not [possible], due to contradiction — this too has already been stated. If one resorts to a division into parts, then to establish that, yet another part must be resorted to, and so on for that [part] too — resulting in an infinite regress; and [this would entail] the self being a composite (<s>saṅghāta</s>).
(Thus the demonstration of contradiction in the self being both grasped and grasper.)

children.text: nanu ca grāhakāvabhāsaḥ śrutyā, svasiddhāntaśraddhāvipralabdhabuddhi- bhirabhihitaḥ; indriyādipratyāsannatattatpadārthamātrasphuraṇāt / tādṛśo 'pi kvacidastu nāma pratyayaḥ / sa tvāgantukātmapratiyogikaprākaṭyaprakāśādipadābhidheyārthadharmānumitajñānaviśiṣṭamānasapratyakṣasiddhātmanibandhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: But [one might say]: the manifestation of a grasper has been stated by <s>śruti</s>, by those whose intellects are misled by faith in their own doctrine — [the manifestation occurs] merely from the shining forth of the respective objects proximate to the sense organs and so forth. Let such a cognition exist somewhere. But that is grounded in the self established through <s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s> (mental perception) qualified by knowledge inferred from properties denoted by the terms <s>prākaṭya</s> (manifestness), <s>prakāśa</s> (luminosity), and the like — properties that belong to an adventitious counterpart of the self.
(Thus the counter-position of the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> within the <s>Prābhākara</s> doctrine as well.)

children.text: ucyate / aho khalu svānubhava eva vibhramaḥ parīkṣakāṇām, yat viṣayānubhavasamaye pūrvāvasthāto na kañcidviśeṣamayamātmano 'vabudhyata iti / uktaṃ hyetart-idṛśa evāyamarthaḥ, jñāyate na veti na vidmaḥ, mama vā pratibhāsate parasya vetyapi na vidma iti na
children.translated_text: It is replied: Ah, indeed, there is delusion among the examiners regarding their own experience itself — in that [they claim] at the time of experiencing an object, one does not apprehend any distinction of the self from the prior state. For this has been stated: 'This is exactly the nature of the matter — whether it is known or not, we do not know; whether it appears to me or to another, we do not know either' — such

body.translated_text: (Thus the refutation, through the voice of the teacher, of the inference for the mental perceptibility of the self.)

body.text: jātucidevaṃ pratītirasti, jñānajñātroranavabhāse tādṛśyapi pratītirāpadyeta; iti / so 'yaṃ parasaṃcetitāt svasaṃcetitasyātiśayaḥ sarvatra parisphurannasati grāhakāvabhāse nopapadyeta / anumitajñānālambanatve cājñāsiṣamityeva pratibhāsaḥ syāt, na jānāmīti; jñānajanyārthātiśayadarśanatadvyāptyanusandhānānumānodayasamaye 'num itsitajñānasyātivṛttatvāt / jñānānumānāsambhavaḥ pūrvamevoktaḥ / mānasapratyakṣatvaṃ cātmagrāhyadhīnirastam / tathāsati hi svaparavedyayoranatiśayaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: a cognition never arises in this manner. If neither the cognition nor the cognizer were manifest, then even such a cognition [as described] would occur. This superiority of one's own awareness over another's awareness, shining forth everywhere, would not be possible in the absence of the manifestation of the grasper. And if [the self] were grounded in inferred cognition, the appearance would be 'I inferred' rather than 'I know' — because at the time of the arising of the inference through observing the excellence of the object produced by cognition and the apprehension of the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) thereof, the cognition that was to be inferred has already passed. The impossibility of inferring cognition has been stated earlier. And mental perceptibility has been refuted as dependent on the self being an object of apprehension. For if that were so, there would be no superiority between what is known by oneself and what is known by another.

body.text: (iti prābhākarīyaṃ svapakṣasādhanam)

children.text: nanu kathamiva grāhakānavabhāse svaparavedyayoranatiśayaprasaṅgaḥ? nahi grāhakasiddhinibandhanaḥ svaparavedyaviśeṣaḥ; svasamavetaviṣayabodhajanmanā parasamavetabodhajanmanā ca tadviśeṣopapatteḥ / svaparasambandhibodhaviśeṣodavyavasthāpi svīyaparakīyendriyārthasannikarṣādijñānahetusāmagrībhedanibandhanā / na cātmasiddhirapi tatsāmagryanupraveśamarhati; indriyāderivānavabhāsamānasyaiva hetutvasambhavāt / naca viṣayabodha evātmabodha iti sāmpratam / na hyarthāntarasiddhirarthāntarasya siddhirbhavati, atiprasaṅgāt / api ca yadadhīnā bhāvānāṃ rūpabhedavyavasthā, tadapi hi saṃvedanaṃ tadānīṃ nilīnarūpamevendriyādivat / kutastu punaḥ tadāśrayasyātmanaḥ pratibhāsaprasaktiḥ? yadāhuḥ-idamahaṃ jānāmīti tritayāvabhāsaḥ sārvatrikaḥ, iti, tadapyanubhavānārūḍhamevānantarameva pratikṣiptamiti /
children.translated_text: But how can there be the absurd consequence of no superiority between what is known by oneself and by another, in the absence of the manifestation of the grasper? For the distinction between what is known by oneself and by another is not grounded in the establishment of the grasper; because the distinction is explained by the cognition born from an object inhering in oneself and the cognition born from [an object] inhering in another. The determination of the distinction between cognition belonging to oneself and to another is also grounded in the difference of the assemblage of causes of cognition, such as the contact of one's own and another's sense organs with their objects. And the establishment of the self too does not deserve entry into that assemblage — because it is possible for it to be a cause even while unmanifest, just like the sense organ and the like. And it is not proper [to say] that cognition of an object is itself cognition of the self. For the establishment of one thing is not the establishment of another, due to overextension. Moreover, that awareness upon which the determination of the distinction of forms of things depends — even that awareness has its form concealed at that time, just like the sense organ and the like. Whence then the propensity of the self, its substrate, to be manifest? As for what they say — 'the three-fold manifestation of "I know this" is universal' — even that, being not grounded in experience, has been refuted immediately after.
(Thus the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s>'s refutation of the <s>Prābhākara</s> position.)

children.text: astu tarhi grāhakatayaiva sarvārthagrahaṇasamayeṣvātmasiddhiḥ / abhyupagantavyā hi saṃvidaḥ svataḥsiddhiḥ, sarvaprakārasādhanāntaranirākaraṇāt, satyāśca tasyāḥ kadācidanavabhāsādarśanācca / yathā ca saṃvidaḥ
children.translated_text: Then let the establishment of the self occur at the time of every apprehension of objects, precisely in its capacity as the grasper. For the self-establishment (<s>svataḥsiddhi</s>) of awareness must be accepted — since every other kind of means of proof has been rejected, and since awareness, being real, is never seen to be unmanifest. And just as awareness

body.translated_text: (Thus the <s>Prābhākara</s>'s establishment of his own position.)

body.text: prakāśāvyabhicāraḥ, tathā prapañcitaṃ prathamādhikaraṇa iti nātropakṣipya pratikṣeptavyam / sato 'pi prameyajātasya svāpādisamaye 'nupalabderabhyupagataṃ tāvat saṃvidaḥ tatsādhakatvam / ataḥ kḷptārthāntarasādhanabhāvayā tayaivā'tmano 'pi siddhirabhyupagantuṃ nyāyyā /
body.translated_text: never deviates from luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), so this has been elaborated in the first chapter — hence it should not be introduced here only to be rejected. That awareness serves as the means of establishing even the entire range of knowable things that exist but are not apprehended during states such as deep sleep — this much has been accepted. Therefore, it is proper to accept that through that very [awareness], whose capacity to establish other things is already proven, the self too is established.

body.text: (iti punaḥ prābhākareṇa svamatasthāpanam)

children.text: yattu viṣayavittyuparame 'pi svāpasamaye 'yamātmā prakāśata iti, tat upapattibhirupapadyamānamapi yathāpratīti vyavaharatāṃ na cittamanurañjayati /
children.translated_text: As for [the claim] that even when the cognition of objects ceases, in deep sleep this self is luminous — that, even though it is supported by reasoning, does not satisfy the mind of those who proceed according to actual experience.
He also presents a logical argument:
'<s>acittve</s>' (in the case of non-sentience)

children.text: ti / acittvapratibaddhaḥ-acittvavyāpyaḥ / ātmā nendriyagrāhyaścetanatvāt, yannaivaṃ tannaivaṃ yathā ghaṭādīti cātra prayogaḥ //17//
children.translated_text: Thus. Bound by non-sentience (<s>acittva</s>) — meaning: pervaded by non-sentience. [The argument is:] the self is not graspable by the sense organs, because it is sentient (<s>cetana</s>); whatever is not so [i.e., not sentient] is not so [i.e., is graspable] — like a pot and the like. And here the formal argument is: [verse 17].

body.translated_text: (Thus the <s>Prābhākara</s>'s re-establishment of his own position.)

body.text: atra bhāṭṭamatamupakṣipati

children.translated_text: '<s>syānmatam</s>' (the view might be)
Thus. The <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedāntin) refutes it:
'<s>tanna</s>' (that is not so)

children.text: ti / gandhādimattvādeva hi ghrāṇādergandhādigrāhakatā vyavasthitā / tathā ca bhautikatvaṃ ghrāṇādeḥ sthitam / tannidarśanena ca manaso 'pi bhautikatvaṃ setsyati / tathā cābhautika'tmāgrāhakatvaṃ ghrāṇāderiva manaso 'pisyāditi bhāvaḥ / bhautikatve manasaḥ śrutimapyāha
children.translated_text: Thus. For the capacity of the nose and other [organs] to grasp smell and the like is established precisely because they possess smell and the like. And thus the materiality (<s>bhautikatva</s>) of the nose and other [organs] is established. And by that analogy, the materiality of the mind (<s>manas</s>) too will be established. And therefore, just as the nose and other [organs] cannot grasp the non-material self, so too the mind would be unable [to grasp it] — this is the purport. He also cites <s>śruti</s> regarding the materiality of the mind:
'<s>annamayam</s>' (made of food)

Thus.
The <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> replies:
'<s>athocyeta</s>' (now it may be said)

children.text:
tyādinā / aparokṣāvabhāsaḥ-parokṣapratītibhinnaḥ, laukikaviṣayitāvāniti yāvat / sukhādau manasaḥ svātantryaṃ ca bahirindriyānapekṣapratyakṣajanakatvam / mānasapratyakṣagrāhyaḥ-mānasapratyakṣanirūpitalaukikaviṣayatāvān / śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam /
prakṛtamanumānaṃ dūṣayati gurumukhena
children.translated_text:
By this and what follows. 'Immediately manifest' (<s>aparokṣāvabhāsa</s>) — different from mediate cognition, meaning: possessing ordinary objecthood. And the independence of the mind with respect to pleasure and the like is its capacity to generate perception without depending on the external sense organs. 'Graspable by mental perception' (<s>mānasapratyakṣagrāhya</s>) — possessing ordinary objecthood as determined by mental perception. The rest is clear.
He refutes the inference at hand through the voice of the teacher:
'<s>tanna</s>' (that is not so)

children.text: tyādinā / sādhyābhāvavati heto sattvaṃ hi vyabhicāraḥ / tatra saṃvidi hetau viśeṣaṇāṃśasya siddhatvādviśeṣyāṃśaṃ tāvatsādhayati
children.translated_text: By this and what follows. The presence of the <s>hetu</s> (logical reason) in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved) is indeed <s>vyabhicāra</s> (deviation). Therein, since the qualifier-aspect of the <s>hetu</s>, namely awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), is already established, he first demonstrates the qualificand-aspect:
'<s>na ca tad</s>' (and that is not)

children.text: ti / ananyopādhikatayā liṅgapadajñānādikāraṇānapekṣatayā / pratibhānāt-prakāśāt / nanu jñātatayaiva jñānānumānamityananyopādhikatvaṃ jñānapratibhāsasyāsiddhamityatrāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — Because it shines forth independently, without depending on any other condition (ananyopādhikatā) and without requiring causes such as the knowledge of the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) or word-knowledge — from its self-luminous manifestation (<s>pratibhāna</s>). Now, [the objection is:] 'The inference of cognition is made solely through the state of being known (<s>jñātatā</s>), therefore the independence of the appearance of cognition is unestablished.' To this he replies:
'If [cognition were] not perceptible (<s>apratyakṣa</s>)' —

children.text: ti / jñānātiriktāyāṃ jñātatāyāṃ jñānaliṅgatvenābhimatāyāṃ pramāṇābhāvāt, satyā api tasyā atīndriyatvena jñānasya tenāvinābhāvagrahāyogāt, jñānajanakasāmagryā jñātatāyā eva sākṣājjananasambhavādantarā jñānakalpanāyā apārthatvāccāsiddhireva syājjñānasyāpratyakṣatva iti bhāvaḥ / saṃvedane sādhyasyāpi sattvamāśaṅkate
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — Because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) for a state of being-known (<s>jñātatā</s>) that is distinct from cognition and is regarded as an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for cognition; because even if such a state existed, since it is beyond the senses (<s>atīndriya</s>), the apprehension of the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) of cognition with it would be impossible; and because the very causal complex that produces cognition can directly produce the state of being-known itself, making the additional postulation of cognition pointless — therefore the non-perceptibility of cognition would indeed remain unestablished. This is the purport. He raises the possibility that even the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) exists in <s>saṃvedana</s> (awareness):
'Nor is even that' —
[The root text says] 'ti' — He refutes the <s>mānasa-pratyakṣatva</s> (mental perceptibility) of awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) on the ground that it cannot withstand conceptual analysis (<s>vikalpa</s>).
'In the examination (<s>vimarda</s>)' —
[The root text says] 'ti' — He subjects it to conceptual analysis (<s>vikalpayati</s>).
'When (<s>yadā</s>)' —
Thus.
'That being so (<s>tathā sati</s>)' —

children.text: ti / viṣayajñānasyodayakāla eva tadgocarajñānajñānasyāpi ātmamanaḥsaṃyogarūpakāraṇabalādutpattisvīkāre pūrvottarībhūtaviṣayajñānajñānajñānajñānajñānajñānadīnāṃ samudāyasya yaugapadyaprasaṅgaḥ ityarthaḥ / nikurumbam-samudāyaḥ / viṣayajñānajñānajñānayoryaugapadye dūṣaṇāntaramāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — If one accepts that at the very moment of the arising of object-cognition, the cognition-of-cognition directed at that object also arises by the force of the cause in the form of the contact between the self and the mind (<s>ātma-manaḥ-saṃyoga</s>), then the absurd consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>) follows that the entire aggregate of prior and subsequent cognitions — cognition-of-object, cognition-of-cognition-of-object, cognition-of-cognition-of-cognition, and so on — would arise simultaneously. This is the meaning. <s>Nikurumba</s> means aggregate (<s>samudāya</s>). He states another objection against the simultaneity of object-cognition and cognition-of-cognition:
'Simultaneously (<s>yugapad</s>)' —

children.text: diti / pratyakṣe viṣayasya hetutvātpūrvajñānajanitasyottarajñānasyānuvyavasāyarūpasya pūrvajñānaviṣayakatvamupapadyeta kramabhāvitve na tu yaugapadya ityarthaḥ / astu tarhi kramikatvaṃ viṣayajñānatadanuvyavasāyayorityatraha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'diti' — In perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), because the object serves as the cause, the subsequent cognition — which is in the form of reflective judgment (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) produced by the prior cognition — could have the prior cognition as its object only if they arise in sequence, but not if they arise simultaneously. This is the meaning. [Objection:] 'Then let there be sequential arising of object-cognition and the reflective judgment upon it.' To this he replies:
'At different times (<s>asame</s>)' —

children.text: ti / jñānasya kṣaṇikatvāduttarajñānotpādakāle pūrvajñānasyāsattvānna pratyakṣatvaṃ sambhavetpūrvajñānejñānāntaravedyatvopagame 'pītyarthaḥ / jñānasya kṣaṇikatvānupagame doṣamāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — Because cognition is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), at the time of the arising of the subsequent cognition, the prior cognition no longer exists; therefore perceptibility would not be possible even if one accepts that the prior cognition is knowable by another cognition. This is the meaning. He states the fault if one does not accept the momentariness of cognition:
'If it persists (<s>bhāve</s>)' —
'if (<s>ced</s>)' —

children.text: ti / nanu na kṣaṇikatvam, nāpi sthiratvam / kintu svakāryeṇaiva nivṛttiriṣyate jñānasyeti cettatrāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — [Objection:] 'It is neither momentary, nor permanent; rather, it is held that cognition ceases only through its own effect.' To this he replies:
'Through the effect (<s>kārye</s>)' —

children.text:
ti / kāryasya viro
dhitvaṃ nāśakatvalakṣaṇaṃ ceddvikṣaṇāvasthāyitvaṃ syājjñānasya / sahānavasthānalakṣaṇaṃ cedekakṣaṇamātravṛttitvam/ atra tu sahānavasthānalakṣaṇa eva virodho vivakṣitaḥ / dvikṣaṇāvasthāyitve tu naiyāyikaprakriyayā mānasapratyakṣopapattestanniṣedhānupapatteriti bodhyam / naiyāyikamate 'pi dvitīyatṛtīyādijñānaviṣayakajñānādhārānuvṛttiprasaṅgo bodhyaḥ / ātmano mānasapratyakṣatvānumāne virodhamapyāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — If the opposition of the effect means the capacity to destroy, then cognition would persist for two moments. If it means the impossibility of co-existence, then cognition would last for only a single moment. Here, however, opposition in the sense of impossibility of co-existence is intended. If cognition were to persist for two moments, then by the <s>Naiyāyika</s> method, <s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s> (mental perception) would be established, and its refutation would not succeed — this should be understood. Even in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, the absurd consequence of the substratum persisting for the second, third, and subsequent cognitions directed at cognition should be noted. He also states the contradiction in the inference that the self is an object of mental perception:
'Of sense-perceptibility (<s>aindriyikatvasya</s>)' —

children.text: ti / anātmatvavyāpyatvādaindriyikatvasya vyāpakanivṛttyā'tmani nivṛttiravarjanīyā / tathā ca pakṣatāvacchedakātmatvaviruddhaṃ sādhyamiti bhāvaḥ / bāhyendriyagrāhyatvasyaivānātmatvavyāpyatetyāgrahe 'pi dūṣaṇāntaramāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — Since sense-perceptibility is pervaded by non-selfhood (<s>anātmatva</s>), its exclusion from the self is inevitable through the exclusion of the pervader. And thus the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) contradicts selfhood (<s>ātmatva</s>), which is the delimitor of the locus (<s>pakṣatāvacchedaka</s>). This is the purport. Even if one does not accept that only external-sense-apprehensibility is pervaded by non-selfhood, he states another objection:
'And the example lacks the <s>sādhya</s> (<s>sādhyavikala</s>)' —

children.text: ti / sādhyaśūnyo 'nvayaddaṣṭānta ityarthaḥ / sādhanavikalatvamapi yadyapi phalati upapādanaprakāreṇa; athāpi siddhāntaprakriyayā jñānāvasthārūpatvātsukhādeḥ jñānasya ca svayaṃprakāśatvātsvayaṃprakāśatvaṃ sukhāderhṛdi nidhāya sādhyavikalatvameva kīrtitam / anvayaddaṣṭānte sādhyasya sādhanasya vā virahena tadavacchedena sādhyavyāptigraho hetau sambhavatīti vyāpyatvāsiddhirvivakṣitā / nanu sukhaduḥkhayorapratyakṣatve pratyakṣavadavabhāsastayoḥ katham? tatrāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — The corroborative example (<s>anvaya-dṛṣṭānta</s>) is devoid of the <s>sādhya</s>. This is the meaning. Although the deficiency of the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) also applies through the manner of demonstration, nevertheless, according to the established doctrine — since pleasure and other [states] are forms of the state of cognition, and since cognition is self-luminous (<s>svayaṃprakāśa</s>) — keeping in mind the self-luminosity of pleasure etc., only the deficiency of the <s>sādhya</s> in the example is stated. Through the absence of either the <s>sādhya</s> or the <s>sādhana</s> in the corroborative example, the apprehension of the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) delimited by that [example] becomes possible in the <s>hetu</s> — hence the non-establishment of pervasion (<s>vyāpyatvāsiddhi</s>) is intended. [Objection:] 'If pleasure and pain are not perceptible, how is their appearance as if perceptible [explained]?' To this he replies:
'Regarding the sense-organ (<s>indriye</s>)' —

children.text: ti / yathātīndriyatve 'pīndriyāṇāṃ mamedaṃ cakṣuḥ, ahaṃ cakṣuṣmān paśyāmīti pratyakṣavadavabhāsaścakṣurādeḥ kadāciccākṣuṣādivṛtti kāle nānācakṣurādivṛtti pratisandhānavataścetanasyendriyaviṣayasaṃskāraprācuryaprayuktaḥ, tadvadindriyāvasthārūpasukhadūḥkhaparāmarśo 'pi pratyakṣasamānākārastadabhyāsabāhulyādityarthaḥ / atra nidarśanaṃ
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — Just as the sense-organs, though beyond the senses, appear as if perceptible — 'this is my eye,' 'I, possessing eyes, see' — this appearance is due to the abundance of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) regarding the sense-objects in the conscious being who, at the time of visual and other cognitions, connects the various activities of the eye and other organs. Similarly, the apprehension of pleasure and pain, which are states of the sense-organs, also appears like perception due to the abundance of such habitual practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>), having the same form as perception. Here the illustration is:
'Regarding the mental state (<s>manovasthe</s>)' —

children.text: ti / anumeyamanovādinaḥ buddhivyatiriktaṃ mano 'numānena sādhayantaḥ / kāmasaṅkalpādīnāṃ manovṛttirūpatvaṃ
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — Those who hold that the mind is to be inferred (<s>anumeyamanovādin</s>) establish the mind as distinct from the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) through inference. The nature of desire, resolve, and other [mental states] as modifications of the mind —
'Desire, resolve — all this is indeed the mind' —

children.text:
ti śrutyāpratīyate / teṣāṃ ca
pratyakṣatvāvabhāsaḥ tadviṣayānubhāvābhyāsaprācuryādeveti vaktavyaṃ yathā anumeyamanovādibhiḥ, tatheti bhāvaḥ /
sukhaduḥkhayorātmābhinnatvam, ātmana āgantukadharmarūpatvaṃ ca matabhedena prasiddhamanuvadati
children.translated_text: is understood from the <s>śruti</s> (scripture). And their appearance as if perceptible is to be explained solely through the abundance of habitual experience regarding their objects — just as it is explained by the proponents of the inferability of mind. This is the purport. The identity of pleasure and pain with the self, and their nature as adventitious properties of the self, which are well-known according to different doctrinal positions, he restates:
'For the follower of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha)' —
[The root text says] 'ti' — To this he replies:
'By those two (<s>tābhyām</s>)' —

children.text: miti/ caturthīdvivacanam / bauddhaprakriyayā kāṇādaprakriyayā vā kṣaṇikātmānanyatvaṃ, nityasyātmana āgantukadharmarūpatvaṃ vā manyamānābhyāṃ nyāyatattvaśāstrasthaṃ sukhaduḥkhādhikaraṇam, etatprakaraṇasthaṃ svataḥ sukhitvavicāraṃ vā prakīrtayedityarthaḥ / nanu sukhaduḥkhayoḥ mānasapratyakṣatve vivāde 'pi rāgadveṣāveva nidarśane bhaviṣyata ityatrāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'miti' — The dative dual ending [is used]. By those two — who hold either the non-difference [of pleasure and pain] from the momentary self according to the <s>Bauddha</s> system, or their nature as adventitious properties of the permanent self according to the <s>Kāṇāda</s> (Vaiśeṣika) system — let the section on the substratum of pleasure and pain found in the <s>Nyāyatattvashāstra</s>, or the inquiry into the nature of being inherently happy (<s>svataḥ sukhitva</s>) found in this very section, be expounded. This is the meaning. [Objection:] 'Even if there is dispute about the mental perceptibility of pleasure and pain, attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) will serve as illustrations.' To this he replies:
'Regarding pleasure (<s>sukhe</s>)' —

children.text:
ti / sukhatvaprayuktaṃ viṣayīkaraṇamupādeyatāprakāśanaṃ yataḥ tajjñānameva rāgaḥ sukhagocaropādeyatābuddhilakṣaṇa iti yāvat / tasya sukhasya virodha upaghāto yena tadgocaratyājyatāprakāśakajñānameva ca dveṣaḥ / tayośca jñānavadeva prakāśa iti naṃ sādhyānvaya iti bhāvaḥ / śokabhayayorapi na nidarśa
natvaṃ sambhavatītyāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — The objectification prompted by the quality of pleasantness — the manifestation of desirability (<s>upādeyatā</s>) — is such that the very cognition of it constitutes <s>rāga</s> (attachment), which is defined as the judgment of desirability directed toward pleasure. And <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) is precisely that cognition which manifests the quality of being-to-be-rejected (<s>tyājyatā</s>) directed at what opposes or harms that pleasure. And the manifestation of both [attachment and aversion] is just like that of cognition itself — hence there is no corroborative instance for the <s>sādhya</s>. This is the purport. He states that grief and fear also cannot serve as illustrations:
'Regarding what has occurred (<s>bhūte</s>)' —

children.text:
ti / taccalanamiti mudritapāṭhastu na sādhuḥ / atītaduḥkhānusandhānaprayuktaścittavikṣobhaḥ śokaḥ / āgāmiduḥkhahetuparāmarśādhīnaścittasaṅkṣobhaśca bhayam / tayoścāntaḥkaraṇadharmatvādeva na pratyakṣatvamiti dṛṣṭāntatvāyoga iti bhāvaḥ /
ātmano mānasapratyakṣatve sādhakasyāsambhavamuktvā bādhakamapyāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — The printed reading 'taccalanam' is incorrect. Grief (<s>śoka</s>) is the disturbance of the mind produced by the recollection of past suffering. And fear (<s>bhaya</s>) is the agitation of the mind dependent upon the apprehension of a future cause of suffering. Since both of these are properties of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), they are not perceptible — hence they cannot serve as examples. This is the purport. Having stated the impossibility of a means of proof (<s>sādhaka</s>) for the mental perceptibility of the self, he also states the counter-proof (<s>bādhaka</s>):
'Of one [entity] (<s>ekasya</s>)' —

children.text: ti / ekasyaikadaivaikakriyāyāṃ kartṛkarmabhāvāsambhavalakṣaṇo virodho 'tra vivakṣitaḥ / uktavirodhaparihārāyātmani aṃśabhedāśrayaṇedoṣamāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — The contradiction intended here is the impossibility of the agent-object relation (<s>kartṛ-karma-bhāva</s>) in a single entity performing a single action at the same time. He states the fault in resorting to a distinction of parts (<s>aṃśabheda</s>) in the self to resolve this contradiction:
'If there is no distinction of parts (<s>aśaṃbhede</s>)' —

children.text: ti / grāhakātmāṃśāntarasyāpi pramāṇasiddhatvāvaśyambhāvena tadgrāhakāśāntarameṣṭavyam, evamuparyuparītyanavasthetyarthaḥ / kadācidekāṃśenānyāṃśagrahaṇam, anyadā cāṃśāntareṇaitadaṃśagrahaṇamiti kālabhedenopapatternānavastheti cettatrāpyāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — Since the other part of the self that is the apprehender must also necessarily be established by a valid means of knowledge, yet another part to apprehend that part must be posited, and so on upward — resulting in an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>). This is the meaning. [Objection:] 'One part grasps another part at one time, and at another time the other part grasps this part — there is no regress due to temporal distinction.' To this too he replies:
'And the composite nature (<s>saṅghātatvaṃ ca</s>)' —

children.text:
ti / ātmano niraṃśatvaviruddhaṃ ca sāṃśatvamevaṃ sati prasajyata ityarthaḥ / sāṃśatve cānityatvādi āpādanīyam / atredaṃ bodhyam-gururjñāturātmano jñānaviṣayatvaṃ nānumanyate / kintu viṣayajñānakāleṣu jñātṛtvabalātprakāśamātraṃ manute / jñānasyāpi tathaiveti /
evaṃ prābhākareṇa dūṣite svapakṣe bhāṭṭastanmatamapi dūṣayati
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — And thus, having parts (<s>sāṃśatva</s>), which contradicts the partless nature of the self, would follow. This is the meaning. And from having parts, impermanence and other [undesired consequences] should be derived. Here this should be understood — the teacher does not accept that the knowing self (<s>jñātṛ-ātman</s>) becomes an object of cognition. Rather, he holds that at the times of object-cognition, there is merely a manifestation by virtue of being a knower. And the same applies to cognition itself. Thus, having refuted the <s>Prābhākara</s> position, the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> also refutes that [Prābhākara] view:
'But surely (<s>nanu ca</s>)' —

children.text: ti / śrutyetyanantaraṃ tanna, satu iti pūraṇīyam / atra
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — After 'śrutyā' (by scripture), the words 'tanna, sa tu' should be supplied. Here,
'And the appearance of an apprehender is not (<s>na ca grāhakābhāsa</s>)' —

children.text: iti pāṭhaḥ sambhāvyate / śrutyetyanantaraṃ siddhyatī ti śeṣaḥ / svasiddhāntetyataḥ pūrvaṃ sa tu iti yojyam / svasiddhāntābhiniveśavaśīkṛtacetasāmabhimānamūlako grāhakāvabhāsavādo na śrutipramāṇena sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ / grāhakāvabhāso nāma sarvajñāneṣvāśrayatayā'tmanaḥ sphuraṇam / śrutyāsyāsiddhau hetumanubhavavirodhamabhipretyānubhavaprakāramāha
children.translated_text: this is a possible reading. After 'śrutyā', 'siddhyati' (is established) should be supplied as the completion. Before 'svasiddhāntā' (from one's own doctrine), 'sa tu' should be connected. The doctrine of the appearance of an apprehender (<s>grāhakāvabhāsa</s>), rooted in the prejudice of those whose minds are captivated by attachment to their own established doctrine, is not established by scriptural <s>pramāṇa</s>. This is the purport. The appearance of an apprehender means the manifestation of the self as the locus (<s>āśraya</s>) in all cognitions. Since this is not established by scripture, he states the manner of experience, intending the contradiction with experience:
'Sense-organs and so forth (<s>indriyādi</s>)' —

children.text: ti / anubhavaviruddhaṃ hi na śrutiḥ pratipādayediti hārdam / śrutyetyatrānyathā pāṭhaḥ syādvā / svasiddhāntābhimānibhiḥ prābhākarairabhihito grāhakāvabhāso na mantavyaḥ pratītivirodhāt / pratītirhitattatpadārthamātraṃ prakāśayatīti samuditāśayaḥ / nanu ghaṭādipratyakṣegrāhakābhāsābhāve ghaṭamahaṃ paśyāmītyādyanubhavaḥ katham? tatrāha
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — The inner meaning is that scripture would not teach what contradicts experience. Or there may be an alternative reading at 'śrutyā'. The appearance of an apprehender asserted by the <s>Prābhākaras</s>, who are attached to their own doctrine, is not to be accepted — because it contradicts experience (<s>pratīti</s>). For experience illuminates only the respective object itself. This is the combined purport. [Objection:] 'If the appearance of an apprehender is absent in perception of a pot etc., how is the experience "I see the pot" [explained]?' To this he replies:
'Even such [experience] (<s>tādṛśo 'pi</s>)' —

children.text:
tyādivākyadvayena / yasya yadviṣaye jñānaṃ jātaṃ tasyaiva sor'thaḥ prakāśata iti prākaṭyasyā'tmapratiyogikatvamarthadharmasya / talliṅgakaṃ jñānānumānameva ca kādācitkam / tataścānumitajñānoparaktātmamānasarūpo niruktānubhavaśca kādācitka eva, nāyaṃ ghaṭacākṣuṣarūpaḥ / yena viṣayavittiṣu prakāśetā'tmeti bhāvaḥ / atra ca mānasapratyakṣe jñānavattvena viṣayatvaṃ dehādimattayā cāśrayatvamiti karmakartṛvirodhaparihāro 'bhimato bhāṭṭānām /
atra prābhākarasya pratyavasthānam
children.translated_text: through a pair of sentences. [The explanation:] When cognition of a certain object arises in someone, that object manifests for that very person — thus the manifestation (<s>prākaṭya</s>) has the self as its correlate and is a property of the object. And the inference of cognition based on that mark [of manifestation] is only occasional. Consequently, the experience described — which is in the form of the self colored by the inferred cognition and is mental in nature — is also only occasional, and is not of the same nature as the visual cognition of a pot. Therefore the self does not manifest in [all] object-cognitions. This is the purport. Here, the <s>Bhāṭṭas</s> maintain that the resolution of the agent-object contradiction [in self-knowledge] is that in mental perception, cognition serves as the object by virtue of possessing knowledge, while the self serves as the locus by virtue of possessing a body and the like. Here the <s>Prābhākara</s> responds:
'It is said (<s>ucyate</s>)' —
and so forth.
'In one's own experience itself (<s>svānubhava eva</s>)' —

children.text:
ti / jñāne jāte
tadvattvenātmopalambho 'pyanubhavasiddhaḥ / tatraiva vibhramo nāstitābhrama ityarthaḥ / svānubhavamapyajānataḥ parīkṣakatvaṃ śobhanamityupālambhaḥ / viṣayavedanakāle jñānasya jñātuścāvabhāsābhāve doṣaṃ pūrvoktaṃ smārayati
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — When cognition arises, the apprehension of the self as possessing that [cognition] is also established by experience. The error lies precisely there — it is an error of negation (<s>nāstitā-bhrama</s>), [i.e., denying what is experienced]. This is the meaning. The reproach is: 'It is splendid indeed that one who does not even know one's own experience should be an examiner!' He reminds of the previously stated fault if the manifestation of cognition and the knower is absent at the time of knowing an object:
'It has been stated (<s>ukta</s>)' —

children.text: mityādinā / jñānasyā prakāśābhāve jñāyate na vetisaṃśayādiprasaṅgaḥ / jñātuḥ prakāśābhāve mama jñāyate 'nyasya veti saṃśayādiprasaṅga iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. If cognition does not manifest, the absurd consequence of doubt and the like — 'Is it known or not?' — would follow. If the knower does not manifest, the absurd consequence of doubt and the like — 'Is it known by me or by another?' — would follow. This is the purport.
'This very one (<s>so 'yam</s>)' —
[The root text says] 'ti' — <s>Saṃcetitam</s> means 'known.' The excellence (<s>atiśaya</s>) — characterized by self-manifestation (<s>svātmane prakāśamānatva</s>) — is being experienced.
'In what is inferred (<s>anumite</s>)' —

children.text: ti / jānāmītyādipratīterjñātatāliṅgānumitajñānopanītabhānātmakātmamānasapratyakṣarūpatve 'tītajñānālambanatvādajñāsiṣamityevābhilāpaḥ syāt, na tu jānāmīti jñāne vartamānatvollekha ityarthaḥ / nanvatiśaighryāt kṣaṇabhedāgrahanibandhano vartamānatvāṃśe bhramalakṣaṇo jānāmīti pratyaya iti śaṅkāyāṃ tanmate dūṣaṇāntaramapi saṃsphorayati
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — If the experience 'I know' were in the form of mental perception of the self (<s>ātma-mānasa-pratyakṣa</s>), constituted by the appearance brought about by inferred cognition — cognition inferred through the inferential mark of the state of being-known (<s>jñātatā</s>) — then, since it would have past cognition as its object, the verbal expression should be 'I knew' (<s>ajñāsiṣam</s>), not 'I know' (<s>jānāmi</s>) with its indication of present tense in the cognition. This is the meaning. In response to the doubt that the cognition 'I know' involves an error regarding the present-tense aspect due to failure to apprehend the distinction of moments because of extreme rapidity, he brings forth yet another objection against that view:
'In cognition (<s>jñāne</s>)' —

children.text: ti / svajñānavyavahārahetukameva svajñānānumānamiti na sambhavatītyuktameva prāk / jñātatāliṅgakamapi jñānānumānaṃ jñānena jñātatāyā avinābhāvagrahāsambhavājjñānasāmagryaivānyathāsiddhatvācca jñātatāyā duḥsthameveti hārdam / viṣayajñāna eva jñātuḥ prakāśaṃ sādhayituṃ tasya mānasapratyakṣaṃ ca nirasyati
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — It has already been said that the inference of one's own cognition, which itself serves as the basis for the usage regarding one's own cognition, is not possible. The inference of cognition based on the mark of being-known (<s>jñātatā</s>) is also untenable — because the apprehension of the invariable concomitance of being-known with cognition is impossible, and because the causal complex of cognition itself is otherwise established [as the cause of being-known] (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>). This is the inner meaning. In order to establish the manifestation of the knower in object-cognition itself, and to refute mental perception of the same, he says:
'Regarding mental [perception] (<s>mānase</s>)' —

children.text:
ti / ātmana ityādiḥ / mānasapratyakṣatvamityatra bahuvrīheḥ tvapratyayaḥ /
ātmagrāhyatvaṃ dhiyaḥ svayaṃprakāśatvam / tacca jñānasya mānasapratyakṣānumānāyogapratipādanāt siddham / ātmano mānasapratyakṣatvaṃ ca vyabhicārātsādhakatvābhimatasya nirastaṃ sādhakābhāvādityarthaḥ / dhīnirastam-vyabhicāranirūpikayā dhiyā nirastam / vyabhitāranirūpakatvopapādakamātmagrāhyeti dhīviśeṣaṇam / atrā'tmagrāhyadhīvyabhicāranirastamiti vā anyathā vā mūlapāṭhaḥ sambhāvyate / evaṃ grahagrāhakayoḥ prakārāntareṇa bhānāsambhavamupapādya tadanavabhāse viṣayavittau pūrvoktātiśayāsambhavaṃ nigamayati
children.translated_text: [The root text says] 'ti' — '<s>Ātmanaḥ</s>' (of the self) should be supplied at the beginning. In '<s>mānasapratyakṣatvam</s>' (mental perceptibility), the suffix 'tva' forms a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. The self-apprehensibility of cognition (<s>dhī</s>) is its self-luminosity (<s>svayaṃprakāśatva</s>). And this is established through the demonstration that cognition is not amenable to either mental perception or inference. The mental perceptibility of the self has been refuted through the deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) of what was claimed as the means of proof, and through the absence of any valid means of proof. This is the meaning. '<s>Dhīnirastam</s>' means 'refuted by the cognition that establishes the deviation.' The qualifier '<s>ātmagrāhya</s>' of '<s>dhī</s>' (cognition) demonstrates the basis for its capacity to establish the deviation. Alternatively, the root text reading may be '<s>ātmagrāhyadhīvyabhicāranirastam</s>' or some other variant. Having thus demonstrated the impossibility of the manifestation of both the cognized and the cognizer in any alternative manner, he concludes with the previously stated impossibility of the excellence [of self-luminosity] in object-cognition when such manifestation is absent:
'That being so (<s>tathā sati</s>)' —

children.text:
ti / anatiśayaḥ-aviśeṣaḥ / svasmai jñāyamānatvena bhānamabhānaṃ cārthasyeti vailakṣaṇyasya virahaḥ svaparavedyayoḥ prasajyate viṣayavittau jñānajñātrorabhāne hītyarthaḥ /
bhāṭṭaḥ pratikṣipati
children.translated_text:
[continued] — thus. 'Without excellence' means 'without distinction.' The meaning is: if the manifestation and non-manifestation of the object [are both characterized] by being known to oneself, then the absence of difference between what is known by oneself and what is known by another would follow — since when cognition and cognizer do not manifest, [this would be the case] in the cognition of objects.
The <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> (follower of <s>Kumārila</s>) objects:
'But how [can this be]?'

children.text:
iti / svasmai bhāsamānatvarūpo viśeṣor'thasya tajjñānasya svaniṣṭhatvādeva ghaṭate tajjñāne svasyābhāne 'pi / viṣayabodhāśrayatvameva svasyātiśayo 'pūrvo viṣayavittikāla iti ca bhāvaḥ / naca vittiveditroragrahe pūrvoktaḥ saṃśayastadavastha iti vācyam/ svajñānajārthadharmaprakāśasya svaṃ prati pratyakṣatvādeva mama prakāśate na veti saṃśayasyānavakāśāt / jñānaphalaprakāśena jhaṭityeva jñānasyānumānācca mama jñānaṃ jātamanyasya vetyāderapyaprasakteḥ / naiyāyikaprakriyayā tu kāryanāśyatvājjñānasya dvikṣaṇāvasthāyitvādanuvyavasāyabalādeva
na niruktasaṃśayādiprasaṅgo jñānajñātroranavabhāse 'pi viṣayavittāviti ca bodhyam / ātmani bodhodaye ātmaprakāśasya hetutvaṃ nirasyati prasaṅgataḥ
children.translated_text: — thus. The distinction in the form of 'being manifest to itself' belongs to the cognition of the object due to its being self-established; hence, even when the self does not manifest in that cognition, [the distinction obtains]. The point is: being the locus of object-cognition is itself one's own novel excellence at the time of object-cognition. Nor should one say that the previously stated doubt persists when cognition and cognizer are not apprehended — because there is no room for the doubt 'does it manifest to me or not?', since the illumination of object-properties born of one's own cognition is itself perceptible to oneself. And because through the illumination of the result of cognition, cognition itself is immediately inferred, the [doubt] 'has cognition arisen in me or in another?' etc. also does not arise. But according to the <s>Naiyāyika</s> (Nyāya) procedure, since cognition is destructible as an effect and persists for only two moments, through the force of <s>anuvyavasāya</s> (subsequent reflective cognition) alone, there is no occasion for the stated doubt etc., even when cognition and cognizer do not manifest in object-cognition — this should be understood. He refutes, by way of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio), the claim that the self's luminosity is the cause of the arising of cognition in the self:
'Nor in the self'
— thus. Now, even if not constituted by the establishment of the self, let the aggregate of conditions for object-cognition itself be the cause of the self's illumination as well — to this he says:
'Nor in the object'

children.text: ti / indriyārthasannikarṣārthayogyatādighaṭitā viṣayabodhasāmagrī nāyogyātmabodhe 'pi samarthetyarthaḥ / atiprasaṅgāt-paṭabodhasāmagryā ghaṭādibodhaprasaṅgāt / viṣayabodhe bodhasyāpyaprakāśa ityāha
children.translated_text: — thus. The meaning is: the aggregate of conditions for object-cognition — constituted by sense-object contact, fitness of the object, etc. — is not capable of producing the cognition of the self, which is not its proper object. Because of over-extension — since it would follow that the aggregate of conditions for the cognition of cloth would produce cognition of a pot etc. He states that even in object-cognition, cognition itself does not manifest:
'Even if'

children.text: ti / mānādhīnā hi meyasiddhiḥ / tat padārthānāṃ jātiguṇādiviśeṣavyavasthā yadadhīnā tadapi saṃvedanaṃ viṣayaprakāśakāle 'prakāśamānasvarūpaṃ svarūpasadeva cakṣurādivadityarthaḥ / svarūpasajjñānenaiva viṣayaviśeṣasiddhivat svarūpasajjñātraiva svavedyaviṣayātiśayasiddhiriti bhāvaḥ / prābhākarāṇāṃ matamanuvadati
children.translated_text: — thus. For the establishment of what is to be known depends on the means of knowledge. That cognition too — on which depends the determination of particulars such as universal, quality, etc. of entities — has its own nature unmanifested at the time of illuminating the object, yet exists in its own form, just like the eye and other [sense organs]. The point is: just as the particulars of the object are established through cognition that exists in its own form, so too the excellence of what is known by oneself and the knower is established through the cognizer that exists in its own form alone. He restates the view of the <s>Prābhākaras</s> (followers of <s>Prabhākara</s>):
'As they state'
— and so forth. 'Universal' means: pervading all object-cognitions such as perception, inference, etc. He refutes it:
'That too'

children.text:
ti / anubhavānārūḍhamiti sādhakābhāva uktaḥ, anantarameva pratikṣiptamiti ca bādhakam /
jñānasyaivāyaṃ svabhāvaḥ-yat svaviṣayasyeva svasvāśrayaprakāśahetutvamapīti punaḥ prābhākaraḥ śaṅkate
children.translated_text:
— thus. 'Not verified in experience' states the absence of a proof; 'refuted just above' states the counter-proof.
The <s>Prābhākara</s> raises a further objection that it is the very nature of cognition to be the cause of illuminating its own locus as well as its own object:
'Let it be then'

children.text: ti / grāhakatayaiva-jñānāśrayatayaiva / viṣayabodhasāmagryā viṣayajñānameva jātam / tacca jñānaṃ svasāmarthyādeva aviṣayamapi svaṃ svāśrayaṃ ca prakāśayatīti bhāvaḥ / jñānasya svayaṃprakāśatvaṃ tāvatsādhayati
children.translated_text: — thus. 'Through being the grasper alone' means: through being the locus of cognition alone. Object-cognition alone has arisen from the aggregate of conditions for object-cognition. And that cognition, by its own power alone, illuminates even itself and its own locus, which are not its objects — this is the purport. He first establishes the self-luminosity of cognition:
'It must be admitted'
— thus.
'In every way'
— thus. The meaning is: because mental perception and inference based on signs such as 'being known' have been refuted.
'At some time'
— thus. The meaning is: because there is a necessary connection between existing and being manifest.
'Has been elaborated'
— thus. The rest is 'in the <s>Nyāyatattvāśāstra</s>' (Treatise on the Truth of Logic).
'Not here'

children.text: tyādi / prakāśavyabhicāritvamatamupakṣipya jñānasya tat nātra nirākaraṇīyamityarthaḥ / evaṃ svaprakāśatvamuktvā jñānasya viṣayaprakāśahetutvaṃ ca sādhayati
children.translated_text: — and so forth. Having introduced the view that [cognition] deviates from illumination, the meaning is: it is not to be refuted here. Having thus established self-luminosity, he also establishes cognition's capacity to illuminate objects:
'Even when existing'

children.text: ti / sato 'pi viṣayasya svāpe 'prakāśo jñānanivṛttyeti jñānasya viṣayaprakāśakatvasiddhiriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: — thus. The purport is: even though the object exists, in sleep there is no illumination due to the cessation of cognition — hence cognition's capacity to illuminate objects is established.
'Therefore'

children.text:
iti / paraprakāśakatvenaiṣṭavyāyāḥ saṃvida eva pramātravabhāsakatvamapi yuktamiti nātmanaḥ svayaṃprakāśatvamapi kalpanīyamiti bhāvaḥ /
svāpe 'pyātmano jñānamastīti matamanūdya khaṇḍayati
children.translated_text:
— thus. The purport is: since it is to be accepted that <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness) itself, through its capacity to illuminate other [things], is also the illuminator of the cognizer — it is not necessary to postulate self-luminosity for the <s>ātman</s> (self) as well.
Having restated the view that even in sleep there is cognition of the self, he refutes it:
'But that which'
— thus.
'That'

children.text:
diti / sukhamahamasvāpsamityādipratisandhānasya svāpe ātmaprakāśamantarānupapadyamānatvalakṣaṇayuktiyuktamapi svapo ātmanaḥ prakāśamānatvaṃ nānubhavamātraśaraṇānāṃ hṛdyaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ / upapadyamānamapītyapinopapattirapi naiva / pratisandhānasyānyathaivopapatteriti sphoryate / anyathāsiddhiragre prapañcayiṣyate
mūla eva /
children.translated_text: — thus. The meaning is: the self's being manifest in sleep, though justified by the reasoning characterized by the impossibility of the recollection 'I slept happily' without the self's illumination in sleep, is not agreeable to those who rely on experience alone. 'Even though justified' — the word 'api' ('even') [suggests] that even the justification itself does not hold. Because the recollection can be explained otherwise — this is hinted at. The alternative explanation will be elaborated further on in the root [text] itself.
But for the liberated one, cognition is impossible due to the absence of cause;
If [cognition were] eternal, there would be eternal liberation; and the scriptural passages [about omniscience] are <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogy). //18//

children.text: nirdhūtanikhilakaraṇakalevarajñānakarmavāsanānubandhasyāpavṛktasya na khalu svaparasaṃvedanodayanibandhanaṃ kiñcit sambhāvyate / naca manaso nityendriyatvena tatsaṃyogādeva tadā jñānaṃ janyata iti yuktam; svarūpato gaganavat nityasyāpi satastasyendriyabhāvena jñānotpādakatvasya dharmādharmāvarodhanibandhanatvāt /
children.translated_text: For the liberated one — whose connection with the residual traces (<s>vāsanā</s>) of all instruments, body, cognition, and <s>karma</s> has been shaken off — nothing whatsoever can be conceived as the ground for the arising of self-knowledge or knowledge of others. Nor is it reasonable that cognition is produced then through conjunction with the mind, [arguing] that the mind is an eternal sense-organ; for although the mind, like space, exists eternally in its own nature, its status as a sense-organ capable of producing cognition is dependent on the operation of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit).

children.text: svāpa ātmanaḥ prakāśaṃ niṣidhya muktāvapi taṃ niṣedhati
children.translated_text: Having denied the self's illumination in sleep, he denies it also in liberation:
'Of the liberated one'
— thus. 'Of the liberated one' means: of the one who has attained <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). If one says 'let the eternality of the liberated one's cognition be accepted,' to that he says:
'If [cognition were] eternal'

children.text: iti / saṃsaraṇābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ phalito 'tra / nanu tarhi muktau sārvajñyaparaśrutīnāṃ kā gatiḥ? tatrāha
children.translated_text: — thus. The consequence here is the absence of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). Now then, what is the status of the scriptural passages about omniscience in liberation? To that he says:
'<s>Arthavāda</s> (eulogy)'
— thus. The meaning is: the scriptural passages about omniscience etc. have as their intent the praise of the means of liberation, being occasioned by the absence of the effects of ignorance. //18//

body.translated_text: Here he introduces the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> position:

body.text: ślokārthameva prapañcayati

children.translated_text: 'Whose residual traces have been shaken off'

— and so forth. '<s>Jñānavāsanā</s>' (impressions of cognition) and '<s>karmavāsanā</s>' (impressions of <s>karma</s>) are the 'connection.' The meaning is: of one whose connection with the residual traces of all body, senses, etc. has been removed.
'Self and other'
— thus. The meaning is: the ground for the production of cognition, whether pertaining to one's own nature or to another object.
'<s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>'
— thus. The meaning is: because it is dependent on the cooperation of the unseen [karmic force].
The mind, assisted by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, while existing, is the means of cognition;
Even though it is an eternal sense-organ, [this is so] because of its status as instrument, like the ear. //19//

children.text: naca yogajadharmānugṛhītatatsaṃyogasya sādhanatvama; 'kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi' 'tadā vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ' ityādiśukletarasakalakarmaprakṣayaśrutivirodhāt / dharmaphalatve cāpavargasya punarāvṛttiprasaṅgaḥ / 'nāstyakṛtaḥ kṛtena' 'tadyatheha karmacito lokaḥ kṣīyate evamevāmutra puṇyacito lokaḥ kṣīyate' ityādiśravaṇācca / na cātmasattayaiva tadānīṃ tajjñānanimittamiti vācyam / klaptatyāgāklaptakalpanaprasakteḥ / tanmātranimittatve ca sarvadā ātmasvarūpavattadapi vidyata iti saṃsārānavatāraprasaṅgāt, bandhamokṣāvasthayoraviśeṣāpatteśca / na ca dehendriyādipratibaddhatayā idānīṃ tadabhāva iti vācyam / tat khalu pratibandhakam, yat sati puṣkalakāraṇe kāryodayaṃ niruṇaddhi / na cādyāpyātmanaḥ tatpuṣkalakāraṇatvaṃ siddham; śarīrendriyavatāmeva jñānadarśanāt / klaptajñānakāraṇabhāvasya tasyaiva tadbandhakatvavacanamunmattavacaḥ / ato nāstyapavargadaśāyāṃ jñānam /
children.translated_text: Nor is the conjunction [of the self] with the mind, assisted by <s>yoga</s>-born <s>dharma</s>, a [sufficient] means [for cognition in liberation]; because it contradicts the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) declaring the destruction of all <s>karma</s> — both bright and otherwise — such as 'his <s>karmas</s> are destroyed' and 'then the wise one, having shaken off merit and demerit, becomes stainless.' And if liberation were the result of <s>dharma</s>, there would be the unwanted consequence of return [to <s>saṃsāra</s>]. And because of such <s>śruti</s> texts as 'what is not done [cannot be had] through what is done' and 'just as here the world accumulated by <s>karma</s> is exhausted, so too the world accumulated by merit is exhausted.' Nor should one say that at that time the self's mere existence is the cause of that cognition — because there would be the unwanted consequence of imagining what has not been accepted while abandoning what has been accepted. And if mere [self-existence] were the cause, then, just as the self's nature always exists, that [cognition] too would always exist — leading to the unwanted consequence of never entering <s>saṃsāra</s>; and the states of bondage and liberation would become indistinguishable. Nor should one say that at present there is absence of that [cognition] because it is obstructed by the body, senses, etc. For that is an obstruction which, in the presence of a complete cause, prevents the arising of the effect. And it has not been established even now that the self is a complete cause of that [cognition]; because cognition is seen only in those possessing a body and senses. To call that [self] — whose causal status for cognition has been accepted — an obstruction to that very [cognition] is the speech of a madman. Therefore, in the state of liberation, cognition does not exist.

children.text: tātkālikajñānasukhādivādāstvātmajñānavidhiśeṣatayā guṇavādena netavyāḥ / ato viṣayavittisamaya evātmasiddhiniyamādyathoktanītyā arthavittiṣu veditṛtayaivātmasiddhiriti /
children.translated_text: The doctrines of temporary cognition, pleasure, etc. [in liberation] should be taken as <s>guṇavāda</s> (subsidiary eulogy) in the context of prescriptions for self-knowledge. Therefore, since the establishment of the self is necessarily at the time of object-cognition, the self is established precisely through [its status as] knower in the cognitions of objects, according to the method described above.
(Thus, the master's view that the self manifests only at the times of object-cognition has been justified.)

children.text: idamapyātmatattvāparijñānollasitaparimitamativikalpajalpitamiti na rocayante trayyantavidaḥ / viṣayavittirhi viṣayavittireva / na hi tayā ātmavittiḥ svarūpaṃ vā seddhumarhati, atadviṣayatvāt / yo hi yatsaṃvidviṣayo na bhavati, nāsau tayā sidhyati rūpasaṃvidevarasaḥ / aviṣayau ca viṣayavitterbuddhiboddhārāviti tāvapi na tayā sidhyataḥ /
children.translated_text: This too, they say, is the prattle of limited intellects manifesting from ignorance of the true nature of the self — [so] the followers of <s>Vedānta</s> do not approve [of it]. For object-cognition is merely object-cognition; it does not deserve to establish either self-cognition or the [self's] own nature, since they are not its objects. For that which is not the object of a particular cognition is not established by it, just as taste [is not established] by visual cognition. And the intellect and the knower are both non-objects of object-cognition, hence they too are not established by it.
